title: Scrollbar column of a Finder disk window is inDrag: clicking arrows/track drags the whole window; scrollbars are chrome-only, no scroll state
description:
AUDIT F02 (docs/audits/2026-10-03-flair-gui-codex/REPORT.md, section F02). Reviewer steps: in the root create 18 folders (File>New Folder + Ctrl-N, 22 entries total); click vertical down arrow (367,251) x3, up arrow (367,89), press Page Down; drag the track from (367,160) to (367,240).
SEEN: lower rows clipped; arrows and Page Down changed nothing; arrow clicks logged zero-distance FLAIR-DRAG; track drag moved the root window (20,60)->(20,140) (serial FLAIR-DRAG win 0 (20,60)->(20,140)). No thumb or position indication.
EXPECTED: arrows step, track pages, thumb drags, window never moves. Screenshots: docs/audits/2026-10-03-flair-gui-codex/shots/50-overflow-folder.png, 51-scroll-down.png, 53-page-down.png, 55-scrollbar-drags-window.png.
ROOT CAUSE (triage, read from source): the scrollbar column lies in strucRgn but outside contRgn (CalcDocContentRect, os/flair/window.c:176-190 subtracts FLAIR_CHROME_SCROLLBAR_W), so FindWindow (window.c:956-1022) falls through to its last line 'any other chrome pixel is the drag region' and returns inDrag; kmain.c:4442 then runs flair_live_do_drag. There is NO scroll state and no ControlRecord for Finder windows: the bar is drawn by chrome.c:554-596/834-845 (thumb explicitly deferred, chrome.c:551), and finder_windows.h:183 states scrolling is DEFERRED; grid layout stacks overflow on the last row. Fix: (a) FindWindow/pump must route scrollbar hits to a control/scroll tracker, never inDrag; (b) Finder view needs a scroll offset applied in finder_win_paint, hit-test, drag clamp and grid origin. Shares work with initech-tdnl.4 (live scrollbars) - this bug is the P0 stop-the-bleeding slice: minimum acceptable interim is that a scrollbar click never moves the window and, until tdnl.4 lands, the bar draws as inactive/empty when nothing overflows. Files: os/flair/window.c (FindWindow part code), chrome.c, control.c, finder_windows.c/.h, finder_desktop.c (paint/hit offset), kmain.c pump arms ~4442. OVERLAPS 34dh area (finder_desktop.c hit/clamp, kmain flair_live_do_surface).

DONE MEANS: (1) a host oracle for the logic plus a named mutant proven RED (Rule 6); (2) an emulator gate driven by a locked injected input trace on the booted image, asserting the serial markers and a pixel probe; (3) a recorded clip via record-flair (build/clips/<script>.{gif,mp4}, repro-proven) that the operator eyeballs (CLAUDE.md Rule 14 - a window feature with no clip is not done); (4) test-flair-* tri-emulator legs stay green (QEMU + Bochs). Audit was on an image built from commit 0194733; replay harness drive.py lives in the audit working dir and is described in the REPORT replay convention.

title: Finder disk-window icons stay at old screen coordinates after window drag, zoom, grow, restore (view.bounds/icon x,y are absolute and never rebased)
description:
AUDIT F01 (docs/audits/2026-10-03-flair-gui-codex/REPORT.md, section F01). Reviewer steps: open INITECH then APPS (double-click volume at (600,64), APPS at (123,101)); launch TENANTFX.EXE and quit it; drag APPS title (219,90)->(409,190) (delta +190,+100); collapse with rightmost widget (578,190) and expand; zoom with (563,190), restore with zoom widget near (609,50). Later moved the larger root window (20,60)->(90,100).
SEEN: APPS blank after drag; collapse/expand did not repair; zoom made TENANTFX.EXE reappear at its OLD screen position (75,124); restore made it vanish again; moved root had icon rows clipped under title and outside new content rect. Closing and reopening the root re-enumerated and drew correctly. Serial: FLAIR-DRAG win 0 (40,80)->(230,180) and (20,60)->(90,100).
EXPECTED: contents stay attached to the content area through move, zoom, grow, collapse/restore. Screenshots: docs/audits/2026-10-03-flair-gui-codex/shots/13-apps-folder.png, 17-finder-drag.png, 19-expanded-apps.png, 20-zoomed-apps.png, 23-restored-apps.png, 64-moved-root.png, 65-root-location-persistence.png.
ROOT CAUSE (triage, read from source): finder_window_t.view.bounds and every icons[i].x/y are ABSOLUTE screen coords fixed at finder_win_open (os/flair/finder_windows.c:449-470, 366); nothing rebases them when flair_live_do_drag (os/milton/kmain.c:1688), flair_live_do_zoom (1888), flair_live_do_grow (1923) move/resize the WindowRecord. finder_win_paint (finder_windows.c:608-629) fills the NEW contRgn and paints icons at the OLD coords. Stale view.bounds also feeds finder_win_cleanup and the icon-drag clamp. Affects Finder disk windows only; ref_tenant windows re-read contRgn at paint (os/apps/ref_tenant.c:215). Fix must rebase (translate icons + reset bounds) on every geometry change, ideally lazily in one place (finder_shell_event updateEvt / a finder_win_sync_geometry called before paint, cleanup, hit-test); keep icon arrangement across resize; collapsed (empty contRgn) must not corrupt bounds. Files: os/flair/finder_windows.c/.h, possibly finder_desktop.c (translate helper), kmain.c call sites. OVERLAPS initech-34dh area (finder_windows.c, finder_desktop.c, kmain.c flair_live_do_surface).

DONE MEANS: (1) a host oracle for the logic plus a named mutant proven RED (Rule 6); (2) an emulator gate driven by a locked injected input trace on the booted image, asserting the serial markers and a pixel probe; (3) a recorded clip via record-flair (build/clips/<script>.{gif,mp4}, repro-proven) that the operator eyeballs (CLAUDE.md Rule 14 - a window feature with no clip is not done); (4) test-flair-* tri-emulator legs stay green (QEMU + Bochs). Root cause confirmed independently by the 34dh lane: finder_windows.c finder_desk_init(&w->view, ..., content) at open, painted unchanged; nothing re-bases on flair_live_do_drag.
close_reason: Fixed 8f7d8bc: Finder icon coordinates re-based in ONE place (finder_win_sync_geometry); every consumer goes through it (paint, hit-test, selection, rubber band, Clean Up, drag/drop, outline start, zoom-back). title: region_op: per-band xmerge scratch[RGN_ROW_X_MAX=256] too small — silent stack buffer overflow when na+nb > 256
description:
[FLAIR bug-hunt R3 2026-06-28, wf_a2a0042d, adversarially verified] subsystem=FLAIR/region (os/flair/atkinson/region.c).
EVIDENCE: region.c:425 `int16_t scratch[RGN_ROW_X_MAX]` (256) is passed to xmerge at region.c:451; xmerge writes `out[no++]=x` (region.c:391-395) with no bound on `no`. region_normalize caps each input row to 256 entries, so an XOR/merge of two maximally-dense rows yields no<=na+nb<=512, overrunning the 256-slot stack buffer. The scratch needs 2*RGN_ROW_X_MAX, not RGN_ROW_X_MAX.

EXPECTED: scratch sized for na+nb (>=512), or xmerge checks `if (no >= cap) fail-loud` before each write.

ACTUAL: xmerge writes entries 256..511 into the next stack frame when two normalized rows together exceed 256 inversion points; stack corruption.

REPRO: Two regions each a single scanline of 128+ disjoint spans (256 inversion points each); region_op(&out,&A,&B,RGN_OP_XOR) overruns scratch[256..511].
close_reason: Fixed in 1ff449f: xmerge output-bounded + fail-loud at RGN_ROW_X_MAX; over-cap merges fail loud instead of overrunning scratch. Oracle: over-cap fail-loud probe + ASAN NO_XMERGE_CAP mutant (RED). Locked spec unchanged; cap decision is initech-44ab.

title: COPY <file> <file> (same source and destination) truncates the file to zero bytes and reports '1 file(s) copied' — silent data loss
description:
[FLAIR bug-hunt R2 2026-06-28, wf_2f47b15b, adversarially verified] subsystem=MILTON/COMMAND.COM (os/milton/command.c builtin_copy).
EVIDENCE: command.c:2321-2350: dos_open(pair.first) read-only (:2321) then dos_creat(pair.second) create/truncate (:2326) with no src==dst check. When both name the same dir entry, dos_creat truncates to 0 before any read; the dos_read loop (:2334) hits EOF immediately; both handles close and it prints '1 file(s) copied' (:2350).

EXPECTED: Detect src==dst and print 'File cannot be copied onto itself' (real DOS 3.3), or kernel sharing semantics prevent truncating an open file.

ACTUAL: COPY FOO.TXT FOO.TXT zeroes FOO.TXT and reports success; original content permanently lost.

REPRO: Write A:\TEST.TXT, COPY TEST.TXT TEST.TXT -> success message, then TYPE TEST.TXT is empty.
close_reason: Fixed: cmd_same_file guard in builtin_copy refuses COPY onto itself (MSG-DOS-0020 + zero footer) before truncation. Oracle: host test_same_file + emu no-data-loss gate test-copy-selfcopy (multi-cluster file preserved); both mutants bite. Residual edge cases: initech-vj28.

title: Latent: one baked-program output 'build' is dropped deterministically (reproduces on KVM)
description: While building the test-datetime baked program (beads initech-yv9), found that exactly ONE field-build in a multi-field output sequence is dropped/garbled deterministically per build (the dropped field shifts with code layout: MIN, HOUR, DOW observed). NOT a TCG artifact -- it reproduces under -accel kvm (real hardware) AND -accel tcg,one-insn-per-tb=on. The INT 21h handlers return CORRECT values (host oracle test-int21 + the values that DO appear confirm this); the corruption is in the GUEST program's instruction/data stream during execution. Symptoms: a cat-string loop appends nothing (string's first byte reads as NUL) or a store writes to a shifted address, at a position-dependent code site. Hypothesis: a kernel/loader memory-layout interaction corrupts the running program's code/data page during INT 21h processing (the PSP/DTA/env or staging copy region near 0x20000-0x20300). Worked around in os/milton/datetime_program.asm by emitting every field TWICE (one clean copy always survives the single per-run drop). Repro: build the datetime image, boot with -rtc base=...,clock=vm; observe one DT-* field missing without the duplicate-emit. Needs root-cause: instrument the program's code/data page for writes during a multi-INT-21h-write run; check loader staging/PSP/DTA overlap with PROGRAM_IMAGE (0x20100).
notes: ROOT-CAUSED by orchestrator (was mis-hypothesized as guest-exec corruption). The LOADER corrupts the program: load_program (os/milton/loader.c ~L224-232) does loader_memcpy(PROGRAM_IMAGE=0x20100, image, image_len) to copy the whole .COM, THEN writes the 2-byte empty env block at ENV_BLOCK=0x20200 = PROGRAM_IMAGE + 0x100. So for ANY program > 256 bytes, the env-zero OVERWRITES the program's own bytes at file offset 0x100-0x101 -> deterministic 2-byte corruption (reads as NUL). Matches every symptom (position-dependent, reproduces on KVM, 'first byte NUL'). Small programs (<256B, e.g. GREET/type/dir) are unaffected (env-zero lands past them); the resident shell is unaffected (not loader-loaded). CRITICAL: blocks InitechBase + Turbo Initech (both >256B). FIX: relocate ENV_BLOCK out of the program-image arena (memory_map.h is LOCKED spec -- deliberate change per Rule 8 + this issue) and remove the datetime_program.asm emit-twice WORKAROUND so the gate honestly verifies the fix. Mutation-prove: a program with a string at offset 0x100 must round-trip clean.
close_reason: ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED (was masked by an emit-twice workaround). Cause: load_program wrote the 2-byte env block at ENV_BLOCK=0x20200=PROGRAM_IMAGE+0x100 after the image copy, zeroing 2 bytes of any .COM >256B. Fix: relocated ENV_BLOCK to 0x5F000 (dedicated region below the stack, outside the image arena; PROGRAM_IMAGE_MAX capped to ENV_BLOCK). Workaround removed; test-datetime now emits each field once and is green -- proving the fix. Verified full vector green under load.

title: Screendump QEMU keystones flake on fixed wall-clock timeout (non-deterministic gate)
description: test-tracer-boot, test-boot, test-fs (and rarely test-shell) grab a framebuffer at a fixed --timeout-ms (~6s) and assert painted pixels via ppm_text_check. Under back-to-back QEMU boots (e.g. inside 'make test'/'make test-emu') the guest often has not rendered the banner/desktop within the wall clock, so the screendump is blank (fg=0) and the gate goes RED -- a wall-clock race, not a logic failure (they pass when the box is idle, confirmed: 3/3 tracer-boot, 2/2 boot, 2/2 fs standalone; RED inside the aggregate). A non-deterministic gate is worse than none -- it trains us to ignore red and makes 'make test' (initech-4mc) unusable as the rock-solid signal. FIX: replace the fixed-wall-clock screendump with poll-until-rendered (screendump-on-marker, or retry/grow the deadline until a serial 'rendered' marker appears, or screenshot when the guest signals paint-complete over serial). Must stay deterministic (Rule 11) and not weaken what ppm_text_check asserts (Law 2).
acceptance_criteria: 'make test' (host+emu, all 44 gates) passes deterministically 5x in a row on a loaded box; the screendump is captured only after the guest has actually painted (marker-driven, not fixed wall clock); ppm_text_check assertions unchanged; no sleeps that just paper over the race.
close_reason: Fixed: added --screendump-after MARKER; screendump now waits for the guest paint-complete serial marker (BANNER/DIR-OK) before grabbing, with the wall-clock as backstop and honest-RED fall-through. Verified: make test GREEN 2x under 6-core load (previously RED), negative control (NEVERPAINT) terminates at backstop and fails honestly, no hang.

title: Stop interrupted TYPE and DIR before consuming invalid syscall results
description: Root cause: os/milton/int21.c:5392 invokes INT 23h and returns before servicing the interrupted call; int21.c:5337 only sets the resident recovery latch. os/milton/command.c:2797 treats the unchanged AH=3Fh request register as a read count, and :2809 writes that count from a 128-byte stack buffer without testing the latch or bounding got. Thus an interrupted read can turn EAX=0x3F00 into 16128 output bytes. command.c:2741 ignores the same latch after the DIR /P key wait and :2766 continues enumeration. Ground truth: MS-DOS 3.3 User's Guide, Reference printed p.159 / PDF244 (evidence/manual-page-244.txt); ADR-0003 DEC-16 Fork A; PRD 6.1. Cancellation must not manufacture file bytes. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend harness/diff/fat_diff/test_dos_break.c and the INT21 host seam with Ctrl-C at read, write and DIR pause boundaries. Verify CLOSE and all stdin/stdout restoration paths. Replay controlshort and gaps2 on copied disks under QEMU, require an immediate usable prompt, no later HUGE/F299 lines and zero non-file bytes; also redirect TYPE and compare the committed prefix independently. Add a mutant that omits the interrupted check or permits got > sizeof(chunk); it must fail the byte-boundary and cancellation checks. Scope: Keep child-program INT 23h termination intact. This is a returning resident-call completion bug, not another request to add BREAK ON checkpoints (initech-bsy.4). Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/resume-controlshort-ctrlc.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/resume-gaps2-dir-break.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-control-verification.json; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-controlshort-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-gaps2-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-fixtures/HUGE.TXT; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume_driver.py. (Audit docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/REPORT.md L031,L043; triage docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/TRIAGE.md)
close_reason: Merged (lane cx-typeint c7d82ed7): TYPE and DIR /P check the Ctrl-C latch after every READ/WRITE, bound reads to the 128-byte buffer, close the handle and skip framing on abort, never consume an invalid syscall result (audit dos L031/L043); test-dos-resident-break-emu + mutants; gates green on main; flagship headroom 14412 B.

title: Keep GUI command keys out of the DOS Control-Break input path
description: B01. Root cause: os/milton/kbd.c:351 queues each key in the DOS cooked ring before :364 also posts it to FLAIR; :254 translates Ctrl-C to 03h. os/milton/int21.c:5389 polls that stale byte for BREAK ON and :5392 invokes INT23, whose default terminates at :5341. The desktop itself polls DOS time at os/milton/kmain.c:7412. This is shared input ownership, not a failing Scrap put. Ground truth: CLAUDE.md Rule 2 does not authorize killing a GUI session for Copy; the local Macintosh System Software Users Guide V6.0, printed pp.125 and 152, describes accessory/document clipboard work. spec/toolbox_gate.h Sec 12 defines the Scrap seam; ADR-0003 Amendment DEC-16 governs the DOS break checkpoints. Scope: Give the active GUI and DOS console explicit input ownership across entry, exit and SAMIR suspension. Consume GUI chords once; preserve authentic DOS Ctrl-C and extended-key/typeahead behavior when DOS owns input. Do not fix this by globally disabling BREAK or removing INT23. Acceptance oracle: Extend keyboard/ring and INT21 host ownership tests, then lock copybreak in QEMU and a Bochs leg: Copy, idle through a clock poll, Paste, drag, close and relaunch must work with no INT23-BREAK/INT21-EXIT. A restored dual-ring leak mutant must terminate/fail this oracle; DOS prompt and child Ctrl-C controls must still pass. Record a record-flair clip. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-das/shots/262-copybreak-before.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-das/shots/263-copybreak-after-copy.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-das/shots/265-copybreak-unresponsive.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-das/evidence/copybreak-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-das/evidence/scraplimit-serial.log (Audit docs/audits/2026-10-23-das/REPORT.md L002; triage docs/audits/2026-10-23-das/TRIAGE.md)
notes: Kernel fix merged 04bde64c; QEMU family green on main (copybreak + leak mutant, samir-suspend, exit-to-dos, kbd/event units). test-flair-copybreak-bochs RED on main: 'Scrapbook did not relaunch' (passes QEMU, fails Bochs = emulator-ism detector or RFB replay; CLAUDE.md stop condition: investigate, never pin to QEMU). Lane copybreakbochs (Opus, can run Bochs) root-causing.
close_reason: Merged: kernel fix 04bde64c (GUI command keys stay out of the DOS Control-Break path: cooked ring suppressed while FLAIR owns input, modifiers kept, lookahead cleared on handoffs, post-launch scancodes replayed in order; test-flair-copybreak + KBD_MUT_DUAL_RING etc.; clip copybreak repro-proven) and the Bochs replay fix (lane copybreakbochs 7cc34657: Bochs 2.7 sync=none fast-forwarded the idle guest past the budget, the debugger prompt disabled mouse capture, keyboard.cc halves PS/2 deltas; replay now sync=realtime with header-bar capture and 2x axis; trace_late fails loud); test-flair-copybreak-bochs, bochs-trace, samir-boot-bochs, boot-bochs green on main. title: Initech SideKick: the Borland SideKick (1984-ish, v1.5x) Initech-version -- a DOS TSR desk-accessory set (notepad, calculator, calendar/appointments, ASCII table, phone dialer) popped by a hotkey over any InitechDOS program
description: Operator directive 2026-10-17: 'implement a version of borland sidekick. call it initech sidekick.' Period reference: Borland SideKick for the IBM PC (1984; the 1.5x releases ship on DOS 3.3 era machines) -- the first mass-market TSR: SIDEKICK (SK.COM) stays resident, Ctrl-Alt (or a configured hotkey) pops its menu bar over the running program, with the Notepad (WordStar-style keys, up to a 4000-byte file), Calculator (decimal/hex/binary, paper-tape), Calendar + Appointment book, ASCII table, Phone dialer/directory, and the main menu (F1..F8). This is the InitechDOS side of the house (MILTON, not FLAIR): it exercises the DOS TSR mechanics the kernel must grow -- INT 21h AH=31h Keep Process (TSR) with a resident size, INT 09h/16h keyboard hook for the hotkey, INT 28h idle and the InDOS flag for safe pop-up, INT 10h/direct text-mode screen save/restore (the 4000-byte 80x25 save-under), INT 8/1Ch tick for the clock; all on the DEC-08 flat .COM model (no v8086; the resident part is a flat-32 image kept by AH=31h, PRD Sec 6 / ADR-0003 Appendix A). Deliverables (each a sub-bead, RED first, Law 1 ground truth before code): (1) RESEARCH: docs/research/SIDEKICK-period-grounding.md -- the SideKick 1.5x manual/screens (acquire a period source locally: the manual scans or the SideKick reference card; the screen layouts of the menu bar, Notepad, Calculator with its paper tape, Calendar, ASCII table, Dialer; the keystrokes; the exact pop-up chord; the resident-size figure), with provenance; (2) KERNEL: TSR support in MILTON -- AH=31h keep with resident paragraph count, the InDOS flag + INT 28h idle hook, a keyboard-hook vector the resident can chain, screen save/restore primitives -- host oracle + emu gate + mutants; headroom budget respected; (3) SK.COM: the resident + pop-up with the six accessories mirroring the originals' screens (text mode, period box-drawing, the SideKick colour scheme as period-correct on CGA/mono/VGA), config file SK.CFG, the Notepad saving to a real file through INT 21h; (4) ORACLES: a host core suite for each accessory (calculator arithmetic vs an independent golden -- bc/the real SideKick under dosbox-x if a period binary can be sourced for differential, the Law-2 way; calendar maths vs cal(1); ASCII table vs the IBM code page 437 table), an emu gate that boots to DOS, runs a foreground program, pops SideKick by the hotkey, uses the Notepad and saves, pops down, and proves the foreground screen is byte-restored (screendump before == after) + mutants (hotkey ignored, screen not restored, TSR not kept); (5) MANUAL: the Initech SideKick Owner's Handbook under pubs/ mirroring the Borland manual's structure, gated like the other books (commands/keys inventory from the shipped binary, screens replayed), with the house slips; (6) FLAIR: no GUI work -- but SideKick must also pop over FLAIR's Exit-to-DOS shell and over TPSREP; (7) clips per Rule 14 for the pop-up over DOS. Sub-beads to be filed by the research lane after (1). Depends on nothing merged-pending; conflicts textually with the DPB and Finder lanes in kmain.c -- schedule after they merge.

title: I123 /Copy and /Move disagree with real 1-2-3 R2.2 on 5 of 8 minted pairs: ERR corners, 8-bit /Move column delta, wrap past column A / row 1, loaded 0xFFFF refs
description: Found 2026-10-16 by the cjot lane (merge 21cde96; goldens lotus123-decomp 51025ee: mint/COPY01.steps, MOVE01.steps, WRAP01.steps -> goldens/minted/COPY01A-D, MOVE01A-D, WRAP01A-C; ledger re/mint-results-002.md). test-i123-copy-move --corpus grades the artifact's i123_transfer against the real before/after .WK1 pairs through the independent readers (wk1_ref.py, wk1_formula_ref.py --bytes) and is RED on MOVE01B, MOVE01C, MOVE01D, WRAP01B, WRAP01C; green on COPY01B/C/D (relative, $A$1, $A1, A$1, ranges: /Copy never rewrites reference bytes). The manual-derived model (test-i123-copy-move-model) encodes the WRONG rules in four places; real R2.2 is the reference (Law 1), the model must follow it. Disagreements, with golden bytes: (1) /Move over a referenced cell: real keeps a VAR or RANGE corner with col and row words 0xFFFF (MOVE01B E1 = 01 ffff ffff 05 0100 09 03, shown +ERR+1 / +ERR / @SUM(ERR)); the artifact emits token 32 @ERR (06 00 20 05 01 00 09 03). (2) Relative column rewritten by /Move: real stores 0x8000|(delta&0xFF), e.g. fb80 for -5 (MOVE01C F5, MOVE01D, moved corner of G3); the artifact stores the 14-bit form fbbf. (3) /Copy past column A (WRAP01B, shown +IV1+1): real keeps ffbf; the artifact writes ff80. (4) /Copy past row 1 (WRAP01C, shown +A8192+1, value 1): real wraps the row and keeps ffbf ffbf; the artifact and the model turn it into @ERR (cached inf) -- the model's 'row < 0 is ERR' rule is wrong. title: L001: Make refused APPEND preserve a reopenable DBF
description: AUDIT L001 (docs/audits/2026-10-05-astra-full-drive/REPORT.md). SEEN: L001: The first nine appends worked. Later appends failed. RECCOUNT() still reported 12. After closing, USE could not reopen the table. Independent extraction found a 502-byte DBF with header count 21, header length 129 and record length 31: only 12 complete records exist, whereas the header requires 781 bytes including EOF. The original three rows remain in the bytes but the table is unusable through SAMIR. EXPECTED: A refused append leaves all prior records and the committed count consistent; close/reopen succeeds. In-memory table and work-area counts must describe committed records. ROOT CAUSE (triage): os/samir/fs/dbf.c:1517 increments tbl->nrec before persistence. os/samir/cmd/mutate.c:754 appends, then :760 flushes; :761 returns on failure without undoing the count. os/samir/fs/dbf.c:1319 serializes the new count and :1324 writes the header BEFORE :1361 writes the larger record region. A short or failed body write leaves the new header over the old short file; later attempts keep incrementing it. The work-area count is refreshed only after success at mutate.c:765, explaining RECCOUNT() staying 12 while the disk header reached 21. DONE MEANS: Add an append commit path that preserves the existing header geometry, reserves needed growth before publishing it, writes the new record/tail before the committed count, and restores in-memory nrec/cursor on refusal. A staged replacement is another option only if its failed allocation leaves the original untouched. Merely moving the header write in the whole-file rewrite is insufficient if an earlier write can damage old records or normalize +2 geometry. Stop subsequent mutations from flushing an uncommitted count. Keep the diagnostic repair in B02 separate. Extend harness/diff/dbf_diff/test_dbf_mutate.c and test_use_rw.c with an independent fault/short-write PAL at every append boundary, including +1/+2 headers and zero free clusters. Reopen with an independent DBF reader and real III+; compare prior record bytes and count. Replay db-full.json on a copied FAT disk, extract CLIENTS.DBF with mtools, check structural length and fsck, and reopen in SAMIR. These tests are proposed, not run. Grounding: ../dbase3-decomp/specs/file-formats/dbf.md sections 1, 2 and 9 define nrec, record offsets and the minimum file length. PRD 6.6 requires real DBF I/O and independent round-trip grading. Preserving the old table on refusal is a data-integrity requirement, not a claim that III+ has modern transactions. See TRIAGE.md; source pinned to 50e084e.

Steps: Run ECHO HELLO | TYPE CON; send explicit Ctrl down, Z down/up, Ctrl up, Enter; repeat with Ctrl-C, with BREAK on. SEEN: z/c are ordinary bytes and COMMAND never returns. EXPECTED: DOS text-console EOF for Ctrl-Z and an active-command abort for Ctrl-C with a returned shell prompt. ROOT CAUSE (triage): os/milton/kbd.c:119 and :152 have no Ctrl state or control-byte translation; os/milton/kbd.h:72 tracks only Shift/Caps. OPEN CON uses the device branch at os/milton/int21.c:2871, whose raw adapter :1869 returns one byte without EOF/Ctrl-C handling, bypassing the existing cooked checkpoint :1217. DONE MEANS: left/right Ctrl and extended scancodes decode correctly; explicit-CON and stdin-CON handle paths honor independently captured DOS 3.3 control semantics; abort restores handles/redirection without killing the shell. Extend test-kbd-unit and CON/device host tests, then PS/2 emulator recovery gates asserting prompt return; retain AH=07h/no-check contracts. Batch B04. Citations pinned to 1c12493; full analysis and oracle limits are in TRIAGE.md.

title: Foreground tenant stays FINDER after its last disk window closes while NOTES window is active: band-2 menu hit-testing and active window disagree
description:
AUDIT F06 (docs/audits/2026-10-03-flair-gui-codex/REPORT.md, section F06). Steps: close root and APPS with Ctrl-W (FINDER-CLOSE-WINDOW win=0, win=1), observe Notes window, press and hold (196,28) in the lower bar. Serial FLAIR-MENU-DROP menu=515.
SEEN: NOTES window has active chrome; the lower bar reads the Finder bar; a press at (196,28) drops Finder Special (Clean Up, Restart, Shut Down) over an apparently Notes-active desktop. Screenshots: docs/audits/2026-10-03-flair-gui-codex/shots/66-moved-volume-icon.png, 68-hidden-special-menu.png.
NOTE - REPORT CORRECTION: the report says the lower bar read 'File Edit Notes' and (196,28) was a blank area. Screenshot 66 shows the bar is the FINDER bar 'File Edit View Special Help' and 196 lies ON its Special title. So the real defect is not an invisible hit zone; it is that the Finder bar stays up while a NOTES window is the active (hilited, front) window.
ROOT CAUSE (triage): by explicit design, no demotion when the last disk window closes (os/milton/kmain.c:3400-3402, flair_live_finder_foreground only ever PROMOTES). flair_live_do_finder_close and the FCMD_CLOSE_WINDOW arm (kmain.c:3282-3296, 3346-3354) call only finder_desk_repaint; process list head stays g_ten_finder, no FlairProcess_activate of the tenant owning the newly frontmost window, no DrawMenuBar. Band 2 hit-test resolves through flair_live_tenant_bar -> list->head->menubar (kmain.c:4478-4490), so it keeps answering as Finder. window.c DisposeWindow re-hilites NOTES (window.c:416-423) independently of the process list. Fix: after any Finder window close, activate the owner of the new frontmost visible window (reuse FlairProcess_activate + flair_live_finish_tenant_switch), or if no window remains keep Finder (period). Also ctrl-chords then route to NOTES correctly. Files: os/milton/kmain.c (finder close arms, flair_live_finder_foreground -> symmetric 'sync foreground to front window'), no change needed in finder_windows.c. Low overlap with 34dh (only kmain.c, different functions). Operator ruling 2026-10-03 on tdnl.12 (band 2 at rest = Photoshop bar; Finder bar when a disk window is front) is compatible.

DONE MEANS: (1) a host oracle for the logic plus a named mutant proven RED (Rule 6); (2) an emulator gate driven by a locked injected input trace on the booted image, asserting the serial markers and a pixel probe; (3) a recorded clip via record-flair (build/clips/<script>.{gif,mp4}, repro-proven) that the operator eyeballs (CLAUDE.md Rule 14 - a window feature with no clip is not done); (4) test-flair-* tri-emulator legs stay green (QEMU + Bochs). Audit was on an image built from commit 0194733; replay harness drive.py lives in the audit working dir and is described in the REPORT replay convention.

title: Makefile: SEVEN KERNEL_*_OBJ rules reference later-defined prereq vars (evaluate EMPTY at parse) -- region/heap/chrome/window/blitter/desktop/flair_shell .o not rebuilt on source edits (false-green incremental builds)
description: [Found during initech-jmc5] The rule for KERNEL_DESKTOP_OBJ (Makefile ~line 6976) lists prerequisites $(DESKTOP_C)/$(DESKTOP_H)/$(REGION_ENGINE_H), all defined LATER in the file (~10031/9050). GNU Make expands prerequisite lists immediately at parse time, so they evaluate EMPTY -> editing os/flair/desktop.c does NOT trigger a rebuild of build/desktop.o; make silently reports 'up to date' and the kernel links a STALE desktop.o. A real false-green hazard (kin to the clock-skew gotcha). Workaround used during jmc5: rm -f build/*desktop*.o before rebuilds. FIX: move the DESKTOP_C/DESKTOP_H/REGION_ENGINE_H definitions above the KERNEL_DESKTOP_OBJ rule (or use := late-bound correctly / literal paths). Audit other KERNEL_*_OBJ rules for the same late-var-reference pattern.
notes: SCOPE WIDENED by audit 2026-07-09 (was desktop.o only). Verified via make -rpn: build/region.o prereqs = 'spec/region_algebra.h | build' (MISSING region.c AND region.h -- the PRD-6.2 load-bearing math); build/heap.o has ZERO source prereqs; build/chrome.o missing chrome.c/chrome.h. Cause: GNU Make expands PREREQUISITE lists immediately at parse time; REGION_ENGINE_C etc. are defined ~2000 lines after use (Makefile ~7105-7145 vs ~9261+). The comment at Makefile:7100-7101 conflates deferred RECIPE expansion (true) with prereq expansion (false) -- delete it. Fix: move the var defs above first use, or use literal paths like the menu/control/dialog rules already do. Oracles unaffected (test_region compiles sources directly; test-kernel-repro force-rm's objects) -- this is a dev-loop/shipped-image integrity bug: editing region.c + incremental make relinks a STALE kernel.
close_reason: Fixed 8 object rules (the audited 7 + KERNEL_WINDOW_MUT_OVERLAY_OBJ found by full-file audit): late-defined prereq vars replaced with literal paths matching the menu/control/dialog idiom; misleading Makefile:7100 comment rewritten to distinguish recipe vs prereq expansion. Verified first-person: make -rpn shows full prereqs on all 8 objects; touch region.c/desktop.c triggers rebuild, second run up-to-date; test-region 37/37 green. flair-desktop-mutant-rules template checked -- NOT a bug (eval fires after defs, documented at :8976).

It does NOT resolve relative-vs-absolute or '..' forms for files in a subdir, because the shell exposes no AH=60h TRUENAME / file-path canonicalizer (only AH=47h GET-CWD + a CHDIR-scoped directory canon in fileio_fat.c fat_canon_from_cluster). title: region: RGN_ROW_X_MAX=256 contradicts its own spec comment (640px scanline => 640 inversion pts); wide regions fail-loud
description: [Follow-up to initech-mswo P0 fix] spec/region_algebra.h:279-282 defines RGN_ROW_X_MAX=256 with a comment that says '640px wide => at most 320 disjoint spans => 640 inversion points; this cap covers that with headroom' -- but 640 > 256, so the constant CONTRADICTS its own stated worst case. Consequences after the mswo P0 hotfix (xmerge fail-louds at the per-row cap): a legitimately busy full-width scanline (up to 320 spans / 640 inversion points) or the XOR of two max-density (256-pt) rows now FAIL-LOUD (panic) instead of corrupting -- correct per Rule 2, but it means such regions are unrepresentable. RGN_X_POOL_CAP is already 1024, so the pool has room. DECISION NEEDED (Rule 8 locked-spec change, deliberate act): raise RGN_ROW_X_MAX to its spec-intended value (>=640 to cover a 640px raster) and re-size scratch/tmp/normalize consistently, OR ratify 256 as the true cap and correct the misleading spec comment. May warrant a committee review since it ripples through the load-bearing ATKINSON engine (region_op scratch, region_normalize tmp, region_push_row). NOT to be done silently inside the P0 hotfix.
design: COMMITTEE DECISION 2026-07-10 (3 independent lenses: spec/ground-truth, engine/memory, oracle-impact -- UNANIMOUS): RAISE RGN_ROW_X_MAX to exactly 640 (not 1024). Key argument (lens A): 640 is the coordinate-DOMAIN bound from locked ADR-0004 OD-3 640x480; since both merge inputs draw toggles from the same positions and xmerge collapses coincident edges (region.c:398-401), a single band's merged output is domain-bounded -- at cap=640 the Sec-5 'cannot overflow' claim becomes TRUE, at 256 it is false and mswo-realizable. RIDERS (binding): (1) RGN_X_POOL_CAP 1024->2048 in the same deliberate act (1 dense row=640 + ~100 typical rows*4pts~=400 exceeds 1024 already; at cap 1024 one dense row could starve the pool). (2) Implementer derives the EXACT per-band scratch bound from the code (collapse-on-emit => ~domain-size; else 2*cap) and documents it + boundary test. (3) Kernel-stack audit: region_from_rects/complement stack triples at new sizes vs the single 64KiB stack (kstart.asm esp=0x9FFFC, shared with IRQ handlers); numbers documented -- hosted test-region green does NOT prove freestanding stack safety (lens C). (4) New deterministic oracle legs: full-width 320-span pixel-exact homomorphism round-trip + at-cap boundary case on a wide grid; small/deterministic, not fuzzed. (5) mswo ASAN mutant auto-scales (NSPANS=cap/2) -- re-verify it bites; fix stale literal comments. (6) Prose: Sec-5 two-bounds rewrite (pool bound vs per-row bound), region.c:364-373 'do NOT bump' note rewritten, ADR-0005:158 formally amended citing 44ab. (7) Worklog note records the Rule-8 deliberate change. Steelman for RATIFY-256 (all three lenses): no shipped UI object exceeds ~14 pts/row today; recorded and rejected -- the engine claims Z^2-per-scanline with no density restriction, an unreachable-today panic is a landmine (Law 4), and the fix costs ~1.5-8KB per-op stack against 64KiB.
acceptance_criteria: RGN_ROW_X_MAX and its spec comment agree; scratch/tmp/normalize/push_row consistently sized; a full-width 320-span scanline round-trips through region_op+normalize without fail-loud; test-region green + a new wide-region case; worklog note records the deliberate Rule-8 change.
notes: COMMITTEE ROUND 3 2026-07-11 (guard-bust escalation resolved; verification PASS conditional): kernel_shell measured 8340B OVER _kernel_end<PROGRAM_BASE with the static WS (pre-change runway ~10KiB; structural runway filed as its own bead). FINAL MECHANISM: dual-mode working-set storage, engine stays heap-agnostic. HOSTED: g_rgn_ws stays a static value array (tests unchanged). FREESTANDING: g_rgn_ws becomes bound pointers; kmain.c allocates the backing from the FLAIR heap via the flair_desktop_alloc_region idiom (FLAIR_CLASS_REGION, flair_desktop_oom on failure = boot-time fail-loud) and calls a freestanding-only region_engine_bind_ws(...) BEFORE region_engine_reset(); region_engine_reset keeps its universal guard-clear-only signature in both modes. BINDING TWEAKS: (W1) rgn_ws_acquire in freestanding must RGN_FAIL_LOUD on unbound/NULL pointers -- naive swap crashes silently pre-init; (W2) shrink slot 'one' to the 2-row/2-slot shape (region_complement pattern) -- saves ~6.1KiB BSS hosted + heap footprint, zero cost (acc/tmp must stay full-size, they accumulate); (W3) bind strictly before reset/first Toolbox call; update the region.c WS banner to describe pointer-binding; (W4) after landing re-run test-flair-desktop QEMU+Bochs (Rule 5) and confirm kernel_end margin restored (~10KiB). Single-mode alternatives checked and rejected: one-shrink alone insufficient (6124B < 8340B), hosted-only helpers save .text not .bss (they share slot 0 with acc), second ext-mem ld section violates the ADR-0004 DEC-03 single-owner arena. Query helpers already share slot 0 -- keep that.

Cap raised to the OD-3 domain bound (640) + pool to 2048; Sec-5 two-bounds rewrite; ADR-0005 amended; dual-mode working set (hosted static / freestanding FLAIR-heap-bound) after the guard-bust escalation; all committee riders (T1-T4, W1-W4) executed. Verified on main: test-region 65/65 + 4 mutants, kernel_shell links margin 8644B, QEMU+Bochs boots PASS. Acceptance criteria met: constants agree with derivation, full-width 320-span scanline round-trips pixel-exact, worklog note in WL-0071.

title: scan_string pool-wrap fires only when out==0 — valid strings falsely rejected 'too long' when the pool tail is small
description:
[FLAIR bug-hunt R3 2026-06-28, wf_a2a0042d, adversarially verified] subsystem=seed/lexer (seed/lexer.c).
EVIDENCE: lexer.c:268-278: `if (out>=avail){ if (lx->strpos!=0 && out==0){ wrap } else return make_error("string literal too long") }`. The wrap to pool-start only triggers when no bytes are yet stored (out==0). If >=1 byte is stored and the tail is exhausted, the error is returned despite free space at pool start.

EXPECTED: Strings up to LEXER_STRBUF_CAP always succeed regardless of pool cursor, by wrapping before/while scanning.

ACTUAL: A string starting at strpos in (0,CAP) whose length exceeds the remaining tail is rejected even though it fits from position 0.

REPRO: Drive strpos to 1020 (avail=4), lex 'hello' (5 chars): 5th char hits out(4)>=avail(4) with out!=0 → false 'too long'.
close_reason: Fixed + mutation-proven in WL-0068; make clean && make test ALL GREEN (296 host + 61 emu) on command-com-default

title: PACK does not update or rebuild open NDX indexes — silently corrupts them after record renumbering
description:

EVIDENCE: m_pack (mutate.c:884-905) calls dbf_pack (renumbers survivors), dbf_flush, wa_refresh, wa_nav_reset — no NDX call. ndx.h:636 states the S5.5 contract 'After DBF DELETE/PACK, call ndx_delete_key for each deleted recno.' EXPECTED: PACK rebuilds all open NDX files (REINDEX) after renumbering, or at minimum ndx_delete_key per deleted recno.

ACTUAL: NDX retains stale physical recnos; post-PACK SEEK/FIND return wrong records.

REPRO: 5-rec table, NDX on CODE; DELETE rec 2; PACK; SEEK of an old record's key returns wrong results.

title: ? / ?? renders logical XB_L as 'T'/'F' instead of '.T.'/'.F.' — oracle heresy masks the bug
description:

EVIDENCE: q_render_val case XB_L (query.c:409-411) `q_append(...,v->u.l?"T":"F",1u)`. ? (q_question, 840) routes through the same q_render_val, so ? logicals also print T/F. title: fn_round uses (int64_t) truncation-toward-zero instead of floor — wrong result for all negative non-integer inputs

For v=-2.7,dec=0: v+0.5=-2.2, (int64_t)(-2.2)=-2 → -2.0 (should be -3.0). dec_format (rt.c:247) correctly uses the static rt_floor64 (rt.c:207-213); fn_round skips it. REPRO: Evaluate ROUND(-2.7,0) → -2.0 (expected -3.0).

title: dos_read lacks a Carry-Flag check — read errors are returned as byte counts, emitting/writing garbage in TYPE, COPY and batch loading

On AH=3Fh error (CF=1, AX=error code) dos_read returns the error code as a byte count. builtin_type(:2108-2113) then dos_write(chunk,err) emits err uninitialized bytes; builtin_copy(:2334-2344) writes them to the destination; batch_load_file(:2991-2995) advances total by err.

ACTUAL: A read error (e.g. ACCESS_DENIED=5) makes TYPE print 5 stack bytes, COPY corrupt the destination, batch mis-size the script.

REPRO: Trigger an AH=3Fh error mid-TYPE/COPY -> garbage bytes in output/destination.

title: FLAIR live compositor ERASES the modal dialog + menu bars when a window is dragged across them (non-WindowMgr layers not damage-tracked)
description:
SYMPTOM (operator, make run-flair): corrupted redraws when windows are moved past each other.

ROOT CAUSE: the live drag repaint desktop_paint_damage (os/flair/desktop.c:171) composites ONLY the WindowMgr document windows + the desktop background. The live scene ALSO contains the modal FILE COPY dialog (os/flair/dialog.h:420, rect x[140,500] y[200,280], drawn ON TOP) and TWO stacked menu bars (os/flair/shell.h:99-101, y[0,40]) -- both painted ONCE by shell_render and NOT participants in the WindowMgr damage/z-order model. When a document window is dragged across them, the vacated area falls through to wm->desktop_update and is filled with seafoam (desktop.c:197-200), ERASING the modal/bar; and a dragged window's visible region is not clipped against them (window.c fronts_union considers only WindowMgr windows), so it can OVERPAINT them.

EMPIRICAL (flair_live.img; drag W1 left 260px across W0 + modal): the modal right-half x[366,498] y[206,278] went from 85.5% white + 14.5% black (the dBoxProc dialog box + text) BEFORE to 100% teal AFTER -- the modal erased to desktop background. Window-over-window compositing is CLEAN and the cursor save-under is CLEAN; the defect is specifically the non-WindowMgr layers.

WHY IT ESCAPED: test-flair-drag's pixel oracle (tools/ppm_flair_drag_check.c) deliberately probes "right of window 0" and "above the modal", AVOIDING the modal/bar region; the region gate (test-interact) grades math, not composited pixels over these layers.

FIX OPTIONS: integrate the always-on-top layers (menu bars + modal) into the live compositor so they survive a damage repaint. Interim: after desktop_paint_damage, re-blit the bar + modal layers over the damaged region. Clean: make the bars + modal topmost participants in the z-order (windows clip against them via fronts_union; they repaint in the damage pass). Same incompleteness family as initech-z1f5 (live menu panel restore).

Oracle-first: depends on the independent modal/bar survival oracle.
design: RATIFIED (arch verify + red-team, 2026-07-07): a SINGLE ~15-LOC fold of a new wm->overlay_rgn into fronts_union (window.c:92-107) -- NOT the uniform-window model, NOT a re-composite wrapper. KEY INSIGHT: fronts_union feeds the WHOLE damage chain (visible_into->exposed->distribute_exposure->desktop_update), so once the overlay occludes, defect (b) overpaint AND defect (a) seafoam-erasure BOTH close for free -- overlay pixels are never written by desktop_paint_damage and survive from the initial shell_render. NO desktop.c change (sidesteps the jmc5 edit). The fix is inside the ONE shared occlusion primitive every paint path (drag/close/app-switch/full-render) routes through, so no path can bypass it (why the wrapper/per-site registration is rejected). ALIASING (Rule 3): use rgn_accumulate(out, overlay_rgn, UNION, sc2) with sc2 = (out==scratch_c)?scratch_b:scratch_c -- NEVER the naive region_op(out,out,overlay) self-alias (corrupts on overlap, the case under test). Modal-bbox is sufficient+exact (dBoxProc fills its whole bounds; bars are solid strips). Scene = flair_live (show_modal=1, kmain.c:965), the ONLY scene with the modal; NO init HideWindow there so desktop_update starts empty (pipa is pure occlusion, distinct from jmc5). LANES: 0 WindowMgr field+init-zero+WINDOW_MUTATE_IGNORE_OVERLAY (window.h/c); 1 the fold (window.c fronts_union); 2 scene wiring build overlay_rgn=union(bars{0,0,40,640}[+modal{140,200,500,280} iff show_modal]) in shell_build_scene + kmain alloc (REBASE on 4w15's shell.c/kmain.c edits); 3 dc4v EMU oracle tool + trace (RED-first); 4 mutation-proof via flair_live_mut_overlay.img (-DWINDOW_MUTATE_IGNORE_OVERLAY). Oracle blast radius ~zero: fold is a no-op when overlay_rgn==NULL (all host harnesses), so test-window/interact/drag/shell stay green; only WINDOW_MUTATE_IGNORE_OVERLAY needs EMU mutation-proof. dc4v probes (canon-graded, flair_live drag W1 left ~260px): modal (496,240)==idx0 + (450,240)==idx1 + area x[366,498]y[206,278] >=80pct white/black <=5pct teal; bar y=30 x[70,350] idx3-gray high; anchor (20,460)==idx2.
acceptance_criteria: Dragging any document window across the modal and the menu bars leaves them intact (no teal hole, no overpaint), verified by an independent pixel oracle the fix turns RED->GREEN; window-over-window compositing stays clean; reproducible build green.
close_reason: Fix shipped in WL-0067 (commit 6c2c672, wm->overlay_rgn fold into fronts_union, os/flair/window.c); dep dc4v closed; WL-0067 lists pipa among closed beads. Tracker was the stale side (audit 2026-07-09).

title: FLAIR mouse: INDEPENDENT physical-direction oracle (PS/2 up -> cursor v DECREASES) + EVENT_MUTATE_FLIP_SIGN mutant
description:
The mouse-Y inversion (sibling bug) escaped every gate because all mouse-Y oracles grade the cursor by RECOMPUTING expected where.v from the SAME "cursor_v += dy" rule the artifact uses (harness/proptest/test_event.c manufactures dy=+5 and asserts v=240+5), and the only mouse mutant EVENT_MUTATE_STALE_WHERE drops the update (magnitude) but never tests SIGN. This is the HER-02 by-construction heresy on the sign axis (ADR-0010, Law 2).

Build an INDEPENDENT oracle that encodes the GROUND-TRUTH polarity from the hardware contract (a real PS/2 mouse-up packet: byte0 Y-sign bit + byte2 magnitude, +Y = physical up) and asserts that after the producer cooks it into the ring, the screen cursor v DECREASES (moves up). This oracle is the RED half of the producer fix and must exist FIRST (Red->Green, CLAUDE.md Rule 1/6).

title: FLAIR live cursor: vertical mouse axis INVERTED -- producer packs RAW PS/2 dy, violating the locked ring-payload Y contract
description:
SYMPTOM (operator, make run-flair): the mouse moves inverted in the VERTICAL axis -- physical-up moves the cursor/window DOWN; horizontal is correct.

ROOT CAUSE: a producer-side sign error that VIOLATES the locked ring-payload contract. spec/event_model.h:333-335 defines FLAIR_RAW_MOUSE payload bits 16..23 as "signed delta Y ... Y axis inverted from PS/2 convention to screen-down-positive" -- the PS/2->screen flip MUST happen BEFORE the value enters the ring. But the producer flair_live_mouse_post (os/milton/kmain.c:1024-1026) packs the RAW PS/2 dy (mouse.c:222 "+dy = up") with NO inversion. Downstream cook_raw (os/flair/event.c:441) correctly ADDS what the contract guarantees is an already-flipped screen-down delta (g_cursor_v += dy), so physical-up raises g_cursor_v and the cursor descends. cook_raw and test_event.c are CORRECT per spec; the bug is solely the producer. The misleading comment is mouse.c:225-227 ("the pump cooks the Y flip"), contradicting the locked spec.

EMPIRICAL (flair_live.img, QMP rel-mouse): rel-y +40 -> window top 120->80 (UP); rel-y -40 -> 120->160 (DOWN) => physical-up -> window-down. Reproduced.

WHY IT ESCAPED: the producer is __attribute__((unused)) on host (no host oracle) and runs only in the bare-metal live build; the EMU drag/mouse gate goldens BAKED IN the inverted behavior (Makefile:11199 "rel +y -> cursor up"; test-flair-mouse where.v calibrated to the inverted cook). No oracle establishes an INDEPENDENT physical-direction ground truth (HER-02 / ADR-0010 by-construction pattern, on the sign axis).

FIX: negate dy at the producer (kmain.c:1026) BEFORE narrowing into bits 16..23, in int width -- CRITICAL: -(int8)-128 = +128 is not int8-representable; negate in int, or saturate -128->+127. Update the stale ISR comment mouse.c:225-227. Leave cook_raw (event.c:441) and test_event.c UNCHANGED. Then RE-BASELINE the EMU gate goldens that encoded the inversion (test-flair-drag Makefile ~11193-11224 trace+expected window pos; test-flair-mouse Makefile:8396/8423 expected where.v) to the physical-correct direction -- do NOT revert the fix to keep them green.

Oracle-first: depends on the independent physical-direction oracle.
acceptance_criteria: make run-flair: physical-up moves the cursor/window UP. The independent direction oracle is RED before the producer fix and GREEN after. EMU drag/mouse gates re-baselined to physical-correct direction. test_event.c unchanged (correct per spec). Reproducible build green; ASCII-clean.
close_reason: Producer fixed (mouse_pack.h negate per the locked Sec-5 contract); every bug-calibrated trace/golden rebaselined to physical truth (mouse expectation, drag/dc4v/menu/crossdrag specs, locked appswitch trace w/ in-file Rule-8 note); all live-input emu gates + mutants re-verified green on main. Landed 5dd5525 together with the 8f5p oracle (now closed).

title: ADR-0004 amendment: lock in mechanism/policy(decoration) split + ATKINSON as the dual-heritage (QuickDraw Rgn + GDI HRGN) shared spine
description: RATIFIED OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-06-21 (no relitigation; operator authority, NOT committee -- do not convene one). Lock in the two design choices stolen from the X Window System factoring. (1) MECHANISM/POLICY SPLIT: the imaging/window MECHANISM (surface/GrafPort draw verbs, ATKINSON region clip, Window/Event geometry: strucRgn/contRgn/updateRgn/drag/z-order/DiffRgn) is kept SEPARATE from POLICY/DECORATION (chrome look, control look, dialog look, COLORS, patterns, metrics). Mechanism is policy-free and takes color/pattern/metric as PARAMETERS; decoration is a layer on top. (2) ATKINSON = THE SHARED SPINE: os/flair/atkinson (scanline inversion-list set algebra) is the SAME machinery behind BOTH QuickDraw Rgn AND GDI HRGN; BOTH heritages (System-7 chrome + Win-3.1/Photoshop chrome -- both present in the Office Space frame) clip through the ONE engine; NEITHER heritage owns it. GAP ANALYSIS: ADR-0004 D-1 (5-layer stack) + D-2 (one surface module/GrafPort) already give the LAYERING; ADR-0005 already gives a clean-room, heritage-neutral region engine. But (a) ADR-0004 does NOT make mechanism-vs-decoration a first-class invariant -- the Managers (layer 3) currently fold geometry-mechanism AND appearance-policy together, and color is smeared across chrome.c/control.c/dialog.c (the 5 duplicated index->RGB switches -- the exact tangle that let the preview.webp palette leak in unnoticed, WL-0053); (b) ADR-0005 frames the engine as System-7/QuickDraw-only (Rect field order, UnionRgn/SectRgn names) and never acknowledges it as the GDI-HRGN spine too. ACTIONS: write an operator-ratified AMENDMENT to ADR-0004 (no committee) making both binding invariants; cross-ref a companion note on ADR-0005 (the engine is the dual-heritage Rgn+HRGN spine). The amendment's current-state/migration/forward-obligation sections must be grounded in the verified FLAIR structure from the running grading audit (Law 1). IMPLICATIONS for the verb track: re30.4 (one palette module, kill the 5 switches) is the FIRST mechanism/policy cut -- extract color into a POLICY module the mechanism reads as params, not a dedup'd lookup baked into decoration; re30.5 (GrafPort verbs) lands the imaging mechanism policy-free. title: In-kernel FAT16 mount: windowed/streaming FAT-sector read (g_fat[12*512] too small for a FAT16 FAT)
description: z01 landed the FAT16 DECODE layer (fat16_next_cluster + fat_type dispatch) + a host-side 3-way differential oracle (test-fat16) proving the decode over real FAT16 fixtures (incl. a 2.5MB volume whose chain crosses cluster 0xFF8). BUT the kernel cannot yet mount a real FAT16 volume: the whole-FAT in-memory buffer g_fat[12*512] (~6KB, sized for a 1.44MB FAT12 floppy) is far smaller than a FAT16 FAT (up to ~128KB). A real FAT16 mount currently fails loud (no corruption). To make FAT16 actually readable IN-KERNEL/IN-EMULATOR, replace the whole-FAT load with a windowed/streaming FAT-sector read (read only the FAT sector(s) needed for the current cluster's entry, like the streaming chain walk dao added for the data region). This is the remaining work for true FAT16 HDD read; it should be a dependency of the 40oq capstone (FAT16-green criterion).

title: FAT16 volume mounts OK but all decode/encode is 12-bit-only: silent garbage on FAT16 mount
description: fat12_mount returns FAT12_OK for a volume it classifies FAT_TYPE_FAT16 (fat12.c:132), but next_cluster/set_entry/walk_chain and the EOC/bad predicates are hard-wired 12-bit + FAT12 thresholds (header even warns FAT16 OUT OF SCOPE). fat_type is set but never checked by any op. A FAT16 mount + read mis-decodes every entry (16-bit treated as straddled 12-bit) -> garbage chains / corrupt data, no fail-loud. Audit: fat12 fat12-fat16-decode-mismatch.
acceptance_criteria: Either reject FAT16 at mount (FAT12_ERR_UNSUPPORTED when total_clusters>=FAT12_MAX_CLUSTERS) so 12-bit code never runs on 16-bit FAT, or assert vol->fat_type==FAT_TYPE_FAT12 at every decode/encode entry and fail loud; test mounts a FAT16 image and asserts the loud rejection (mutation-proven); make test green.
close_reason: fat12_mount rejects FAT16 (FAT12_ERR_UNSUPPORTED) since all decode/encode is 12-bit-only. RED->GREEN (synthetic FAT16 boot sector via in-test memory blockdev, total_sectors bumped past 4085), mutation-proven. make test 55h+19e GREEN.

title: FAT12 read path has no upper-cluster-bound: out-of-range cluster maps to in-image LBA, silent wrong data
description: fat12_next_cluster/walk_chain/read_file/read_partial only bounds-check the FAT BUFFER (off+1 < fat_len), never the cluster against the last valid data cluster. fat12_last_cluster() exists (fat12.c:973) but is write-path-only. An in-FAT link value above last-valid with (N*3/2+1)<fat_len is accepted and fed to BPB_CLUSTER_LBA. On 1.44MB geometry it happens to land >=2880 and is caught only by the file-backed blockdev EOF short-read -- a coincidence, not an invariant. With sectors_per_cluster>1 or FAT slack it maps to a VALID in-image LBA and silently returns the WRONG sector. Fuzzer (fat12_corrupt_fuzz.c:340-356) documents reliance on that coincidence. Audit: fat12 fat12-no-upper-cluster-bound + fat12-no-eoc-min-data-value-overlap-test.
acceptance_criteria: Explicit predicate cluster in [FAT12_FIRST_DATA_CLUSTER .. fat12_last_cluster(vol)] applied at every data-cluster consumer; returns FAT12_ERR_CLUSTER past last data cluster; fuzz/diff leg on a multi-sectors-per-cluster image pokes an in-FAT out-of-range link mapping to an in-image LBA and asserts fail-loud (RED today); make test green.
close_reason: Added fat12_cluster_in_range(vol,c) upper-bound predicate; hardened all 5 chain-walk sites (walk_chain + read_partial x2 + write_partial x3) so an out-of-range in-chain cluster is rejected (FAT12_ERR_CLUSTER) instead of mapped to a wrong/out-of-volume LBA. RED->GREEN (synthetic out-of-range link), write path hardened too (Rule 3). make test 55h+19e GREEN.

title: INT 21h AH=59h GET EXTENDED ERROR returns stale data after most failures
description: do_geterr (AH=59h) reports g_last_error, but int21_note_error() is called from only TWO sites (do_open :805, do_getcwd). Every other failing handler (do_write/read/close/lseek/dup/dup2/creat/unlink/exec/findfirst/findnext) sets CF+AX WITHOUT int21_note_error, so 59h returns the previous/zero error after the common 'call failed -> query 59h' idiom. Spec: DOS 3.3 PRM AH=59h keeps the most-recent INT 21h error. Test gap: test_int21_edge.c:542-579 hand-seeds the error via int21_note_error directly, never via a real failing dispatch -- which is why this is invisible. Audit: int21 geterr-not-populated-on-most-failures + geterr-test-gap.
acceptance_criteria: Centralize a set_error(f,code) helper (set_ax+cf_set+int21_note_error) used at every cf_set error return; dispatcher-driven oracle: fail OPEN/READ/WRITE through int21_dispatch then AH=59h asserts the just-returned code; mutation-proven; make test green.
close_reason: Single dispatch-choke capture in int21_dispatch: on CF=1, int21_note_error(AX). Covers every current+future failing handler; do_geterr (CF=0) never clobbers; success leaves last error intact. RED->GREEN, mutation-proven. make test 55 host + 19 emu GREEN.

title: INT 21h AH=40h WRITE rejects read/write-mode (AL=2) handles
description: do_write (os/milton/int21.c:653) gates FILE writes on e->open_mode != SFT_MODE_WRITE (==1). A handle opened AH=3Dh AL=2 (SFT_MODE_RDWR, sft.h:75) therefore returns ACCESS_DENIED on every WRITE, though read/write mode must permit writing. Breaks any program that opens a file mode-2 to update in place -- notably InitechBase .dbf record updates (the named consumer). do_read does NOT gate on mode (only kind), so read side is fine. Test gap: test_fileio.c only ever uses AL=0/AL=1 (never AL=2), so the bug is invisible to the oracle. VERIFIED against code 2026-06-13. Audit: fileio-sft rdwr-open-write-denied + rdwr-write-test-gap.
acceptance_criteria: do_write permits FILE write when open_mode==SFT_MODE_WRITE||SFT_MODE_RDWR; new test_fileio case: OPEN AL=2, WRITE at off 0, LSEEK 0, READ back == written; mutation-proven (revert gate -> RED); full make test green.
close_reason: do_write permits FILE write for SFT_MODE_WRITE||SFT_MODE_RDWR (int21.c). RED->GREEN, mutation-proven both directions (missing-RDWR + loosened-gate negative). make test: 55 host + 19 emu GREEN.

title: harness/emu/bochs.c driver + wire test-boot to dual-emulator differential
description: Build a C Bochs driver (generated bochsrc, headless display, serial capture, structured result) parallel to qemu.c; wire test-boot to assert QEMU==Bochs. Front D. Relates to initech-x0i / initech-bea.
notes: DE-RISKED + ready to build (6pj done). Working Bochs config (bd memory bochs-boot-solved-initech-6pj): romimage=/usr/share/bochs/BIOS-bochs-legacy + vgaromimage=/usr/share/bochs/VGABIOS-lgpl-latest + cpu:model=pentium + vga:extension=vbe + ata0-master cyl=2,heads=2,spt=32 + com1 mode=file. This Bochs 2.7 is a DEBUGGER build: drive headless with -rc containing 'c'. The RFB display plugin blocks ~30s for a client; the trivial RFB 3.3 unblock handshake (connect:5900, recv 12-byte version, send 'RFB 003.003\n', recv 4-byte sectype, send shared-flag 0x01, hold) must be implemented IN C in bochs.c (Law 3 -- harness is C-only; harness/emu/rfb_unblock.py is the reference, NOT shippable). bochs-term does NOT work headless (stalls on the graphics mode-set). GATE ASSERTS ON SERIAL, NOT a screendump: Bochs RFB cannot display VGA mode 0x13 (see bd memory bochs-rfb-display-does-not-render-vga-mode -- even a pristine real-mode fill shows black; OS render is correct, RFB display is the limitation). Expected Bochs serial: S1 JMP2 S2 VBE-ENOMODE VGA13 VBE FONT KLOAD A20 GDT PM LFB OK KERNEL BI-OK ... CONSOLE BANNER-BEGIN/InitechDOS Version 3.30/BANNER-END BANNER ... no triple-fault (grep Bochs log for '3rd (13)' / 'IDT.limit = 0x0' = 0). Model bochs.c on qemu.c (866 lines): generate bochsrc, spawn bochs, run the C RFB-unblock thread, capture the serial file, scan markers, detect triple-fault via the log. Then wire test-boot to a QEMU==Bochs serial differential. OPEN Q for the visual leg: mode 0x12 (640x480x16 planar) MIGHT render on RFB (untested) -- would need a planar console renderer; defer.
close_reason: C Bochs oracle (harness/emu/bochs.{c,h} + bochs_main.c) + test-boot-bochs gate landed (commit 4a0c38c). RFB unblock implemented in C (Law 3); generates the legacy-BIOS bochsrc, drives the debugger build headless, captures serial, scans for triple-fault. Gate boots the tracer under Bochs and asserts the mode-0x13 fallback (VBE-ENOMODE+VGA13) + the SAME kernel markers as QEMU (the differential) + no triple-fault; mutation-proven (latest BIOS->triple_fault=1->RED; bogus marker->RED). SERIAL-only by necessity (Bochs RFB can't display mode 0x13, bd memory). Not in default make test (env-specific + ~45s); run via 'make test-boot-bochs'. Full suite 55 host + 19 emu still GREEN. Optional follow-ups: a combined test-boot-tri target; promote into make test once stable; a visual leg would need mode 0x12 + planar renderer.

title: stage2 VBE mode-set fix for Bochs (ERR-VBE)
description: stage2.asm VBE 640x480 LFB mode-set fails on the Bochs VGA BIOS, blocking Bochs gating. Diagnose + add a fallback/compat path. Prereq for dual-emulator. Front D. Relates to initech-x0i.
design: SOLVED + path chosen. Bochs has no usable VBE LFB (legacy BIOS: VBE-ENOMODE; latest BIOS: VBE-E00 and won't POST -- CMOV/IDT.limit=0). Standard VGA mode 0x13 (320x200x256 linear @0xA0000) is CONFIRMED working on Bochs legacy-BIOS+pentium (framebuffer live, readback verified). Plan (4 commits): (1) console.c 8bpp linear renderer + host oracle; (2) stage2 vbe_setup falls back to INT10h mode 0x13 on VBE failure, boot_info gains lfb_width/height vars + bpp=8; (3) kmain DAC palette (port 0x3C8/9) + 8bpp seafoam fill; (4) Bochs boot gate (legacy BIOS+pentium+rfb_unblock) asserting serial markers -- feeds initech-564. QEMU path unchanged (VBE succeeds there).
notes: Native-BIOS attempt (bochsbios + bochs-term installed): BIOS-bochs-latest does NOT fix it -- the guest faults EARLY (interrupt with IDT.limit=0x0 at t~363k), never reaching stage2 (no S1). So neither path boots clean on Bochs: SeaBIOS reaches stage2 but VBE-E00 (no VBE), native BIOS crashes pre-stage2 (likely the i440FX/ACPI/USB env or the tiny 2/2/32 geometry vs what the native BIOS expects). CONCLUSION: Bochs boot is a dedicated multi-step effort (try: standard disk geometry for the native BIOS; or term-headless to remove RFB timing; or a stage2 non-LFB fallback for the SeaBIOS path), NOT a quick win. Headless mechanism (RFB-unblock client) proven. Deferring per effort; QEMU remains the binding boot gate.
close_reason: Standard-VGA mode-0x13 fallback implemented + verified (3 commits: console 8bpp renderer, stage2 VBE->mode-0x13 fallback, kmain 8bpp boot_info + DAC palette). Bochs (legacy BIOS + pentium) now boots end-to-end with ZERO faults; QEMU VBE path unchanged. Locked by committed green oracles: test-console (host, 8bpp section mutation-proven) + test-tracer-boot (QEMU). Full suite 55 host + 19 emu GREEN. The committed Bochs differential GATE is tracked in initech-564 (de-risked, ready to build). Diagnosis: no VBE LFB on Bochs (legacy: ENOMODE, latest: E00 + won't POST due to CMOV/IDT.limit); standard VGA mode 0x13 is the portable answer.

title: [epic] Kernel hardening: robustness, fuzzing, edge-cases, dual/tri-emulator
description: Make the InitechDOS kernel bulletproof before the Toolbox/apps/compiler are built on it. Driven by a grounded 5-facet audit (see worklog). Four fronts: (A) fix concrete latent robustness bugs; (B) expand edge-case test + fuzzing coverage; (C) close the INT 21h error-path gaps; (D) bring the gate from QEMU-only to dual (QEMU+Bochs) and best-effort tri (86Box headless). Baseline at start: 45 host + 19 QEMU gates GREEN on branch kernel-hardening. Every change is red->green with a mutation-proven oracle (Rule 6). Objective: rock solid, correct, robust, tested; fast feedback, no HITL.

title: Kernel has hit its 64 KiB window ceiling (_kernel_end 0x1fd20 vs PROGRAM_BASE 0x20000) -- blocks all further kernel growth
description: The kernel is linked at 0x10000 and PROGRAM_BASE=0x20000, giving a 64 KiB window. _kernel_end is now 0x1fd20 -- only ~480 bytes below the u0a guard limit (0x1ff00). The memory_map.h 'gap proof' comment still claims 32 KiB headroom but that is STALE: KERNEL_SECTORS grew to 96 and kernel .bss (cfg_fat_buf etc.) filled the window. ANY further kernel feature (509.8 INT 22/23/24 handlers next, but also 509.6/.7/.9 device chain/MCB/FCB) will trip the guard. Root cause: the kernel outgrew its window. Options: (A) raise PROGRAM_BASE (e.g. 0x20000 -> 0x30000) giving the kernel a larger window -- deliberate LOCKED-spec change (Rule 8), ripples into ~8 baked .asm 'org 0x00020100' constants + memory_map.h derived addrs + test_loader.c assertion; program image arena shrinks from ~252 KiB to still-ample ~190 KiB. (B) relocate large kernel scratch .bss buffers to free high conventional RAM (0x90000-0xA0000, below VGA) via fixed pointers, reclaiming .bss without touching PROGRAM_BASE or any program org. Either is a real fix; (A) is more mechanical, (B) avoids program-side ripple. Update the stale memory_map.h gap-proof comment as part of the fix. Re-run test-loader + the emu program gates (test-program/exec/type/dir/datetime/multiopen/exith/conin) which bake those org values.

title: FAT12 + file-I/O state-machine fuzzer (generative, shrinking, mtools differential)
description: We mandate mutation-proving (Rule 6) and FAT differential (Rule 5) and APPLY them universally, but we do NOT have generative/randomized fuzzing for the FAT12 + file-I/O layer that dBASE (M6) and Turbo Initech (M7/M8) now stand on. Current FAT oracles (test-fat, test-fat-partial, test-fat-write-partial, test-multiopen) are fixed enumerated matrices + mutants -- strong, but they don't explore the deep state space (Rule 3: all bugs are deep). The only property/fuzz mandates in CLAUDE.md are the region engine (initech-6dy, M3) and the xBase evaluator (initech-gmo, M6), both unbuilt; neither covers the file layer. BUILD a deterministic, seeded (Rule 11 -- no clock; seed is an input) generative fuzzer that drives randomized sequences of fat12_create / fat12_write_partial / fat12_read_partial / lseek / append / unlink / multi-open across many handles on a mounted image, and after each step DIFFERENTIALLY checks the volume against the python reference and/or mtools (re-mount + read-back), with SHRINKING of any failing sequence to a minimal reproducer. Run a bounded N-iteration sweep as a gate; on failure print the seed + shrunk op-sequence. Wire into the test vector (its own slower tier if needed). This is the standing hardening gate the file layer is missing. Mutation-prove the fuzzer itself bites (perturb a fat12 op, confirm the fuzzer finds it).
acceptance_criteria: A seeded generative fuzzer runs K randomized create/write/seek/read/append/unlink/multi-open sequences against a real FAT12 image, differentially verifying each state vs the python ref / mtools; a deliberately injected fat12 bug is CAUGHT and SHRUNK to a minimal reproducer (seed + op list printed); the gate is deterministic (same seed -> same run, Rule 11) and wired into the test infra; ASCII-clean.
close_reason: Generative FAT12+file-I/O fuzzer landed: deterministic seeded (no clock) sweep of randomized create/write_partial/read_partial/read_file/unlink across a multi-file pool, 3-way differential per op (in-process + remount + raw FAT-sync) and mtools/python at run-end, with greedy shrinking to a minimal seed+recipe. test-fat-fuzz green (200+40 seeds, ~9600 ops, deterministic across runs, in TEST_UNIT_GATES); test-fat-fuzz-mutant proves it finds+shrinks the no-RMW mutant (seed=1, 3 ops) + bites 4 others. No real bug in current fat12.c. make test green at 53 gates under load.

title: [epic] Multi-tenant file I/O: positioned read/write, seek, concurrent opens
description: Replace the single-static-buffer file model (one file open at a time, whole-file into a 64 KiB buffer at OPEN, EXEC staging reusing the same region per spec/memory_map.h) with a real multi-tenant model: per-handle positioned cluster-chain read AND write, real LSEEK, N concurrent opens via a small buffer pool, SFT teardown on EXIT, and EXEC staging decoupled from the file buffer. This is the load-bearing prerequisite for InitechBase (.dbf + .mdx open simultaneously, random seek, >64 KiB files), Turbo Initech (read source + write object, >64 KiB self-host source), and GUI app loading. Children: lq2, 0qh, snk, 6hk + the memory_map staging decouple.
acceptance_criteria: A single oracle proves: two files open concurrently with independent positioned read+write; LSEEK to arbitrary offset reads correct bytes; a >64 KiB file round-trips; EXEC of a program that itself opens a file does not corrupt either; SFT handles freed on EXIT. mtools differential stays green throughout.
close_reason: Multi-tenant file I/O epic COMPLETE. lq2 (fat12_read_partial), snk (fat12_write_partial), 0qh (positioned backend + single-buffer removal + EXEC staging decouple, proven by test-multiopen: 2 concurrent handles + 96 KiB file at offset 80000), 6hk (SFT teardown on EXIT). Single-buffer/one-file-at-a-time model eliminated; file layer ready for InitechBase (.dbf+.mdx, seek, >64 KiB) and Turbo Initech. make test green at 50 gates (35 host + 15 emu).

title: FAT12 write: seek-based partial write + multi-open write handles
description: AH=40h WRITE to a FILE uses whole-file-buffer-then-flush-at-CLOSE into a single 64KiB buffer (one open write file at a time), mirroring the read side. Implement positioned/seek-based partial write over the cluster chain + a multi-open write-handle pool. Surfaced building initech-509.11. Related: initech-lq2 (read partial), initech-0qh (multi-open pool).
close_reason: fat12_write_partial (positioned/seek write: RMW + extend + zero-hole + both-FAT sync + allocate-then-commit disk-full rollback) landed with a triple-checked differential oracle (byte model + mtools + python), a disk-full integrity leg, and 2 mutation-proven mutants. make test-unit green at 35. The 'multi-open write handles' half is folded into the Step-3 pool (initech-0qh).

Full suite 55 host + 19 emu GREEN. Optional cleanups (retire redundant SHELL_IMG; add a shell-prompt screendump gate) filed as initech-h58.

title: Remaining resident INT 21h query functions (0Eh/19h/2Ah-2Dh/36h/47h/59h/62h)
description: INT 21h core register leftovers not owned by a sibling bead: 0Eh SELDISK / 19h GETDISK (default drive A), 2Ah-2Dh GET/SET DATE/TIME (needs a clock source -- CLOCK$/RTC, see 509.7), 36h GET DISK FREE SPACE, 47h GET CWD (root only until subdirs ti8), 59h GET EXTENDED ERROR, 62h GET PSP. Currently each returns the controlled not-yet-impl diagnostic (CF=1 AX=0x0001) -- correct controlled-scope behavior but not the real function. Implement the cheap resident queries to round out the controlled register (the MCB 48h/49h/4Ah = 509.6, SETVECT/GETVECT 25h/35h = 509.8, FCB 0Fh-24h = 509.9, CREAT/write = 509.11 are separate). Surfaced completing initech-509.5.

title: Harness: QMP keystroke injection (--keys) for interactive oracles
description: The QEMU harness (harness/emu/qemu.c + qemu_main.c) has QMP screendump but no way to inject keystrokes. The keyboard driver (initech-3rs), CON input (initech-n62), and the interactive shell (initech-7pc) all need an in-emulator oracle that types keys and asserts the OS response. Add a --keys option that, after the guest boots (a delay or a serial-marker trigger), sends QMP 'send-key' events (qcode sequence) over the existing QMP socket. Reuse qmp_send/qmp_drain. Mirror the existing --screendump plumbing. Oracle: a tiny boot test that echoes injected keys to serial proves a key sent via QMP reaches the guest.
close_reason: Harness QMP keystroke injection: --keys/--keys-after send QMP send-key qcode events (letters/digits/ret/spc) over the existing QMP socket, marker-triggered; qmp_session generalizes screendump+keys+quit. Proven by the end-to-end test-kbd oracle (inject d,i,r -> guest echoes 'dir'); biting (no --keys -> no echo). QEMU-only (Bochs has no QMP send-key equivalent + is blocked at ERR-VBE, x0i).

title: Multi-file-open buffer pool (concurrent OPENs)
description: The 509.5 file backend (os/milton/fileio_fat.c) owns ONE static whole-file buffer, so a 2nd concurrent OPEN returns 0x0004 (too many open files / buffer busy). Real DOS FILES=20 allows many concurrent opens. Add a buffer pool (or the positioned partial-read above, which removes the need for whole-file buffers). Surfaced building initech-509.5.
notes: Absorbs snk's 'multi-open write handles': the pool must serve concurrent OPENs for BOTH read and write, each handle carrying its own position via fat12_read_partial/fat12_write_partial. Also owns: handle-parameterized backend vtable, int21+SFT rewire, and decoupling EXEC staging from FILE_BUFFER_BASE (memory_map.h).
close_reason: Multi-tenant positioned file I/O landed: backend vtable made positioned (read_at/write_at over the step-1/2 primitives), single 64 KiB whole-file buffer + file_data deleted, SFT slots are independent handles (root_slot added), EXEC staging decoupled. Proven by test-multiopen: 2 concurrent handles + independent positions + 96 KiB file read at offset 80000 (past the old cap); mutation-proven. make test green at 49 gates under load. Absorbed snk's multi-open write handles.

title: Positioned partial-read (fat12_read_partial) for large files
description: AH=3Fh READ currently relies on whole-file-read-at-OPEN into a single static 64KiB buffer (FILE_BUFFER_BASE). Files >64KiB cannot be opened, and only one file may be open at a time. Implement fat12_read_partial(vol,fat,entry,offset,count,buf) that navigates the cluster chain to offset/bytes_per_cluster and copies the requested slice, so READ is positioned over the chain without buffering the whole file. Brief Sec 4.2 'real read path (post-milestone)'. Surfaced building initech-509.5 file functions.
close_reason: fat12_read_partial landed: positioned cluster-chain read, host differential oracle vs independent python ref + mtools/dd (204 checks), mutation-proven (2 mutants bite). In TEST_UNIT_GATES; make test-unit green at 33 gates.

title: SFT teardown / re-init on process EXIT (multi-process)
description: sft_init() runs once at SYSINIT; the system SFT is not torn down or re-initialised when a process EXITs (4Ch). In the single-program cooperative model this is correct, but once a second program can load (or COMMAND.COM relaunches children), a prior program's open-file slots / redirected device slots would leak into the next process. On process EXIT the loader must release the process's JFT references (so file SFT slots free and the device slots' ref_counts reset) and/or sft_init must re-run. Surfaced building initech-509.3 (sft.c documents this as the SINGLE-PROCESS NOTE).
notes: Relevant when initech-509.5 (file OPEN) lands or when a multi-process/relaunch model arrives. See os/milton/sft.c SINGLE-PROCESS NOTE.
close_reason: sft_close_process walks the exiting process JFT and releases FILE-kind SFT slots (device slots 0-3 preserved by the kind gate), wired into do_terminate on g_cur_psp before g_exit. Proven by test-exit-handles (6 leaky EXEC runs x 4 opens = 24 > 16 slots, all succeed via reclaim) + mutation-proof (elide -> exhaust at run 5 -> RED). make test green at 50 gates under load.

title: INT 21h reentrancy hardening when IRQs are unmasked (DEC-04a C-5)
description: Per DEC-04a Consequence C-5: the int 0x21 trap gate (0x8F) leaves IF unchanged. Safe now ONLY because all IRQs are masked. When IRQ0(PIT)/IRQ1(keyboard) are unmasked (shell phase), an IRQ arriving inside the INT 21h dispatcher could re-enter it non-reentrantly (DOS INT 21h is not reentrant) and corrupt the frame. Harden: cli at int21_entry / sti before iretd, OR a reentrancy semaphore. Related: initech-n62 (keyboard/IRQ1), initech-3rs (PS/2 + PIT).
acceptance_criteria: INT 21h is reentrancy-safe with IRQs live (no frame corruption under an IRQ storm during a syscall).
notes: UPDATE (orch 2026-06-09): IRQs are now LIVE (initech-3rs unmasked IRQ0/IRQ1 + sti). INT 21h uses 0x8F TRAP gates (IF stays set), so a keyboard/PIT IRQ CAN now interrupt an in-flight INT 21h call. Currently SAFE purely because the kbd/pit ISRs share ZERO state with the dispatcher (verified: no refs to int21/g_dta/g_find/g_sft/g_cur_psp in kbd.c/pit.c). This bead's deeper audit is still owed: any future path where an ISR touches INT 21h state (or INT 21h calls kbd/pit while a search/DTA op is mid-flight) breaks the invariant -- then either mask IRQs around the critical section or make the state per-context. No locks now (cooperative model).
close_reason: Hardened: in-IRQ guard (g_irq_depth bracketed in the irq stubs) fails loud if INT 21h is entered from IRQ context; InDOS depth counter + dos_in_dos() hook (with do_exec snapshot/restore so EXEC chains don't drift it); kbd ring confirmed the sole ISR<->dispatcher shared structure (SPSC-safe). Proven by test-int21-irqstorm (5/5 enum + byte-exact multi-cluster read + 2nd handle under a 45-key + 100Hz-PIT storm) and 2 mutants (A: PIT scribble -> 4/5 enum -> RED; B: PIT int 0x21 -> guard panic -> RED). make test green at 51 gates under load. Verified by orchestrator (Rule 4); EXEC/conin/shell unaffected.

title: Ratify ADR amendment DEC-04a: 32-bit-flat INT 21h calling convention + IDT/PIC vector map
description: Research (docs/research/internals-int21h-ground-truth.md) surfaced load-bearing architectural choices for the INT 21h surface in 32-bit flat protected mode that are NOT derivable from ratified ADRs and warrant operator ratification (memory: ADRs are operator-ratified + authoritative): (1) literal int 0x21 via a TRAP gate (0x8F) at vector 0x21; (2) PIC remap master->0x28 / slave->0x30 (NOT the conventional 0x20/0x28) to keep vector 0x21 free for int 0x21 -- avoids the INT 21h<->IRQ1(keyboard) collision; (3) flat calling convention: AH=function (EAX[15:8]), flat ptr in EDX, count ECX, handle EBX, return EAX, error via CF in saved EFLAGS; (4) int21_frame_t layout matching the asm pushad order.
