title: I123 B08: Supply the existing NOW evaluator with the guest clock on recalculation
description: Root cause: os/i123/core/recalc.c:92 initializes have_now=0; eval.c:912-914 correctly requires it. os/i123/app/face_a.c:931,938,974-981 and :699-702 recalculate without supplying now/have_now anywhere in the app. The existing clock service is os/apps/tbx/tbx.h:137-139, tbx_get_clock. Ground truth: Lotus Reference p. 13-46 (PDF 334), @NOW current date/time serial refreshed at recalculation; spec/i123/wk1_formula.h and the existing date serial rules, including the Lotus 1900 convention. This is an omitted input to an implemented evaluator, not evidence that the engine lacks @NOW. Pickup: Read the real guest clock through the existing gate into valid static/BSS storage, convert to the Lotus serial and supply a coherent clock snapshot to every recalculation route and its nested context. Clock failure must remain explicit, without fixed fake success values. Clock rendering/configuration is separate from this formula input. Acceptance oracle: Extend test-i123-formula and the Face A mock with injected guest dates/times, F9, automatic edits, manual mode and nested evaluation. Replay functions on QEMU/Bochs with a locked RTC, independently check saved @NOW numeric cache and its change after a known clock step. A mutant omitting have_now or freezing the second snapshot must fail. Record a record-flair clip. Evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-i123/REPORT.md (L011); docs/audits/2026-10-23-i123/shots/func-25.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-i123/evidence/functions-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-i123/evidence/extracted/functions/FUNCS.json (Audit docs/audits/2026-10-23-i123/REPORT.md L011; triage docs/audits/2026-10-23-i123/TRIAGE.md)

title: I123 B07: Accept the documented leading dollar sign in numeric entry
description: Root cause: os/i123/app/face_a.c:905-908 classifies $ as VALUE, but os/i123/core/fmt.c:653-668 accepts only an optional sign followed by digits/decimal point; commit at face_a.c:934-947 then attempts formula parsing and refuses $12.34. Ground truth: Lotus Reference p. 1-19 (PDF 35), audit evidence/references/manual-pdf-035.txt: a leading dollar sign enters the number and currency display is a separate format choice. Pickup: Recognize the documented typed-number currency prefix at the entry boundary without treating absolute formula references such as +$A$1 as numeric literals. Preserve percent, exponent, sign and invalid-input rules; capture sign/currency ordering edge cases from real Lotus before broadening the grammar. Acceptance oracle: Extend the numeric/Face A entry host oracles with $12.34 -> numeric 12.34, separate currency formatting, absolute-reference controls and invalid embedded dollars. Replay entry on QEMU/Bochs, save and independently decode the WK1 numeric record. A mutant rejecting the leading dollar must fail. Record a record-flair clip. title: I123 B06: Render and hit-test the visible part of an oversized active column
description: Root cause: os/i123/app/face_a.c:343 uses whole-column i123_cols_fitting (sheet.c:429-439); col_x at :350-351 rejects even the first column when zero full columns fit. paint_border at :445 and paint_pointer at :486-488 therefore omit heading and pointer although Set-Width accepts 1..240 at :719-725. Ground truth: The authored native-viewport usability requirement in REPORT.md L008 and the implemented 1..240 width contract at sheet.c:398-402; Lotus Reference chapter 12 Column. Existing native-window geometry is face_a.c:102-124. No requirement to shrink the supported width range is inferred. Pickup: Keep a partially visible first column in the view and consistently clip heading, cell, pointer and hit-testing to the actual content rectangle. Retain full 240-character storage/display width, and preserve navigation/resizing behavior. Acceptance oracle: Extend test_i123_resize.c/test_i123_hit.c and the row renderer oracle with width 240 at normal and minimum window sizes, partial first columns, neighbor navigation and clicks. title: I123 B05: Return prompts and ordinary error notices to their proper caller
description: Root cause: os/i123/app/face_a.c:864 sends every M_RANGE Escape through menu_mode even when A_GOTO was entered directly from READY. At :868 Return dismisses M_NOTICE only when g_error is set, but notice() at :578 sets g_notice instead. Ground truth: Lotus Reference p. 1-5 (PDF 21) explicitly allows ESC or ENTER to clear an error; chapter 1 GOTO/cancellation plus the authored caller-restoration expectation in REPORT.md L018. Audit evidence/references/manual-pdf-021.txt contains the error-key rule. Pickup: Retain the origin of direct GOTO versus slash-command range prompts and make all ordinary error notices dismiss on Return as well as Escape. Do not change menu-level Escape/backtracking or discard a pending input line on unrelated notices. Acceptance oracle: Extend test_i123_keys.c and test_i123_range_menu.c with F5/Escape from READY, nested menu range Escape, unsupported leaf/Return, invalid-GOTO/Return/Escape and saved-input controls. Replay keyslook in QEMU/Bochs and assert mode/pointer/worksheet preservation. Mutants routing all M_RANGE Escape to MENU and restoring the g_error-only Return guard must fail. Record a record-flair clip. title: I123 B04: Resume Finder power actions after an asynchronous worksheet Save
description: Root cause: os/milton/kmain.c:5715-5723 asks Quit, services the immediate callback, then equates still resident with cancellation. os/i123/app/face_a.c:1245-1247 has only opened the Save filename prompt; successful write/exit happens later at :660-662. finder_power returns at kmain.c:5738-5739 and retains no pending continuation. Ground truth: Inside Macintosh Vol VI PDF p. 345, Listing 6-8, as cited at kmain.c:5691-5704: the normal Quit routine saves documents or returns userCanceledErr. The pending-Save continuation is an authored native shutdown workflow requirement, not a DOS Lotus feature. Pickup: Represent pending quit separately from explicit cancellation and resume the original Shut Down/Restart action only after the app finishes successfully. Save failure/cancel keeps the desktop and document open. Coordinate with initech-cqej for its decline/Bochs/clip tests; its title tracks test coverage, not this asynchronous continuation defect, so L003 is not DUP. Acceptance oracle: Extend the power/tenant host state-machine oracle and test-flair-shutdown/test-flair-restart with Save -> filename -> successful exit -> one power completion, Cancel, failed save, replacement cancellation, and no-app controls. Replay power twice on QEMU and Bochs with independent WK1 extraction plus FLAIR-SHUTDOWN-SAFE/reset markers. A mutant restoring still-resident==declined must fail the deferred-Save case. Record a record-flair clip. title: I123 B03: Format supported high decimal counts without a scaled-integer ceiling
description: Root cause: os/i123/core/fmt.c:245-248 and :784-787 multiply by 10^decimals then reject magnitudes >=9e15. The display path emits stars independently of available width; eval.c:1166-1167 turns the same fixed-text refusal into ERR for @STRING. Ground truth: Lotus Reference pp. 10-4..10-6 (PDF 222..224) and p. 13-56 (PDF 344), retained in the audit reference extractions: 0..15 decimal places, width-based display overflow, and @STRING(x,n). Real rounding/precision bytes must come from Lotus rather than an artifact-derived expected string. Pickup: Use a bounded decimal conversion that supports the documented decimal counts and separates numeric conversion from field-width overflow. Preserve the existing currency/comma signs, percent scaling, trailing reserved character and rounding rules; share the conversion where the rules agree. Acceptance oracle: Extend test-i123-wk1-roundtrip and test-i123-formula with independent real-Lotus goldens for the exact 1234.5678912345 cases, signs, zero, carry rounding, F/C/comma 12..15, percent 10..15 and @STRING. Replay formats_wide and edge_more on QEMU/Bochs; compare displayed text and extracted formula/string caches separately. Mutants restoring each 9e15 guard must fail. Record a record-flair clip. close_reason: Not a bug: real Lotus 1-2-3 R2.2 shows stars / ERR at the same bounds (lane cx-i123num minted real goldens under fixtures/i123-numeric: F/C/comma 13-14 fit, 15 stars; P11-12 fit, P13-15 stars; @STRING(1234.5678912345,15) is ERR in Lotus itself). The audit's B03 expectation exceeds the real product. Law 1/2: the golden wins.

title: I123 B02: Reclaim erased default cells and reuse replacement label storage
description: Root cause: os/i123/app/face_a.c:756-758 erases then always reapplies the format, and os/i123/core/sheet.c:388 allocates a BLANK even for the default format. sheet.c:250 allocates a replacement blob before subtracting the old live bytes at :259; compaction at :207-209 still sees both allocations. Ground truth: The authored capacity-recovery/data-preservation expectations in REPORT.md L010/L032; os/i123/core/sheet.c:308 and face_a.c:169-170 define the accepted label/store limits. ../lotus123-decomp/specs/file-formats/wk1-format.md Sec 4.1 says content-free default-format cells are omitted, while nondefault format/protection needs BLANK records. Lotus Reference p. 10-3 requires erasing contents while preserving effective format/protection. Pickup: Elide a BLANK only when absence represents exactly the same effective default format and protection. Replace equal/smaller label blobs in place or transact them without requiring duplicate live capacity; retain old contents on genuine failure. This owns allocation/recovery, not the already tracked unexplained-exhaustion diagnostic in initech-vdgd. Acceptance oracle: Add capacity and allocator cases to the sheet/Face A host oracles: 2048 cells then erase ordinary A1 and enter A2049; preserve explicit-format/protection BLANKs; 135 labels of 240 characters then equal-size/shorter replacement and genuine overflow with old bytes intact. Replay capacity and pool on QEMU/Bochs and independently parse CAPERA.WK1/POOLOUT.WK1. Mutants restoring unconditional default BLANK allocation and allocate-before-reclaim must go red. Record a record-flair clip. title: SAMIR: preserve typed precondition and malformed-index errors at command boundaries
description: Root: os/samir/cmd/set.c:415-417 maps all ndx_open_rw failures to missing-file ordinal 1. os/samir/cmd/mutate.c:609/:767/:917 returns syntax with ec=0 for absent tables, so the correct catalog mapper emits 10. Preserve typed causes at these hook boundaries: missing stays 1, malformed NDX gets its measured damaged-index code, and no database gets 52. This differs from old u78k internal-status/catalog collisions. Ground truth: spec/samir/dbase_msg_codes.tsv contains 1/52/114; ../dbase3-decomp/specs/file-formats/ndx.md defines header validation and commands/data-definition-and-manipulation.md gives table preconditions. Mint the precise III+ corrupt-index response; a present malformed file is definitely not nonexistent. Acceptance oracle: Extend test_interp_set.c/test_samir_repl.c for missing/truncated/bad-geometry NDX versus valid files, and DELETE/RECALL/PACK/REPLACE without a table versus genuine syntax errors. Replay errors.json/artifact-controls.json; assert no disk/work-area mutation. Mutants mapping malformed to 1 and no-table to 10 must each fail the error-class matrix. title: SAMIR: retain, recall and list command history
description: Root: os/samir/samir_main.c:644-656 reads a new line without history storage; os/samir/pal/pal_milton.c:633 drops nonprintable keys on the app editor. query.c:1389-1397 has no HISTORY dispatch and set.c:732-739 rejects it. title: SAMIR: recognize four-letter command and keyword abbreviations consistently
description: Root: os/samir/cmd/flow.c:660-703 uppercases whole tokens without canonicalization; :879-894 and hooks compare full spellings (os/samir/cmd/query.c:1389; mutate.c:1437). REPL special dispatch also compares whole words (samir_main.c:206). Add one recognition policy before classification, dispatch and applicable keyword parsing, without changing identifiers or strings. Ground truth: ../dbase3-decomp/specs/runtime/interpreter-and-execution-model.md:188-224 documents minimum-four-character recognition and full matching for short verbs. The shipped u2-commands.tex:26 restriction is an honest limitation, not canon. Mint ambiguous/invalid long spellings before choosing behavior. Cover PRGs/prompt, clauses, invalid suffixes and same-prefix variable names. Replay missing.json. A mutant disabling recognition for one hook must fail that abbreviation differential. title: SAMIR: apply SET FIXED through the existing numeric formatter
description: Root: os/samir/cmd/set.c:660 implements DECIMALS but :732-739 rejects FIXED. os/samir/cmd/query.c formatters have no FIXED-state consumer. Add the toggle and its display policy without altering stored numbers or DBF descriptor precision. Ground truth: ../dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/set-commands.md sec.2/sec.3.1 defines FIXED with DECIMALS. Capture integer/fractional/negative/stored-field output in real III+ rather than extrapolating modern formatting. title: SAMIR: support literal TEXT blocks and program command echo in the flow executor
description: Root: os/samir/cmd/flow.c:872-897 lacks TEXT/ENDTEXT block classification; :1570-1574 expands/dispatches ordinary lines as commands. os/samir/cmd/set.c:732-739 rejects ECHO, and run_block has no trace consumer. Implement literal-line handling before macro/comment/verb processing plus stored ECHO state consumed at execution. These share the flow-output mechanism, not the expression printer. Ground truth: ../dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/programming-and-io.md:494-517 requires literal whitespace-preserving TEXT without macros; commands/set-commands.md:150 defines ECHO. Use existing CONSOLE/ALTERNATE routing; mint exact III+ trace layout. Acceptance oracle: Extend test_interp_flow.c/test_interp_set.c for literal blank/indented lines, ampersands, && and command-looking text; missing ENDTEXT must fail cleanly. Test ECHO ON/OFF around programs/nested calls without changing program output. Compare new III+ transcripts and run TEXT/USEPRG in an emulator. Mutants feeding literal lines to flow_expand and omitting trace must fail separate checks. title: SAMIR: add a common printer output route for LIST and print settings
description: Root: os/samir/cmd/query.c:451-490 handles scope/FOR/WHILE/OFF, so TO PRINT becomes expression text. os/samir/cmd/set.c:732-739 lacks MARGIN/PRINT/DEVICE branches. os/samir/cmd/workarea.c:1499-1506 routes to mirror/console only; PAL has no printer sink. First pickup: one real output-router contract for LIST TO PRINT, PRINT ON/OFF mirroring, margin and DEVICE state; integrate @ SAY printing as its forms consumer lands. Missing printers must reach the real unavailable-printer error, never false success. Ground truth: ../dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/navigation-query-display.md:656-665 and commands/set-commands.md:225-233/:359-370 define behavior: MARGIN is print-only; DEVICE routes @ SAY; PRINT mirrors ordinary output. report.c:460 already reaches catalog 126. Mint independent III+ output, add an emulator captured-printer leg and a no-printer leg reaching 126. Verify SCREEN/PRINT OFF controls. Mutants dropping LIST routing, applying margins to screen or ignoring DEVICE must fail. Parser-only success does not certify printing. title: SAMIR: connect UNIQUE index creation and SET UNIQUE to the NDX engine
description: Root: os/samir/cmd/mutate.c:1122 rejects tokens after the output name. os/samir/cmd/set.c:732-739 rejects UNIQUE; os/samir/fs/ndx.c:1488 always writes unique_flag=0. Add the setting/option with duplicate suppression and persistent policy, not syntax accepted without altered index contents. Ground truth: ../dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/data-definition-and-manipulation.md sec.15 says UNIQUE keeps the first record for equal keys without deleting DBF rows; commands/set-commands.md:165 and file-formats/ndx.md define policy/header. This absent command policy is distinct from the generic ahu codec epic. Acceptance oracle: Extend test_samir_dml.c/test_ndx_build.c with duplicate C/N/D keys, UNIQUE versus SET UNIQUE ON/OFF, reopen, REINDEX and insert/replace maintenance. title: SAMIR: open and edit PRG files through MODIFY COMMAND
description: Root: os/samir/samir_main.c:593-615 registers no program editor; query/mutate/set/proc/report hooks do not accept MODIFY, so os/samir/cmd/flow.c:1208 refuses it. The disk PRG loader at samir_main.c:472 supports execution only. First pickup: load FLOW.PRG, edit text, save/cancel and return to the session; retain broader editor commands on this feature. Ground truth: ../dbase3-decomp/specs/full-screen/assist-ui-and-editors.md sec.9 describes MODIFY COMMAND and program editing. Use reference-confirmed III+ keys and a new real-software trace rather than inventing modern editor bindings. Acceptance oracle: Add host buffer/file-lifetime tests and a locked guest open/edit/save/reopen/DO trace, plus cancel, missing file, size boundaries, full disk and failed close. Saved files must execute and open in III+; failed/cancelled saves must preserve original bytes. Record the interaction. A mutant omitting the save write must fail independently extracted bytes, not merely an editor-state assertion. title: SAMIR: add a bounded SAY, GET and READ form workflow
description: Root: os/samir/cmd/flow.c:660 tokenizes @ but :872-897 gives it no form classification; os/samir/samir_main.c:593-615 registers no forms module and flow.c:1208 reports unknown verb. Terminal PAL slots exist (os/samir/include/samir/pal.h:148), but no GET list/READ consumer does. First pickup: @ SAY and one character memvar GET/READ with actual positioning, write-back and measured accept/cancel behavior; retain broader grammar on this feature. Ground truth: InitechOS-PRD.md sec.6.6 expressly includes @ SAY/GET/READ; ../dbase3-decomp/specs/full-screen/say-get-read.md sec.1-8 and real CLIENTS.FMT/MENUMASK.PRG ground coordinates, input and values. Exclude later Harbour syntax explicitly marked in the spec. Acceptance oracle: Add independent host form-state/PAL cursor/input tests, then drive FORM.PRG and @ 2,3 SAY HELLO on both emulator launch routes. Compare coordinates and accepted values with real III+; cancel/invalid input must preserve measured state. Record the interaction. Mutants swapping row/column or dropping READ write-back must fail distinct checks. Coordinate B08 terminal binding and existing CONFIRM/ESCAPE settings without duplicating their beads. title: SAMIR: resolve nested DO calls to disk PRGs
description: Root: os/samir/cmd/proc.c:609-613 searches only p_find_procedure and rejects a miss. Disk loading exists solely in os/samir/samir_main.c:550 and the outer REPL call at :675; no program-side fallback uses it. Add a shared owned-source loader/call-frame path, without invoking the REPL recursively or overwriting caller source. Ground truth: ../dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/programming-and-io.md:71-85 defines DO of a procedure or PRG. Same-name precedence is oracle-resolves; mint it. The manual honestly documents internal-only nested DO. Existing u78k USE/CLOSE dispatch is a different missing route. Acceptance oracle: Extend test_interp_proc.c/test_samir_repl.c for OUTER -> USEPRG, WITH character/numeric parameters, nested internal procedures, missing files, errors and repeated calls. Assert source lifetime, caller continuation, scope cleanup and table survival. Run control.json in an emulator against III+ output. A mutant removing file fallback must fail. Coordinate QUIT/retry/unwind/recursion with initech-39e5. title: SAMIR desktop launch: provide its terminal controls and consume BEL correctly
description: Root: os/samir/pal/pal_milton.c:581-596 emits ANSI cursor/attribute controls for the status screen. The FLAIR launch at os/milton/kmain.c:2946-2963 clears the raw console and executes SAMIR, bypassing DOS-path ANSI binding at :8082-8095. os/milton/int21.c:764 requires the binding/gate; raw os/milton/console.c:237-270 lacks BEL handling and paints byte 7. Bind terminal capabilities on desktop text launch and handle BEL without visible glyphs; preserve byte-transparent file output. Ground truth: pubs/manuals/initechbase-quick-reference/qr-set.tex:16 documents the status bar; ../dbase3-decomp/specs/full-screen/assist-ui-and-editors.md sec.10 describes it. BEL must not advance/paint text, per the audit terminal requirement. Intentional raw ANSI behavior without ANSI.SYS does not authorize an app to use unavailable controls. Acceptance oracle: Extend test_samir_status.c/test_samir_screen_emu.c and console/ANSI tests. Drive status ON/OFF, query, scroll and return on DOS/desktop; inspect guest pixels for bar/cursor and rejected-key BEL for no extra glyph/cursor movement. Verify redirected bytes and desktop restoration; record a record-flair clip. Mutants omitting desktop binding and rendering BEL as printable must each fail. title: SAMIR: set both BOF and EOF for physically empty work areas
description: Root: os/samir/cmd/workarea.c:538-539 initializes empty BOF=0 and EOF=1; :678-681 repeats this on refresh. os/samir/cmd/nav.c:263-267 returns early for empty GO TOP without correcting flags. Apply one empty-table boundary invariant across USE, navigation and count-changing operations while preserving closed-area and nonempty BOF semantics. Ground truth: ../dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/navigation-query-display.md:999 explicitly requires EOF and BOF true and RECNO=1 for empty files. The contrary nav.c comment is not independent ground truth; mint the exact III+ boundary transcript before locking it. Acceptance oracle: Extend test_interp_nav.c/test_interp_use.c for USE EMPTY, GO TOP/BOTTOM, refresh, last-record PACK/ZAP and append back to nonempty. Distinguish physically empty from nonempty FILTER/DELETED-hidden tables. Replay verify-final.json against a newly minted III+ transcript. A mutant clearing empty BOF must fail both open and navigation assertions. title: SAMIR: run programs within the advertised byte limit regardless of short-line count
description: Root: os/samir/cmd/flow.c:54 fixes FLOW_MAX_LINES at 512. samir_do at :1847-1867 uses fixed line/kind arrays and maps split_lines overflow to error 43; 7018-byte SHORT1K.PRG never executes although the loader permits 8191 bytes (os/samir/samir_main.c:459). Replace the hidden line-count bottleneck with bounded storage for the supported byte envelope. Simply growing automatic arrays aggravates the fixed-stack recursion defect on initech-39e5. Ground truth: pubs/manuals/initechbase-volume-one/u5-entries-a.tex:331-333 advertises 8191 characters without a 512-line restriction; the fixture is 7018 CRLF bytes. PRD 6.6 requires working program execution. This undocumented lower implementation limit is not deliberate canon. Acceptance oracle: Extend test_interp_flow.c/test_samir_repl.c for 511/512/513/1000 lines and the smallest-line worst case within 8191 bytes. SHORT1K must print 1000; over-byte-limit rejection must be clean. Include constrained PAL memory/guest stack bounds, a copied-image programedges trace and a subsequent command. A mutant restoring the 512-line cap must fail. Coordinate storage ownership with the recursion lane. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/fixtures/SHORT1K.PRG, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/programedges-serial.log, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/programs-real-serial.log, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/shots/programedges-1000.png. title: SAMIR: accept complete 254-byte console commands with STATUS both off and on
description: Root: os/samir/pal/pal_milton.c:650-654 selects application line input only with an active status screen; otherwise it frames AH=3Fh cooked console input. os/milton/int21.c:3227/:3252 intentionally cap that DOS editor at 128 bytes. Fix SAMIR console-input selection/framing, retaining the DOS handle contract and redirected streams. Consume an overlong application line without executing its truncated prefix. Ground truth: pubs/manuals/initechbase-volume-one/ua-keys.tex:20-22 and u2-commands.tex:16 promise 254 characters; ../dbase3-decomp/specs/runtime/interpreter-and-execution-model.md sec.2.1 independently defines the limit. The DOS staging buffer is not itself defective. Acceptance oracle: Extend test_samir_input.c/test_samir_repl.c and locked emulator traces for 127/128/129/253/254/255 characters, STATUS ON/OFF, both launches and redirected CRLF input. The 254-byte LEN case must return 245; 255 must raise 18 and leave the next command intact. Assert no truncated mutation executes. A mutant routing STATUS OFF back through 128-byte cooked input must fail. title: SAMIR: infer INDEX key geometry independently of the current record and enforce its limit
description: Root: os/samir/cmd/mutate.c:1124-1130 evaluates the incoming current record to determine key type/width. os/samir/cmd/workarea.c:866 returns empty typed character values at EOF/empty, so ndx_build rejects zero key length (os/samir/fs/ndx.c:1336). The command also lacks a 100-byte key check; ndx_build validates page geometry only (:1339-1345), permitting the archived 101-byte key. Derive stable expression geometry including zero-record tables and report catalog 23 for oversize character keys. Ground truth: ../dbase3-decomp/specs/file-formats/ndx.md empty-root layout, commands/data-definition-and-manipulation.md sec.15, and spec/samir/dbase_msg_codes.tsv:31 (100 char maximum). Expression-source length is a different limit. The corpus marks precise boundary semantics oracle-resolves; mint III+ 100/101 cases before locking them. Acceptance oracle: Extend test_samir_dml.c/test_ndx_build.c for empty C(12), EOF/BOF/current-record permutations, expressions and 100/101/254-byte values. An empty index must reopen, SEEK miss and accept an append. Compare nonempty traversal with real III+ and independent decoded bytes; keep blank-date L016 on initech-ylqs. Replay index-fresh.json/index-boundary.json. Mutants using the current zero-width value or removing the cap must fail distinct cases. title: SAMIR: refresh the live memo reader after a successful replacement
description: Root: os/samir/fs/dbf.c:1763-1770 appends through a separate writable DBT handle and publishes the new pointer. The work area retains its reader (os/samir/cmd/workarea.c:487/:903). os/samir/fs/dbt.c:521-531 already refreshes next_free, contrary to the audit guess; Milton handles still retain independent file-size snapshots (os/milton/fileio_fat.c:39-43; os/milton/int21.c:3374). Reading the appended block through the old handle returns short, and workarea.c:905 converts that failure to empty text. Refresh/reopen the reader on successful write; do not require USE or hide real read errors as empty memos. Ground truth: ../dbase3-decomp/specs/file-formats/dbt.md sec.4/sec.8 and commands/data-definition-and-manipulation.md REPLACE; PRD 6.6 requires correct DBF/DBT round trips. This is a distinct same-session read-after-write defect; persisted text is correct. Acceptance oracle: Add a PAL with Milton-style per-open size snapshots to test_dbt_read.c/test_samir_core.c; a POSIX reader alone misses the defect. Repeat two replacements, direct reads, GO away/back and reopen; check lengths and DBF pointer/DBT bytes. Replay memo.json on desktop and DOS. A mutant retaining the old reader after append must return empty in the oracle and fail. Inject genuine short-read failures separately. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/memo.json, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/memo-serial.log, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/memo-files/EDGE.DBF, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/memo-files/EDGE.DBT, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/shots/memo-write.png. (Audit docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/REPORT.md L005; triage docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/TRIAGE.md)

title: SAMIR: remove failed new INDEX, SORT and COPY FILE outputs so retry works
description: Root: os/samir/fs/ndx.c:1472 creates/truncates output, but :1500 and later failed-write exits only close it. os/samir/cmd/mutate.c:1202-1209 creates SORT output and closes on failure without remove; :1294 and :1309-1323 do the same for COPY FILE. d_destination at :1084-1085 then rejects the abandoned name under SAFETY. Use one owned-output failure/commit policy across these paths; never delete a pre-existing destination as failed-new-file cleanup. Ground truth: ../dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/data-definition-and-manipulation.md sec.15 describes deleting an incomplete interrupted index; DBF/NDX format invariants require complete structures. Removal or safe staging of failed new SORT/COPY outputs is the audit recovery requirement, not a claim of historical transaction guarantees. Acceptance oracle: Extend test_samir_dml.c, test_ndx_build.c and PAL fault injection across create, each short/failed write, and close. Verify source hashes, SAFETY and existing targets survive. At zero free clusters, run full-recovery, free FILLER.BIN and retry all three names without manual ERASE; extract valid outputs with mtools and independently parse DBF/NDX. A mutant omitting cleanup must leave a zero-byte name and fail the retry assertion. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/full-recovery-serial.log, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/full-recovery-bytes.json, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/full-recovery-files/FULLIDX.NDX, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/full-recovery-files/SORTED.DBF, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/full-recovery-files/COPIED.DBF, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/shots/full-recovery-failure.png. (Audit docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/REPORT.md L043; triage docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/TRIAGE.md)

title: Implement prompt-level ECHO state and the blank-line shorthand
description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:184 tokenizes ECHO. as a distinct external word and the classify table at :86 recognizes only ECHO. dispatch_control at :4541 updates echo_on only when a batch frame exists; otherwise builtin_echo at :2968 always reports on and :2971 prints OFF/ON as text. No processor-level echo state or ECHO. syntax exists. Ground truth: MS-DOS 3.3 User's Guide ECHO, Reference printed p.143 / PDF228 (evidence/manual-page-228.txt), defines ON/OFF; ADR-0003 DEC-11. Mint actual DOS 3.3 interactive ON/OFF and ECHO. behavior because the report explicitly labels the blank-line shorthand as memory. Shipped Reference currently documents the narrower prompt behavior. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend command parser/execution host tests with ECHO., ECHO text, ON/OFF/query, @ suppression and CALL/secondary processor state. Replay B036 and advanced-keyboard on QEMU: blank line without Bad command; OFF followed by a query reports off. Grade ECHO. bytes and state lifetime against the real DOS 3.3 golden. Mutants: classify ECHO. externally or keep frame-only state; each must fail. Update both ECHO manual entries and examples. Scope: Define state inheritance/restoration with B11 before changing nested-session semantics; the feature must not consume literal message text as an option unexpectedly. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/suite3-B036-echo.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/suite3-B036.txt; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/advanced-keyboard-interactive-expansion.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/advanced-keyboard-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/manual-page-228.txt. (Audit docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/REPORT.md L023,L024; triage docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/TRIAGE.md)

title: Add DATE and TIME entry prompts and TIME fractional-field parsing
description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:3469 and :3499 only report the clock when no argument is supplied. The entry loops exist solely in startup_datetime at :3654/:3664. cmd_parse_time at :972 rejects remaining .hundredths text, and dos_settime at :2206 always passes DL=0. int21.c:4924 explicitly ignores fractional seconds because the current RTC seam has one-second resolution. Ground truth: MS-DOS 3.3 User's Guide DATE printed p.55 / PDF140 and TIME pp.120-121 / PDF205-206 (evidence/manual-page-140.txt, manual-page-205.txt, manual-page-206.txt); spec/int21h_register.json AH=2Ch/2Dh. The shipped manual currently promises display-only/no-fraction forms. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend test_command date/time parsing plus a fake-clock C execution oracle: no-arg entry, blank retains, invalid reprompts, leap-day and range limits, .00/.99 and malformed suffixes. Replay B038/B039 under QEMU; TIME 13:14:15.99 must be accepted and both no-arg commands must request input. Mutation: omit the no-arg prompt or reject the fractional field; require each leg to fail. Document the RTC rounding/resolution contract explicitly rather than claiming retained hundredths without implementing and testing it. Scope: Reuse entry/validation logic without rerunning startup as a side effect; synchronize the Reference syntax and examples when the broader forms ship. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/suite3-B038-date-formats.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/suite3-B039-time-values.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/suite3-B038.txt; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/suite3-B039.txt; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/manual-page-140.txt; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/manual-page-205.txt; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/manual-page-206.txt. (Audit docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/REPORT.md L021,L036,L037; triage docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/TRIAGE.md)

title: Implement DEL directory as confirmed deletion of its contained files
description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:3321 recognizes delete-all confirmation only for a literal *.* leaf. A non-wildcard directory reaches dos_unlink at :3347, so the backend correctly rejects deleting the directory as a file. No directory-operand expansion to contained files exists at the shell entry. Ground truth: MS-DOS 3.3 User's Guide DEL, Reference printed p.56 / PDF141 (evidence/manual-page-141.txt), explicitly accepts a directory name to delete its files. Backend rejection of unlinking directories must remain. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend the host DOS safety/FAT oracle with a named directory, nested subdirectory, read-only child and 300 ordinary files; N must preserve every byte and Y must delete only eligible immediate files while retaining directories and protected children. Replay B023 under QEMU and verify the stopped image with mtools/fsck.fat. Mutants: route the directory straight to unlink, delete without confirmation, or recurse into children; the state assertions must fail. Scope: Resolve the operand as a directory before transforming it to directory\*.*; retain drive identity and the existing protected-file/no-cap enumeration behavior. title: Offer the DOS batch-termination question and support continuing with N
description: Root cause: os/milton/int21.c:5337 sets the shell recovery latch; os/milton/command.c:4618 immediately exits the batch loop whenever it is set. There is no batch-specific Y/N decision or resume path for a PAUSE or ECHO/GOTO loop. Ground truth: MS-DOS 3.3 User's Guide PAUSE, Reference printed p.149 / PDF234 (evidence/resume-manual-page-234.txt). pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch4-batch.tex:38-39 currently documents immediate cancellation, so this is a missing compatibility feature, not a broken narrow promise. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Add a C execution-state oracle and QEMU resume_driver.py batch legs: Ctrl-C at PAUSE and in LOOP.BAT, Y ends and N continues exactly once; test invalid answer, nested CALL and redirected input/output cleanup. Capture real DOS 3.3 behavior for which nested frame is cancelled. Mutant: always terminate or always resume regardless of answer; each must fail a post-question sentinel. Update the manual and its examples with the new behavior. Scope: Depends on reliable resident-call interruption handling from B01; do not use a nonlocal jump that skips open-handle restoration. title: Honor SORT starting columns and reject unsupported options
description: Root cause: os/milton/sort_program.asm:64 scans for /R only and silently advances past every other switch at :76. compare_lines at :272 always starts both pointers at the first byte; no /+n offset exists. Ground truth: MS-DOS 3.3 User's Guide SORT, Reference printed p.116 / PDF201 (evidence/manual-page-201.txt), defines /R and /+n. Unsupported-option refusal should use an independently captured DOS 3.3 diagnostic/status rather than a new invented success. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend test-sort-filter with SORTCOL.TXT, /+1, /+4, reverse plus column, short/empty lines, invalid columns, /BAD and status checks, graded against literal independent results and a real DOS 3.3 argument golden. QEMU followup must put 02 apple before 01 zebra with /+4, and external must refuse /BAD. Mutants: ignore the column offset or accept unknown switches; require both to go red. Scope: Keep the existing explicit capacity refusal and ordinary case-insensitive/reverse comparisons intact; over-capacity truncation was not found by this audit. title: Keep batch arguments beyond percent-9 and correct the SHIFT manual
description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:4650 allocates only ten argv slots and :4670 stops parsing after nine supplied parameters; batch_frame.view[10] at :4444 and the count clamp at :4611 provide no later-argument reservoir for SHIFT. SHIFT at :4575 correctly starts at zero, so %0 changes. pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch4-batch.tex:247 incorrectly promises %0 is unchanged. Ground truth: MS-DOS 3.3 User's Guide SHIFT, Reference printed p.151 / PDF236 (evidence/manual-page-236.txt), explicitly describes more than ten parameters and losing the original %0. The shipped nine-argument limit describes the current narrower feature; only the %0 statement is a present documentation defect. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend an execution-level C batch oracle with 11+ short parameters within the command-tail limit, repeated SHIFT through exhaustion, empty arguments and independent nested CALL frames. QEMU B060/TEN must expose ten then eleven in %9 while shifting %0 as DOS does. Correct the Reference comment/text and recorded SHIFT example; run test-pubs-examples and the DOS manual gate. Mutants: stop storing after nine or start shifting at slot one; both must fail independent expected output. Scope: Keep the visible substitution window %0..%9; the missing feature is retaining later command-tail arguments, not adding modern %10 syntax. Correct the separate manual limit when the reservoir ships. title: Provide a secondary interactive COMMAND session with EXIT back to its caller
description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:4705 rejects every COMMAND invocation that does not begin /C. There is no interactive secondary-prompt entry even though /C already saves private environment and shell-exit context at :4711-4727. Ground truth: pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch2-entries-b.tex:102-104 promises typing commands in a second processor; MS-DOS 3.3 COMMAND, Reference printed pp.46-47. ADR-0003 DEC-11 defines the native interpreter. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend the command-session host oracle and a QEMU followup trace: COMMAND -> private SET/PROMPT -> COMMAND /C ECHO NESTED -> EXIT -> parent prompt. Verify the parent environment, CWD/handle rules from the real DOS 3.3 golden, nested depth refusal, and permanent-shell EXIT. Mutant: retain the mandatory /C guard or let EXIT unwind the permanent processor; each must fail the session marker assertions. Scope: Factor an interactive loop that does not rerun SYSINIT/AUTOEXEC or reset the parent state. Coordinate the shared builtin_command epilogue with B05; each remains a separate acceptance item. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/followup-commands-env.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/followup-serial.log. (Audit docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/REPORT.md L009; triage docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/TRIAGE.md)

title: Use one correct environment-expansion path for prompt and batch input
description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:4887 sends raw interactive input directly to the pipeline dispatcher; batch_expand is called only in run_batch at :4627. os/milton/batch.c:265 deliberately emits an undefined closed variable literally, and test_batch.c:119 currently pins that behavior without an independent period golden. Ground truth: pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch4-batch.tex, Replaceable Parameters, promises %NAME% as the value; ADR-0003 DEC-11 grounds COMMAND compatibility. The exact interactive, unset, unmatched-percent and percent-escape rules need a real DOS 3.3 golden before replacing existing expectations; the report labels these expectations as memory. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Mint a real DOS 3.3 corpus for defined/unset/mixed-case variables, %% escapes, unmatched percent, %0..%9 and interactive FOR %F versus batch %%F. Extend test_batch and a command-entry C host oracle; expand exactly once before pipe/redirection parsing while preserving FOR syntax. Replay advanced-keyboard and BENV.BAT on QEMU. Mutants: bypass interactive expansion or preserve an unset closed variable in batch; compare against the independent corpus, not the same implementation. Scope: Do not blindly reuse batch %% collapsing at the interactive prompt or expand IF/FOR bodies a second time. Reconcile the existing literal-unset host expectation only after independent reference capture. title: Render the foreign-MZ refusal reason on the panic screen before halting
description: Root cause: os/milton/loader.c:1138 loader_panic_foreign_mz writes its name and reason only to COM1 at :1141-1148, then executes cli/hlt at :1152. It never calls the framebuffer panic painter. panic_screen.h:37 only supports numeric exception vectors, so a typed loader-reason path is needed rather than inventing a CPU vector. Ground truth: CLAUDE.md Rule 2 and the explicit deliberate-canon foreign-MZ rule; ADR-0003 DEC-08a.5 requires refusal/panic for untagged 16-bit MZ. The requirement is a visible contextual panic, not execution or return to a shell. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Add a host rendering assertion for a typed foreign-MZ reason, plus a QEMU foreign-MZ leg using T_DOS16.EXE that captures the screen after the serial HALTED marker. Require PC LOAD LETTER and a readable unsupported 16-bit MZ reason; test-panic must still show ERROR 06 for #UD. Mutant: bypass the framebuffer reason call while retaining serial PANIC/HALTED; the screen assertion must fail. Scope: Do not turn the authorized terminal refusal into recovery or add 16-bit execution. This batch is only the missing visible context. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/prog-mz16-result.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/prog-mz16-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/special-fixtures/T_DOS16.EXE; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/prepare_special.py. Clips film_panic/film_scene owed on main (quiet box).

title: Preserve the last completed command template after Ctrl-C
description: Root cause: os/milton/int21.c:1536 gives conin_cooked_line the same buf+2 for output and the saved template. conedit.h:102 overwrites those bytes while typing. The Ctrl-C path at int21.c:1544 skips publishing a new count but does not restore the old bytes; command.c:3632 retains the static AH=0Ah block, so F3 reuses cancelled text with the previous count. Ground truth: pubs/manuals/initechdos-users-guide/ch8-keys.tex:25-33 says completed Enter commits the template and Ctrl-C discards the unfinished line. MS-DOS 3.3 keyboard-template pages are supporting reference; no new historical claim is needed to enforce this shipped promise. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend harness/conkeys/test_conkeys.c plus the INT21 AH=0Ah wrapper tests: a completed template, a cancelled replacement that is shorter/equal/longer, then F1/F3; include empty input, Escape, Insert and F5 controls. QEMU resume_driver.py keyboard must recall the preceding completed command, never ECHO CANCELED. Mutant: retain the aliasing/no-rollback path; the recalled-byte assertion must fail. Scope: The pure conedit snapshot alone is insufficient: the loss happens in the persistent caller buffer across two AH=0Ah calls. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/resume-keyboard-cancel-template.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-keyboard-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume_driver.py. (Audit docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/REPORT.md L038; triage docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/TRIAGE.md)

title: Apply DOS hidden and system attribute filtering in handle searches
description: Root cause: os/milton/int21.c:3850 limits the special-attribute mask to volume labels and directories, omitting DIR_ATTR_HIDDEN and DIR_ATTR_SYSTEM. command.c:2734 correctly requests directories (0x10), so the backend still returns hidden/system files into ordinary DIR, /W and wildcard listings. Ground truth: MS-DOS 3.3 User's Guide DIR, Reference printed pp.57-58 / PDF142-143; DOS AH=4Eh attribute-mask contract; spec/dos_structs.h. The audit fixture attributes were independently set with mattrib. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend os/milton/test_int21_wildcard.c and test_dir_disk.c with ordinary, H, S, HS, directory and combined attributes, exact and wildcard searches and multiple requested masks. Compare with a real DOS 3.3 DTA golden and mtools fixture inventory. Replay B001/B003 on QEMU; no H/S names may enter ordinary output. Mutant: omit H/S from the search filter; the enumeration and rendered-name assertions must fail. Scope: Fix the shared AH=4Eh/4Fh mechanism, while retaining intentional hidden-file searches by callers that request the attributes; a DIR-only string filter hides the backend bug. title: Complete FIND file operands, quoted strings, validation and result status
description: Root cause: os/milton/find_program.asm:62 scans past ordinary operand characters and :134 always reads handle 0; file-operand opening was never implemented. At :109 every quote closes a string and :123 overwrites nlen for subsequent quote groups, so doubled quotes can produce an empty final needle. Unknown option letters fall through at :93. The normal exit at :254 always returns 0, even when count is zero; parameter errors return 1 at :263. Ground truth: MS-DOS 3.3 User's Guide, Reference printed pp.72-73 / PDF157-158 (evidence/manual-page-157.txt and manual-page-158.txt), for named files, quoted literal strings and switches. L017's exact malformed-argument status of 2 is auditor memory, not established by those pages; mint actual DOS 3.3 match/no-match/parse-error statuses before changing that branch. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend test-find-filter with one/multiple named files, stdin as a control, doubled quotes, /V /C /N, valid documented Initech /I, invalid switches and batch ERRORLEVEL tests. Compare bytes, headings and exit statuses to a real DOS 3.3 golden (document /I as the Initech extension). QEMU B032 must finish without keyboard EOF and QUOTES.TXT must print only the matching quoted line. Mutants: always read stdin, stop at the first doubled quote, accept /BAD, or always exit 0; each needs a failing assertion. Scope: One filter parser/result pickup. Do not claim modern FIND error codes are a DOS 3.3 golden; preserve the independently established filter behavior. title: Expose the child exit status after COMMAND /C
description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:4713 saves g_errorlevel before the secondary command; run_external at :3609 correctly latches the child result, then builtin_command at :4727 unconditionally restores the old errorlevel and loses it. Ground truth: pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch4-batch.tex:185-186 and MS-DOS 3.3 IF, Reference printed p.147, define ERRORLEVEL from the last program. Capture real DOS 3.3 COMMAND /C exit propagation before locking exact secondary-shell edge cases. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend the secondary-command execution oracle with ERR0.COM/ERR7.COM directly, through /C, through nested /C and with prior nonzero parent status; retain private environment and EXIT isolation. Replay advanced-misc under QEMU and require CHILD-EXIT7 and DIRECT-EXIT7, not CHILD-STATUS-LOST. Mutant: restore the saved parent status after /C; the child-status assertion must fail. Scope: Keep status ownership explicit for a builtin or failed lookup that does not run a program; do not overwrite unrelated parent state. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/advanced-misc-errorlevel-shift.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/advanced-misc-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/more-fixtures/ERR7.COM; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/more-fixtures/ERR0.COM; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/prepare_more.py. title: Resolve qualified executable suffixes and preserve meaningful EXEC failures
description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:1319 makes an explicit path a single candidate and :1336 appends only .COM, omitting .EXE/.BAT. run_external at :3612 discards every nonzero EXEC error and :3616 reports Bad command. For the audited GUI files, loader.c:367 rejects e_minalloc beyond the DOS arena but returns LOADER_ERR_BAD_FORMAT; kmain.c:813 maps that to DOS 0Bh, not a memory-specific result. Header arithmetic independently confirms 123 needs 298240 bytes versus 65168 available, WORD 491472 versus 79792. Ground truth: pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch4-batch.tex:32; ADR-0003 DEC-08a.2/.3 and DEC-11; spec/memory_map.h:276/:382/:389; ADR-0013 AC-3 DEC-AC3-1 defines FLAIR GUI launch separately from DOS EXEC. evidence/recovery-extra-verification.json preserves the original MZ headers. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend os/milton/test_command.c candidate planning with qualified COM/EXE/BAT suffix search and explicit-extension controls. Extend test_mzload.c with the audited header geometry to distinguish insufficient memory from invalid format. QEMU followup must run qualified BATCH2 without .BAT; native 123/WORD may still be refused but must receive the actual memory/launch-context diagnosis. Keep test-flair-app-launch green. Mutants: qualified paths try only COM, or map every existing-file EXEC refusal to Bad command; each must be detected. Scope: Do not expand DOS memory limits, shrink BSS reserves or force FLAIR tenants through the DOS ABI to satisfy L040. It is a diagnostic defect; direct DOS execution of these GUI tenants is not an established contract. No TSR is used, so initech-h4bk is not this failure. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/followup-commands-env.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/followup-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/special-fixtures/BATCH2.BAT; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/resume-app123-qualified.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/resume-appword-qualified.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-app123-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-appword-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/recovery-extra-verification.json. (Audit docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/REPORT.md L008,L040; triage docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/TRIAGE.md)

title: Execute complete batch files or reject an oversized script before execution
description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:4212 caps the shared batch buffer at 4096 bytes; batch_load_file at :4375 silently stops at the cap and returns a normal length at :4396. run_batch at :4614 interprets the prefix as a complete file, so the final commands disappear without an error. Ground truth: pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch4-batch.tex:19-25 promises sequential execution; CLAUDE.md Rule 2 forbids silently incomplete success. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend a C execution/PAL oracle at lengths 4095/4096/4097 and the BIG.BAT length, with split lines, labels and CALL reloads crossing the boundary. QEMU B063 must execute BIG-END then BIG-RETURNED, or reject the whole oversized file visibly before BIG-BEGIN. Mutant: restore silent 4096-byte truncation; the final sentinel or reject-before-side-effects assertion must fail. Scope: A streaming/re-reading interpreter is preferable for full compatibility; an explicit all-or-nothing size refusal is the bounded safety fix. Merely raising the constant leaves the defect at the next boundary. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/suite4-B063-batch-long.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/suite4-B063.txt; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/cases/BIG.BAT; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/cases/B063.BAT; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/suite.py. (Audit docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/REPORT.md L005; triage docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/TRIAGE.md)

title: Transfer batch control on a plain invocation and reserve return for CALL
description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:3595 sends every resolved BAT to run_batch_invoke; :4695 always nests run_batch and :4636 restores the previous frame. The plain invocation has no transfer-control result distinguishing it from BL_CALL at :4581. The shared g_batch_buf also needs explicit ownership when frames transfer or return. Ground truth: MS-DOS 3.3 User's Guide, Reference printed p.142 / PDF227 (evidence/manual-page-227.txt); shipped Reference ch4-batch.tex CALL entry. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Add an execution-level C host oracle for parent -> child -> grandchild with both plain invocation and CALL, including IF/FOR bodies. Replay resume_driver.py batch on QEMU: CHILD=arg appears, SHOULD-NOT-RETURN does not, while CALL runs its post-call sentinel. Mutant: route a plain invocation through CALL-style frame restoration; require the forbidden sentinel to make the oracle red. Scope: Keep this pickup on frame transfer and buffer ownership; the batch termination question is B14. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/resume-batch-flow.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-batch-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-fixtures/CHAIN.BAT; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/cases/CHILD.BAT; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/manual-page-227.txt. (Audit docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/REPORT.md L033; triage docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/TRIAGE.md)

title: Define and render the extended MacRoman text repertoire
description: B17. Root cause: spec/assets/geneva12.h:25 bounds the authored strike to 20h..7Eh and :161 maps every other byte to the same missing-glyph box. os/apps/itext/itext.c:153 draws through that face; the audit extraction proves the original high-bit bytes survive Save. Ground truth: ../system7-decomp/specs/fonts/geneva.md:91 records a real NFNT extending through MacRoman code 217; that Geneva 9 reference establishes the repertoire, not Geneva 12 artwork. PRD 6.4 and CLAUDE.md require clean-room authored glyphs. A matching independent 12-point extended specimen/metrics must be acquired before asserting glyph fidelity. Scope: Lock the supported single-byte encoding and author its non-ASCII display repertoire with measured metrics and honest missing-glyph behavior. Keep on-disk bytes intact. initech-6grv concerns the shared Geneva 9 shape mismatch; it is not this Geneva 12 repertoire gap. Acceptance oracle: Extend font-art/metrics and text-render host oracles against an independent extended-font specimen, then open EIGHT.TXT in an emulator and extract unchanged bytes after Save. A mutant mapping one supported accented code back to missing must fail its pixel oracle. Record a record-flair clip. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-das/shots/078-text-eightbit.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-das/evidence/fixtures/EIGHT.TXT; docs/audits/2026-10-23-das/evidence/extracted-text/comparison.json; docs/audits/2026-10-23-das/evidence/text-serial.log (Audit docs/audits/2026-10-23-das/REPORT.md L015; triage docs/audits/2026-10-23-das/TRIAGE.md)

title: Add Paint picture Open and Save through one verified native format
description: B16. Root cause: os/apps/paint/paint.c:39 declares Open and Save with ITEM/G=0 and :99 has no file dispatch, chooser or codec call. The missing image file workflow is separate from the absent drawing engine. Ground truth: PRD 1.4 supplies Standard File and application services; the specific picture persistence requirement is the auditor stated ordinary paint-program expectation. Choose and lock a period native bitmap format against independent real-software files before implementation; this audit supplies no verified picture-format golden. Scope: After B15 defines retained pixels, implement one bounded independently verified bitmap import/export and shared Standard File Open/Save. Include dirty-close protection and safe failure/cancel preservation through the atomic file layer. Broader format/layer compatibility stays open on the feature. Acceptance oracle: Add host codec tests with independent period files/readback, plus a draw -> Save -> quit -> Open emulator leg with exact pixel comparison and full-disk/invalid-file controls. A dropped row or no-file-write mutant must fail. Require a locked trace and record-flair clip; a private codec round-trip alone is insufficient. title: Build a bounded usable InitechPaint drawing surface
description: B15. Root cause: os/apps/paint/paint.c:102 handles update by filling a white canvas; the only other route at :107 is Quit. There is no image model, tool state or mouse stroke consumer. :34 disables all other menu rows. Ground truth: PRD 6.5 says Paint primarily carries the canonical Photoshop menu; it does not establish full Photoshop parity. PRD 1.4 and the auditor stated paint-program expectation ground this additional feature. CLAUDE.md freezes the menu titles, not a ban on drawing. Scope: First bounded pickup: retained monochrome raster plus pencil/eraser strokes that survive repaint, movement and resize; expose actual tool selection. Fill, selection, patterns and layers remain explicit later slices on the feature. Keep the canonical menu titles and do not enable nonexistent actions. Acceptance oracle: Add a host raster/stroke oracle with independently specified boundary pixels, clipping and erase expectations; lock an emulator draw -> obscure/reveal -> resize trace and grade the retained picture. A drop-stroke or clear-on-update mutant must fail. Record a record-flair clip. title: Add cancellation to the real modal FILE COPY operation
description: B14. Root cause: os/milton/kmain.c:5282 absorbs every event in the real copy loop and never checks Cancel/Escape. os/flair/dialog.c:1101 builds only two display items with no cancel item at :1103. No cancellation route is implemented. Ground truth: PRD 6.5 / Appendix B defines the paced real FILE COPY operation; spec/toolbox_gate.h Sec 12 defines completion. A Cancel affordance is the auditor stated long-operation usability expectation, not evidence that the staged film prop writes files. Scope: Add a visible cancel control and Escape handling with one explicit cancelled completion. Coordinate atomic staging with initech-mcep and destination/persistence semantics with initech-qxft so cancellation preserves the old destination and discards only incomplete temporary output. Preserve the configured progress rate. Acceptance oracle: Extend test_calc_file_copy host tests for cancellation before open, mid-copy and near completion; replay apps at a slow rate on copied media and compare old destination/source bytes with mtools. An ignored-cancel mutant must fail promptly and unchanged-disk assertions must hold. Add a record-flair clip. title: Connect Calculator Copy and Paste to the shared Scrap
description: B13. Root cause: os/apps/calcda/calcda.c:48 disables all Edit rows, including Copy/Paste at :52; :109 handles only File Close. No result-to-Scrap or Scrap-to-number path exists although the shared Scrap gate is implemented. Ground truth: Macintosh System Software Users Guide V6.0 printed p.127 / PDF p.147 explicitly supports copying results and pasting numbers; evidence/references/mac-calc-147.png is the independent page. spec/calcda/calcda_vectors.tsv governs existing arithmetic. Scope: Enable result Copy and validated numeric Paste through the existing text Scrap. Preserve calculator state on invalid/empty clipboard data and define accepted numeric syntax from a real-Mac fixture. Coordinate B01 input isolation; arithmetic must keep its existing semantics. Acceptance oracle: Extend test-calcda and the tenant route mock with exact Scrap strings and independent numeric paste vectors. Lock Calculator Copy -> close -> Text Paste and Text Copy -> close -> Calculator Paste emulator legs. A drop-Copy/ignore-Paste mutant must fail; record a record-flair clip. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-das/shots/024-calc-edit-settled.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-das/evidence/references/mac-calc-147.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-das/evidence/main-serial.log (Audit docs/audits/2026-10-23-das/REPORT.md L021; triage docs/audits/2026-10-23-das/TRIAGE.md)

The Mac guide p.127 confirms Copy/Paste on the Calculator but not the accepted numeric paste syntax, invalid/empty input, or pending-operation behaviour; the audit TRIAGE said real-Mac vectors are needed and the corpus has none (mint-results-007 absent). title: Provide bounded Undo for destructive InitechText edits
description: B12. Root cause: os/apps/itext/itext.c:103 permanently disables Undo; the edit dispatch at :485 has no E_UNDO case and replace_sel at :412 retains no inverse edit. This is a never-built Undo entry point, not an enabled command that lost its history. Ground truth: Independent Mac OS 8 evidence/references/s8_simpletext_editmenu.png shows Undo; the local TextEdit selection contract supplies offsets. Capture the period one-level edit/undo behavior before choosing coalescing or redo semantics. Scope: First pickup: bounded one-level recovery of Cut/Clear/Paste/typing, including selection and dirty state, with no-op behavior when nothing is undoable. Reset history safely for New/Open. Reuse the document engine rather than a private second editor. Acceptance oracle: Extend test-itext-route with exact before/after bytes for Cut -> Undo, paste replacement and capacity rejection. Replay main and verify both visible restored text and saved bytes. A no-snapshot/no-undo mutant must fail. Record a record-flair clip; do not claim unimplemented multi-level history. title: Add anchored Shift-arrow selection to the shared text applications
description: B11. Root cause: os/apps/itext/itext.c:444 sends arrow tokens without Shift state; os/apps/notepad/notepad.c:403 does the same. os/flair/textedit.c:351 has only collapse/move semantics and :377 sets both selection ends to the same offset. Shift-click selection already exists, but keyboard extension does not. Ground truth: ../system7-decomp/specs/toolbox/textedit.md Sec 2 defines half-open selection and active endpoint state. Shift-arrow itself is the auditor stated period-editing expectation; capture its exact boundary/reversal rules independently rather than claiming the generic TEKey spec proves them. Scope: Add an anchor/moving-end keyboard adapter shared by Text and Note Pad. Support left/right/up/down extension, reversal, collapse without Shift and document/wrapped-line boundaries while preserving text. Acceptance oracle: Extend test-textedit/test-itext-route/test-notepad-route with independently specified selections and keyboard sequences; replay the three-line Shift-Left case in both apps. A mutant dropping Shift or moving the anchor must fail. Add a locked emulator trace and record-flair clip. title: Give Standard File filename fields caret and selection editing
description: B10. Root cause: os/milton/kmain.c:4975 draws only an end caret; :5092 handles end Backspace and :5093 appends printable bytes without checking command modifiers. :5192 copies the default name without selection state. The filename field has no caret/range model. Ground truth: The independent Mac OS 8 save-dialog capture evidence/references/s8_sf_saveas_default.png shows the selected default name; ../system7-decomp/specs/toolbox/textedit.md Sec 2 supplies the range model. Home/End key details are the audit usability expectation and need a captured contract before claiming native parity. Scope: Use the shared edit model for selection, cursor movement, replacement and deletion; initially select the supplied default name. Ctrl-A must select rather than append A. Keep filename validation feedback on initech-oobx (L017), and retain DOS 8.3 policy. Acceptance oracle: Extend Standard File host UI routing tests and test-stdfile, then lock new-name typing, Ctrl-A, Home/End, Shift selection and replacement cancellation in an emulator Save As trace. title: Make Scrapbook capacity notices fit the alert contract
description: B09. Root cause: os/apps/notepad/notepad.c:299 passes a 49-byte single line to notice, which ignores tbx_alert failure at :128. spec/toolbox_gate.h:689 allows only 47 bytes plus NUL per line and :690 caps it at 285 Chicago pixels. os/flair/tbxgate.c:882 rejects its byte length; its measured advance is also 296 pixels, so simply increasing byte capacity would not fix it. Ground truth: spec/notepad/store.h locks the 32-clip capacity; spec/toolbox_gate.h Sec 11 locks alert limits. The ordinary capacity-feedback contract is the auditor stated usability basis, not a claim of changed clip limits. Scope: Split/shorten the full and too-large notices into valid lines, check the alert result, and give an actionable visible message without modifying any clip. Audit the nearby TEXT-only notice against the same constraints. Keep the strict gate validator. Acceptance oracle: Extend test-scrapbook-route with the real alert byte/width validator rather than a success-only alert mock. Replay scrapcapacity at 32/33 and an oversized-clip control; independently decode SCRAPBK.DAT and compare unchanged records. A proposed DA_MUT_OVERLONG_NOTICE mutant restoring the overlong line must fail. Record a record-flair clip. title: Show the actual film startup failure on the panic screen
description: B08. Root cause: os/milton/kmain.c:7084 sends missing-volume, missing-APPS and any CALC load failure to flair_desktop_oom at :7086. That sink prints only FLAIR heap exhausted on screen at :921, including when no allocation failed. harness/film_scene.mk:14 supplies the data image to the accepted scene leg. Ground truth: CLAUDE.md Rule 2 permits a contextual panic for an invariant failure. evidence/film-serial.log reports FAT mount failure before the launch panic; shots/180-film-rest.png visibly misidentifies it as heap exhaustion. The audit request that absent required media never panic is not the project policy. Scope: Preserve the halt policy but carry the mount/load status and a short accurate visible reason identifying the missing required data disk or CALC asset. Distinguish allocation failures. State the two-image requirement in the launch instructions; a new single-disk packaging promise is not implied by this defect. Acceptance oracle: Add a host failure-to-message mapping test and emulator no-data/missing-APPS/missing-CALC controls alongside the normal attached-data scene leg. The screen must show the real cause and the normal control must boot. A mutant routing all statuses to OOM must fail the pixel/text check. Record the GUI/panic acceptance clip. title: Keep the film ledger total within its reachable content area
description: B07. Root cause: os/flair/film_scene.h:12 shrinks the ledger frame to 300x220. os/apps/calc/calc.c:74 still paints a 353x252 body and :92 draws the total at local (204,194); the smaller document content bottom clips it. The app has no scroll extent setup or update-time geometry adaptation. Ground truth: PRD 6.5 and Appendix A require the live ledger and its total; the audit reference film-preview.webp shows that total. The existing authored rest-state geometry contradicts its own implemented content, independently of the missing expense-table fidelity work. Scope: Derive layout/scroll bounds from the current content rectangle or set a minimum fitting film size. Make the total reachable in the supplied rest state and after user shrink/grow. Keep its amount, 570- and the 116% chart unchanged. Coordinate visual layout with initech-c7u1. Acceptance oracle: Extend test-film-scene/test_calc_tenant.c with content-bounds assertions; extend test-flair-live-scene to dismiss the modal, move the chart aside and inspect the total before and after resize. title: Activate an already-running accessory and report slot capacity clearly
description: B06. Root cause: os/flair/tbxgate.c:1404 refuses every occupied-slot launch before comparing the requested identity with g_slot.file. os/milton/kmain.c:3132 maps all negative launch results to FINDER_WIN_ERR_LAUNCH, so same-accessory activation and a different-app capacity refusal become the same generic error. Ground truth: Macintosh System Software Users Guide V6.0 printed p.125 (evidence/references/mac-guide.txt:5664) explicitly says choosing the accessory again activates its window. Scope: Compare full installed application identity and activate the existing tenant for the same accessory without reinitializing it. Explain the current slot limit for a different app. Additional co-resident slots remain on initech-smp0/initech-62hy; this batch does not refile that architecture feature. Acceptance oracle: Add host launch/activation tests for same executable, same basename in different directories and different app. Replay dalife and Finder/Apple repeated launches; edited Note Pad bytes and page must survive with no reentry. A mutant restoring unconditional busy must fail. Record a record-flair clip. title: Redraw both menu bars after applying desktop preferences
description: B05. Root cause: os/flair/cp_service.h:53 marks pattern/clock changes dirty. os/milton/kmain.c:7397 responds with desktop_paint_all and content repaint but draws only MenuClock at :7403. The required complete menu-bar passes exist in os/flair/shell.c:369, including the system bar at :378. Ground truth: PRD 6.3 and CLAUDE.md Law 4 require working menus and the deliberate stacked bars. shell.c:369 defines their compositor order; the intentional second bar is not the defect. Scope: Use the normal composition path to repaint both installed bars and the clock after a preference redraw, preserving current foreground menus, modal layering and cursor save-under. Apply the same rule to temporary Sound preview if it triggers dirty redraw. Grade complete bar strips against independent pre-change captures under a locked clock. Omitting the system-bar repaint must make a mutant red. Record a record-flair clip. title: Let Calculator participate in shutdown and explain a refused quit
description: B04. Root cause: os/apps/calcda/calcda.c:43 installs only Close W and :110 handles only that menu word. os/flair/tbxgate.c:1550 searches for a literal enabled Quit item, returns -1 at :1557, and os/milton/kmain.c:5720 explains cannot-ask only to serial before silently cancelling. Ground truth: The Macintosh guide printed p.125 documents Close as an accessory lifecycle route. spec/toolbox_gate.h Sec 11 and kmain.c:5695 cite cancellable shutdown. This is Calculator integration, not the separate initech-cqej missing declining-app/Bochs acceptance work. Scope: Provide an explicit quit/close-request contract for a documentless accessory and wire Calculator to it; retain Close W. Any genuinely unaskable/declining app must leave the desktop usable with a visible reason. Do not kill document tenants as a generic fallback. Acceptance oracle: Extend test-calcda routing and shutdown host tests; lock Calculator -> Finder -> Shut Down and Restart emulator legs, plus a dirty Text cancel control. A Close-only/unaskable mutant must fail the Calculator leg. Coordinate Bochs coverage with initech-cqej and record a record-flair clip. close_reason: Merged 6e11b5df (lane cx-calcda, Codex gpt-6.1-sol, reviewed + one fix round): Calculator answers the shutdown quit query with an explicit Quit route; a refused quit shows a modal notice naming the app (The operation was cancelled.); calcda/power/shutdown/restart families + mutants + headroom green on main. title: Commit ledger Return input and display file-copy failures
description: B03. Root cause: os/apps/calc/calc.c:186 commits only CR although the event path delivers LF (the paired handling is documented at os/apps/itext/itext.c:454). calc.c:172 drops the immediate tbx_file_copy result and :175 drops every TBX_EVT_FILECOPY completion. os/milton/kmain.c:5258 returns rate/open errors through that event. Ground truth: PRD 6.5 promises an editable grid; spec/toolbox_gate.h Sec 12 defines FILECOPY error/completion delivery. Commit-on-Return and visible Save failure are ordinary document contracts, rather than measured Lotus UI claims. Scope: Accept both cooked Return encodings. Display a bounded, gate-valid explanation for immediate and asynchronous copy errors, identifying missing input/configuration where known and retaining pending entry/state. Keep document persistence and replacement confirmation on initech-qxft. Acceptance oracle: Extend harness/proptest/test_calc_tenant.c/test_calc_file_copy.c with CR/LF and immediate/completion refusal cases. title: Use current text-window geometry and repaint every scroll change
description: B02. Root cause: os/apps/itext/itext.c:74 fixes CONT_W/CONT_H/WRAP_W and :501 initializes wrapping once; :521 handles updates without adopting resized content geometry. show_caret changes g_scroll at :227 before capturing was at :235, so a successful bar round-trip hides that movement and leaves g_full false. paint skips earlier rows at :186. Ground truth: ../system7-decomp/specs/toolbox/textedit.md Sec 4 defines wrapping by destRect and clipping/scrolling by viewRect. The audit LINES25 and WRAP fixtures independently expose stale pixels and unreachable text. Scope: Share actual content width/height among wrapping, drawing, hit testing, scroll extent and caret following. Capture the pre-change scroll offset and fully repaint whenever it changes. Preserve text bytes and selection across resize; a horizontal route is acceptable only if it actually exposes all text. Acceptance oracle: Extend test-itext-route/test-textedit with shrink/grow, coordinate and line-visibility assertions. Extend test-flair-itext-scroll with the LINES25 typing sequence and compare the immediate framebuffer with a forced full repaint. Proposed ITEXT_MUT_FIXED_GEOMETRY and ITEXT_MUT_SCROLL_PARTIAL mutants must fail the geometry and immediate-repaint checks respectively. Require a locked trace and record-flair clip. title: Add executable launching to Finder File Open and Ctrl-O
description: Source @3e44338f53906c23e54fc747a3d689a5d7e0ee2a: os/flair/finder_windows.c:2088-2095 marks only selected folders openable and :1865-1883 opens only folders; os/milton/kmain.c:6305-6307 therefore finds Open disabled for an executable-only selection. The real application launch branch exists at kmain.c:3982-3984 through flair_live_launch_app at :3127-3132 but has no menu/keyboard command adapter. F: this entry point was never built despite working double-click launch. Connect executable Open through the shared command spine and existing launch/lifecycle/error path; enabling the row alone is insufficient. Ground truth: PRD 1.4/6.5; ADR-0013; docs/design/GUI-remediation-R3-finder-design.md F4.4 command spine; ../system7-decomp/specs/toolbox/menu-manager.md; audit REPORT.md L004's authored command/double-click consistency requirement and successful CTENANT control. Acceptance: extend test-finder-menu/test-finder-windows and command adapter coverage for app enablement, folders, mixed selections and unsupported documents; extend test-flair-app-launch with separate File Open, Ctrl-O and double-click CTENANT.EXE legs proving exactly one registration/foreground change, usable Quit/return and visible second-resident-slot refusal. description: Root: os/iword/app/face_a.c:1986 routes End to navigation regardless of Control; :2107-2110 has no Ctrl-End/Ctrl-PgDn deletion or page confirmation state. Ground truth: WP Reference Delete p. 116: Ctrl-End deletion and Ctrl-PgDn then Y, independently checked against the original manual before locking edge transcripts. title: IWORD: share word boundaries for Ctrl-arrow movement and Delete Word
description: Root: os/iword/app/face_a.c:1984-1985 ignores modifiers in cursor_key; :2108 always invokes ED_DELETE for Delete, with no word-operation route. Ground truth: WP Reference pp. 104 (Word Right) and 116 (Ctrl-Del); ref-c.tex cursor limits and ref-d.tex:57-59 admit the reduced routes. Scope: Implement modifier-aware word movement/deletion over complete document units. Establish punctuation, whitespace, attributes and hard-return boundaries from real WP, then share the boundary walker and existing undo machinery. Acceptance oracle (required, not run): Host table-driven real-WP boundary corpus plus test-iword-face exact modifier events; emulator one two three and coded-word controls must move/delete whole words and undo accurately. Mutant: use one-unit movement/deletion. Record clip. Evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-iword/shots/s01-ctrl-right.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-iword/shots/s03-delete-word.png. description: Root: os/iword/app/face_a.c:1952-1989 has no PgUp/PgDn or Ctrl-Home dispatch; :2108-2116 falls back to ordinary cursor/typing and never enters a Go To mode. Scope: Use the document page model to reach next/previous page and parse Ctrl-Home page numbers. No navigation prefix or its digits may enter document text; cancellation preserves cursor/document. Coordinate soft-page support with B10. Acceptance oracle (required, not run): Extend test-iword-face/core with hard/soft/mixed pages, first/last boundaries, invalid page and Go To cancel. Emulator long-document trace must assert page/cursor and unchanged saved bytes. Mutants: ignore PgDn or route Go To digits to typing. Record clip. description: Root: os/iword/core/piece.c:299 recognizes only C1/02 as positioned content; C1/E0 and C1/60 fall back to zero-width IW_U_CODE. os/iword/core/edit.c:388-421 handles paragraph Justification only. spec/iword/fkeys.h:47/:61 gray the two insertion commands. Ground truth: ../wordperfect51-decomp/goldens/minted/MINT01.shots/02_typed.png and MINT03.shots/02_typed.png; spec/iword/wp5_format.h and codes.c:343-344 identify the inline codes. ref-c.tex:118-124 acknowledges left-margin fallback. Scope: Share the inline alignment layout model between imports and Shift-F6/Alt-F6 insertion, including end-of-alignment 0x83, wrapping, cursor and Reveal. Preserve the existing separate Format Justification implementation. Acceptance oracle (required, not run): Extend test-iword-face/codes/WP5 differential against real MINT01/03 positions and newly minted command traces; verify display coordinates and round-trip bytes.
