title: IWORD: support the verified soft-page code variants in real multipage WP5 files
description: Root: os/iword/core/piece.c:245-258 admits neither 0x8C nor 0x0B as a single unit; os/iword/fs/wp5.c:54-56 rejects the file. Read-only byte inspection finds MINT39 first rejected at 0x23E (0x8C), MINT44 at 0x2BB (0x0B). Ground truth: ../wordperfect51-decomp/mint/wpMINT39.steps and wpMINT44.steps, their real saved files/captures, and the audit independent decoder. Existing locked single-code data predates these mints. Scope: Add independently verified HRt-SPg and SRt-SPg semantics to unit scanning, paging, display, editing and serialization. Record the locked-spec update. Keep refusal for unknown/malformed codes. initech-tu3d covers prefix packets/D4 research, not the missing single-byte dispatch. Acceptance oracle (required, not run): Extend test-iword-core and test-iword-wp5-roundtrip with MINT39/44 and mutation-proven soft-page type/round-trip checks. Emulator must retrieve, navigate pages, Save and reopen in real WP with text/paragraphs preserved. Mutant: reject or flatten one soft-page variant. Record clip. title: IWORD: consume the selected entry and status measurement units
description: Root: os/iword/app/face_a.c:1172-1185 stores unit bytes 4/5, but status :733/:745, format :926 and parse_inches :1849 always use inches; no unit consumer exists outside the Setup labels. Ground truth: spec/iword/settings.h:5-8 defines independent entry/status unit preferences; WP Reference Units of Measure pp. 698-700; ref-s.tex:360-362 documents the incomplete consumers. Scope: Implement both preference consumers with explicit units and round-trip conversion for i/c/p/w/u. Keep canonical stored WP coordinates in WPU and settings bytes unchanged; do not merely rename inch values. Acceptance oracle (required, not run): Extend test_iword_p3_part2.c and test-iword-face with independent rational conversion fixtures and differing entry/status settings; emulator save/relaunch, margins and Pos/Ln must use the chosen units. Mutant: force inches at one consumer. Record clip. Evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-iword/shots/s01-units-cm.png. title: IWORD: distinguish zero margins from invalid numeric input
description: Root: os/iword/app/face_a.c:1849-1863 returns zero for both valid 0 and invalid input; :1924 updates the margin only when v is nonzero. os/iword/core/edit.c:1271 permits zero with valid remaining width. Ground truth: pubs/manuals/initechword-reference/ref-m.tex:64-66 accepts readable margins below 9 inches; the core range contract accepts zero. Scope: Return parse success separately from the value. Apply zero when valid; keep blank/default/cancel separate and visibly refuse values that violate paper width. Preserve existing document/cursor on refusal. Acceptance oracle (required, not run): test-iword-face plus core tests for 0, 0.00, blank, malformed, valid fractions and impossible left+right combinations; decode D0/01 values independently after emulator Save. Mutant: use if(v). Record format trace/clip. Evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-iword/shots/s01-zero-margins.png. (Audit docs/audits/2026-10-23-iword/REPORT.md L061; triage docs/audits/2026-10-23-iword/TRIAGE.md)

title: IWORD Search: translate Ctrl-M from the actual FLAIR key event
description: Root: os/flair/event.c:539-547 supplies printable m plus Control; os/iword/app/face_a.c:2311 accepts printable text before :2313 tests ch==13 for Ctrl-M, so that existing SRt branch is unreachable for the real chord. Ground truth: WP Reference printed p. 573 (PDF p. 591), independently re-extracted: Ctrl-m includes SRt. The audit evidence/references/wp-search.txt excerpt is from earlier pages and does not contain this instruction. Scope: Recognize the Control modifier plus M virtual/character key before printable query insertion; insert one 0x0D search token. Keep Ctrl-Enter hard-page and ordinary Enter hard-return behavior distinct. Acceptance oracle (required, not run): Extend test_iword_p3.c/search tests using the exact 0x326D+Control event, then replay target Ctrl-M search across a wrapped line in both directions. description: Root: os/iword/app/face_a.c:1502-1517 omits F1 and Next/Prev handlers and gates motion on g_look_wp; :1614 resets plain-text rendering to byte zero every paint. Ground truth: pubs/manuals/initechword-reference/ref-c.tex:12-15 (Cancel), WP Reference Look printed p. 363/PDF pp. 381-384, and spec/iword/listfiles.h:137 (Look menu). Scope: Use one read-only Look viewport with WP/text scroll state and real Next/Prev document selection. F1 must cancel without editing the active document. Keep directory selection and current unsaved document intact; define missing/read-error and end-of-list behavior from a real WP mint. Acceptance oracle (required, not run): Extend harness/proptest/test_iword_face.c and test_iword_listfiles.c with 80-line text, WP files, F1/Esc/F7/Space and Next/Prev boundaries. Emulator must reach text line 080 and another named file, then restore the unchanged editing document. Mutants: force text offset zero, omit F1, ignore Next. Record clip. title: Toolbox/IWORD: detect or eliminate silent directory enumeration truncation
description: Root: os/iword/app/face_a.c:1369 and :1412 request only 256 records. os/flair/tbxgate.c:1078-1092 keeps walking but stops copying/counting at capacity and returns success; os/iword/core/listfiles.c:143 then removes dot entries, leaving 254 files. Ground truth: pubs/manuals/initechword-reference/ref-l.tex:73-99 promises file listing/count/used size; prepare_stress.py and stress-before-directory.txt independently establish 270 files and 92340 bytes. Scope: Make overflow explicit in the gate contract and app, with continuation/paging or an honest visible partial-list warning. Do not fix this by only increasing LF_MAX: root directories, subdirectories and counts must have a defined capacity contract. Acceptance oracle (required, not run): Add gate and test_iword_listfiles.c cases for 254/255/256/270+ files, dot entries and subdirectories. Emulator must reach F269 or visibly disclose the limit and partial totals; compare against mdir. Mutant: suppress overflow/continuation. Lock the trace and record-flair clip. description: Root: os/flair/tbxgate.c:1550 recognizes only an enabled item literally named Quit; os/iword/app/face_a.c:244 names it Exit. os/milton/kmain.c:5715-5723 cancels on -1 with serial-only cannot-ask. Ground truth: Inside Macintosh VI Quit Application semantics cited at os/milton/kmain.c:5691-5705; Word request_exit at os/iword/app/face_a.c:1703-1707 is the existing save guard. Scope: Represent the quit action independently of its localized/period label and bring Word forward for a usable save/cancel interaction. Preserve dirty text on refusal and visibly explain a tenant that cannot answer. initech-cqej covers decline/Bochs test debt, not this Exit-versus-Quit dispatch defect. Acceptance oracle (required, not run): Extend the Toolbox quit-route host oracle with Exit, Quit, absent and disabled actions. Drive Word dirty/clean/save/no/cancel/failed-save through Finder Restart and Shut Down; require responsive prompts, preserved bytes on cancel and QEMU/Bochs agreement. Mutant: require literal Quit. description: Root: os/iword/app/face_a.c:1172-1185 persists setting byte 6, but write_file at :1236-1263 never consumes it; :1045 only displays it. description: dBASE III PLUS RUN/! executes a DOS command from inside the interpreter. The real-III+ golden (xbase_prog_diff mint, case run) exists and the host/emu legs are written (test-samir-dml-run), but InitechDOS's loader refuses a nested EXEC while a program is resident (loader.c:1193 LOADER_ERR_BUSY) and the PAL has no EXEC seam. title: Easter egg: the Jump to Conclusions Mat (Tom Smykowski's invention) -- hidden in InitechOS, discoverable but never advertised
description: Operator directive 2026-10-17: 'jump to conclusions has to be an easter egg.' Canon: Tom Smykowski's 'Jump to Conclusions Mat' from Office Space -- a mat you put on the floor with different CONCLUSIONS written on it that you could JUMP TO ('That is the worst idea I've ever heard in my life, Tom.'). Design the egg so it reads as a period in-joke, not a 2026 wink: (a) FLAIR: a hidden trigger -- e.g. Command-click (or a specific click count) on the About This Computer version string opens 'Jump to Conclusions', a small modeless window drawing a mat (a grid of pads in the canon palette, Chicago 12 labels) with conclusions on it; clicking a pad 'jumps' the hourglass cursor to it and shows the conclusion in a Platinum alert (conclusions authored in the film's voice and the house's; keep strange capitalisation per the manuals directive); (b) InitechDOS: an undocumented COMMAND.COM internal -- JUMP with no args prints TO WHAT?; JUMP CONCLUSIONS prints the mat as a text-mode grid and lets the arrow keys hop; JUMP must never alter the TPSREP ritual; (c) SAMIR: a hidden function or SET option is OPTIONAL and must not break the real-dBASE differential (an extra, never a change). Oracles: host suite for the mat layout + conclusion table (locked spec/easter/jump_to_conclusions.json: pad grid, labels, the trigger), an emu gate driven by a locked trace that performs the trigger and grades the mat window pixel-exact (mutants: trigger off by one click, mat missing a pad), DOS leg screendump-graded, a Rule 14 clip jump_to_conclusions. Constraints: no mention in any manual index or command inventory (the manuals' command gates must EXEMPT the hidden verb explicitly, like the house slips); the kernel headroom budget; ASCII-only. Check the other canon eggs already present (116% pie, 570- trailing minus, hourglass cursor, PC LOAD LETTER, the Michael Bolton config) for a consistent trigger style; record the trigger in docs/EASTER-EGGS.md (operator-only doc, not shipped).
notes: 2026-10-20: part (a) FLAIR mat MERGED on main (Option-click the Apple icon 3x; spec/easter/jump_to_conclusions.json; test-egg-jtc, test-flair-egg-jtc + mutants; clip jump_to_conclusions repro-proven; docs/EASTER-EGGS.md). Parts (b) DOS JUMP verb and (c) optional SAMIR option remain.

title: [bug] test_keep is address-dependent: g_arena_seg_base truncates the MAP_32BIT mmap address to 16 bits -- rare ASLR-draw RED (B1/B3/B4)
description: Observed 2026-08-24: test-keep went RED inside a full make test (4 failures: B1 resident-owner, B3 ALLOC-above + still-resident, B4 survives-reclaim) then GREEN standalone and 0/90 repeated runs (incl. big-env). Root-cause hypothesis (test_keep.c:319): g_arena_seg_base = (uint16_t)((mmap_addr >> 4) & 0xFFFF) -- a MAP_32BIT address >>4 is up to ~26 bits, truncated to 16, so the arena segment is effectively a random 16-bit value per run; placements near the 0xFFFF wrap (~0.02% of draws) break the B3 'got > seg_base+16' compare and the seg_owner lookups. Fix: derive test segments from an arena-relative base (e.g. force seg_base = a fixed constant by passing paragraphs relative to the arena, or assert/skip when (addr>>4) > 0xFFF0 window), never from truncated host addresses. NOT caused by the GUI lanes (none touch mcb/int21/test_keep; failure reproduced-in-principle from address math alone). Until fixed this gate is a rare coin -- a lone test-keep RED in a vector should be re-run standalone before blaming the diff (Rule 4), and this bead is the citation.

title: tenants scene: flair_live_do_menu's cross-menu restore path calls shell_render, which repaints tenant windows as CHROME-ONLY (WDEF white) and never routes content -- a band-1 cross-menu drag wipes both tenants' content

In the FLAIR_LIVE_TENANTS scene that call walks the LIVE WindowMgr z-order, so it repaints the TENANT windows' WDEF chrome with blank white content (the canon doc windows are hidden), erasing fill/accent/marker; the menu path seeds no damage and runs no route, so the wipe persists until some later dispatch happens to damage the windows. Reachable: band-1 (bar_sys) press + cross-title drag on the booted tenants image. The 9op1 crossdrag gate grades the NON-tenant flairlive image, so it cannot see this. FIX SHAPE (fits the DQ2 contract): after a cross-menu-switch shell_render in a tenants scene, close the cycle -- desktop_validate_all + re-seed both tenants' content (WindowMgr_invalidate contRgn) + flair_route_updates + present; or better, stop using the whole-scene restore in the tenants pump and erase the panel via invalidate(panel rect) -> paint_damage -> route (the b3hl close path). Belongs to the Wave B menu lane (t1rv/7tjp/b3hl -- band-2 dispatch will rework this whole path anyway; rule DQ7/DQ8 there).

title: updateRgn-within-visible is an unstated load-bearing invariant: tenant updateEvt paint clips to contRgn+updateRgn only, so any stale seed surviving a z-order change lets a BACKGROUND tenant stomp the FOREGROUND's pixels
description: Found 2026-07-31 during the Wave A gofc/rqz5 landing (first-person, no delegation). MECHANISM: ref_tenant.c's updateEvt handler (and the ADR-0013 tenant contract generally) paints clipped to contRgn INTERSECT updateRgn, NEVER to the window's CURRENT visible region -- it trusts updateRgn subset-of visible(w) as an invariant. That invariant is maintained only OPERATIONALLY: WindowMgr_invalidate SECTs seeds with visible-at-seed-time, and the DQ2 pump order guarantees no z-order change intervenes between seed and route within one dispatch. But NOTHING re-clips PENDING damage when occlusion changes: any sequence of WM ops without a route/validate boundary (two NewWindows in a row at the tenants launch site was the live instance -- NOTES's brief-front full-struct activation seed survived HELLO launching on top of it) leaves stale damage that the route then delivers, and the tenant paints pixels it no longer owns (background stomps foreground). Caught live: test-flair-appswitch TIER-A went RED (overlap #C0C0C0 NOTES_FILL where #FFFFFF HELLO_FILL belongs) the moment desktop_paint_damage stopped blanket-validating. FIXED NARROWLY at the launch site (desktop_validate_all after the from-scratch shell_render, kmain.c step 4b) -- but the CLASS remains: any future multi-WM-op sequence without a cycle boundary re-opens it. PROPER FIX (BeginUpdate fidelity, IM I): flair_route_updates should clip the damage to the window's CURRENT visible region at delivery time (updateRgn INTERSECT ComputeVisible(w)) before synthesizing the updateEvt -- the exact semantics of BeginUpdate's visRgn INTERSECT updateRgn port setup. Needs a scratch-region discipline decision in process.c (ComputeVisible requires a caller scratch distinct from the manager's internals; route has no scratch param today). Alternative: a window.c verb that re-clips pending damage on every covering op (NewWindow/SelectWindow/ShowWindow) -- more invasive, keeps the invariant globally true. Oracle for whichever lands: a host test that seeds a background window with damage overlapping the front window (simulating the stale case), routes, and asserts the front window's pixels survive; mutant = drop the clip.
notes: R1.4 lane: RED-first three-window stale-seed case failed old route at test_process_update.c overlap; delivery now clips updateRgn INTERSECT current visRgn with Rule-2 subset assertion. Host 18 checks green; UPDATE_NO_VISCLIP red via BACK stomp. Emu intentionally not run per lane brief.

title: kernel low-memory runway: kernel_shell _kernel_end was within ~10KiB of PROGRAM_BASE (0x40000) BEFORE 44ab -- conventional gap nearly exhausted, PROGRAM_BASE relocation decision looming
description: Found during initech-44ab integration: kernel_shell.elf (largest variant: COMMAND.COM + full FLAIR) measured _kernel_end=0x42094 with the 44ab statics (+18.4KiB BSS) = 8340 bytes OVER; implies pre-change margin was only ~10KiB. The 44ab resolution moves the region working set to the FLAIR heap in freestanding builds, restoring the margin, but the runway problem is structural: any future kernel growth (~10KiB of code/data/bss) trips the guard again. Options when it does: raise PROGRAM_BASE (spec/memory_map.h locked change, ripples into loader/PSP arena), move more static data to the ext-mem heap, or high-half relocation (the kernel.ld comment anticipates this). Needs an ADR-level decision when next triggered; the ld guard fails loud so there is no silent risk.
notes: 2026-08-24 (GUI remediation, sjvq lane): the window finally BUSTED -- kernel_shell exceeded PROGRAM_BASE 0x40000 when Platinum menu chrome grew menu.o. Root cause was NOT kernel growth per se: kmain_shell.o and the default kmain.o reference ZERO FLAIR symbols (nm-verified), yet both link lists carried the full KERNEL_FLAIR_OBJS Toolbox set as dead weight. Fixed by removing the set from KERNEL_OBJS + KERNEL_SHELL_OBJS (Makefile, commented, link-verified): shell _kernel_end 0x3f9f8+bust -> 0x31660 = ~60KiB runway restored. The RELOCATION decision (5dr8) is deferred again but the FLAIR kernels themselves (flairtenants 0x3d9c0) are now the closest to the window -- they cannot shed the Toolbox. Keep watching flairtenants.

title: region_from_rects does O(n^2) self-union identity-copy; wide accumulations approach the per-row cap and fail-loud
description: [Found during initech-mswo fix, region.c] region_from_rects accumulates via region_op(&acc,&tmp,&tmp,RGN_OP_UNION) (a self-union identity copy) once per rect -- O(n^2), re-running the full band sweep each rect. For a wide multi-span accumulation each intermediate union approaches the per-row inversion cap (RGN_ROW_X_MAX); combined with the mswo fail-loud bound this makes moderately complex from_rects inputs fail-loud where a direct union-accumulate would not. Distinct from the cap-value question (initech-44ab): this is an allocation/algorithm-shape concern. Consider a direct multi-rect union-accumulate that does not round-trip each rect through a full self-union.

title: SGR 8 (conceal) preserves the bright bit — concealed bright-fg text stays visible
description:

EVIDENCE: ansi.c:218 `st->attr=(st->attr&0xF8u)|bg3;`. REPRO: attr=0x0F then ESC[8m → SET_ATTR 0x08 (expected 0x00).

title: ndx_open_impl: zero-byte file returns -NDX_ERR_IO instead of -NDX_ERR_BAD_SIZE, conflating I/O failure with size violation
description:

EVIDENCE: ndx.c:310-313 `fsize_raw=seek(...,END); if (fsize_raw<=0) return -NDX_ERR_IO;`. An empty file: seek succeeds, returns 0; 0<=0 → -NDX_ERR_IO. A 0-byte file is structurally too small (the BAD_SIZE condition two lines later). Only fsize_raw<0 is a genuine I/O error.

title: Heap REUSE walks the entire class free-list instead of head-only — violates documented LIFO spec, strands undersized head blocks permanently
description:

EVIDENCE: heap.h:166-168 documents head-only ('if the free-list HEAD has cap>=request, pop it'), but heap.c:95-111 is a while(blk!=0) walk with a prev pointer that unlinks the first fitting node anywhere; a too-small head is skipped and a deeper block reused, and small head blocks never return to the bump allocator. The oracle (test_flair_heap.c:168-189, Property 2) tests only a single-element free-list, so head-vs-walk divergence is never exercised.

EXPECTED: If freelist[klass]->cap>=need pop head, else fall through to BUMP; a too-small head must not trigger a deeper search.

ACTUAL: Walks all nodes and reuses any fit regardless of position.

REPRO: Alloc HANDLE/128, HANDLE/8; free 8 (head), free 128 -> list [8->128]; flair_alloc(HANDLE,64): spec says bump (head 8<64), code reuses the 128 block. Absent from test_flair_heap.c.

title: flair_alloc has no upper-bound size guard: huge sizes overflow flair_align_up/span arithmetic -> cap=0 or zero-advance block returned non-NULL (heap alias/corruption); the 'overflo
description:
[FLAIR bug-hunt R2 2026-06-28, wf_2f47b15b, adversarially verified] subsystem=FLAIR/heap (os/flair/heap.c).
EVIDENCE: Only guard is heap.c:84-86 (size==0 || !flair_class_ok) — no size<=UINT32_MAX-HDR-(ALIGN-1) check, yet :30-31 comments 'overflow-safe ... passed the request-sanity check below' (no such check). (a) flair_align_up (:32-35) (n+15)&~15: for size in [0xFFFFFFF1,0xFFFFFFFF], n+15 wraps -> need=0, span=16, avail passes, blk->cap=0 (:140), used+=16 — a non-NULL ptr to a cap=0 block for a ~4GB request. (b) span (:122) 16+need: for size in [0xFFFFFFE1,0xFFFFFFF0], need=0xFFFFFFF0, span=0x100000000->0, avail check '0>avail' false -> passes, used+=0 — cursor never advances, so two consecutive allocs both write headers at base+0 and return base+16, aliasing live allocations.

EXPECTED: Return NULL (Rule 2) for any size whose aligned span overflows uint32_t; correct the false comment.

ACTUAL: Non-NULL returns with cap=0 (write-past-block) or zero-advance aliasing (two live allocs share one address; second clobbers first's header).

REPRO: flair_alloc(h,GENERAL,0xFFFFFFE1) twice -> same non-NULL ptr, used stays 0; flair_alloc(h,GENERAL,0xFFFFFFFF) -> non-NULL, stored cap=0 (verified by uint32_t simulation).

title: make_offset_view: unsigned underflow of view->height (dst->height - y_top) with no bounds check — wraps to ~0xFFFFFFFF, base past buffer, defeats surface clip -> OOB framebuffer wr
description:
[FLAIR bug-hunt R2 2026-06-28, wf_2f47b15b, adversarially verified] subsystem=FLAIR/shell (os/flair/shell.c).
EVIDENCE: shell.c:148-153 view->base=dst->base+y_top*dst->pitch; view->height=dst->height-y_top (both uint32_t). shell_render guards only dst->height==0 (:303-307), not dst->height<=SHELL_MENUBAR2_TOP(=20). For 0<height<=20 the subtraction wraps to ~UINT32_MAX and base advances past the allocation; surface_fill_span's clip y>=bm->height (surface.c:35) never fires, so DrawMenuBar writes rows 0..19 through a base already past the framebuffer end. Safe today only because the sole runtime caller passes height=480.

EXPECTED: SHELL_PANIC (Rule 2) when dst->height < SHELL_MENUBARS_H (40) / y_top >= dst->height, before the subtraction.

ACTUAL: Silent uint32_t underflow; OOB write reachable with any small surface.

REPRO: shell_render with a height=10 bitmap -> make_offset_view(y_top=20) yields height=0xFFFFFFF6, base 20 rows past a 10-row buffer; DrawMenuBar writes rows 20..39 past the end.

title: fb_clear 24bpp arm computes pixel count as (lfb_pitch*lfb_height)/3 with stride-3 writes, ignoring per-scanline pitch — scrambled BGR on padded LFBs
description:
[FLAIR bug-hunt R2 2026-06-28, wf_2f47b15b, adversarially verified] subsystem=FLAIR/present (os/milton/kmain.c fb_clear).
EVIDENCE: kmain.c:166 total=lfb_pitch*lfb_height; :190 pixels=total/3u; writes fb[i*3+k]=b/g/r treat the whole buffer as a flat BGR-triple array with no row stride. For a padded 24bpp LFB (pitch>width*3), row 1 starts at byte 'pitch' in the LFB but width*3 in the flat index, so every row after row 0 gets rotated BGR components (seafoam r=0x6F,g=0xA0,b=0x8E -> B=0xA0,G=0x6F on row 1). The 32bpp arm (:183-186, dwords=total>>2) is safe; flair_desktop_present (:788) correctly uses y*pitch + x*bpp.

EXPECTED: Per-row loop honoring lfb_pitch (fb[y*pitch + x*3..+2]), like flair_desktop_present.

ACTUAL: BGR triples placed at flat i*3; rows 1..N show rotated colors for any pitch>width*3.

REPRO: 640x480x24 VBE mode with 4-byte row padding (pitch=1924): row 0 seafoam correct, rows 1..479 wrong. Latent under QEMU/Bochs (tight pitch).

title: Drag/menu guards and WNE deadline use additive tick (g_tick + N) — instant fire when the tick counter is near UINT32_MAX
description:

The main pump correctly uses unsigned subtraction `(flair_tick_count()-start) < FLAIR_LIVE_TICK_BUDGET` (kmain.c:2345).

REPRO: Set g_tick=0xFFFFFF80 before arming the pump; a drag does not move the window (guard fires before any mouse events).

title: PS/2 byte0 sign bits XS (bit4) and YS (bit5) never applied — dx/dy get the wrong sign/magnitude for |delta| > 127
description:
[FLAIR GUI bug-hunt 2026-06-28, wf_4dfb6f55, adversarially verified] subsystem=mouse/input (mouse.c).
EVIDENCE: mouse.c:220-222 reads b0=g_pkt[0] but only extracts b0 & PKT_BTN_MASK (bits 0-2); bits 4 (XS) and 5 (YS), the 9-bit two's-complement sign bits, are never consulted. dx/dy are cast straight: `int8_t dx=(int8_t)g_pkt[1]; int8_t dy=(int8_t)g_pkt[2];`. No XS(0x10)/YS(0x20) define exists. event.c:45-47 assumes the payload is already sign-extended, but the producer never does it. The overflow check (PKT_OVERFLOW=0xC0) only discards |delta|>255, so [128,255] passes with the wrong sign. (Distinct from initech-rgt8 vertical-axis inversion.)

EXPECTED: `int16_t dx = (int16_t)g_pkt[1] - ((b0 & 0x10u) ? 256 : 0);` (and YS for dy).

ACTUAL: byte1=200 -> dx=-56 (cursor jumps left on fast rightward move); XS=1,byte1=100 -> dx=+100 (jumps right on leftward move).

REPRO: Move the PS/2 mouse fast right so byte1>=128 (XS=0); the cursor moves left / wrong magnitude.

title: teardown_common does not zero app->magic before free — double-teardown is undetected and double-pushes blocks onto free-lists (potential cycle/hang)
description:
[FLAIR GUI bug-hunt 2026-06-28, wf_4dfb6f55, adversarially verified] subsystem=process.c (App Contract lifecycle).
EVIDENCE: process.c:354-355 frees block, records_block, then app via flair_free(.., FLAIR_CLASS_HANDLE, app). The free-list next pointer is written at header+8 (heap.h:126-130, heap.c:56-58), which does NOT overlap app->magic at payload offset 0, so app->magic==FLAIR_APP_MAGIC survives the free. A second terminate/kill on the same pointer passes the magic check (process.c:373/403) and double-frees all three blocks. heap.h:195 states the allocator does not detect double-free; the resulting free-list cycle makes flair_alloc's reuse scan (heap.c:96-111) loop forever.

EXPECTED: Zero app->magic before the final flair_free(app) so a second teardown panics at the magic check (Rule 2).

ACTUAL: app->magic survives; a second teardown is undetected, double-frees, and can cycle the free-list, hanging the next allocation.

REPRO: Launch an app, terminate it, terminate the same pointer again; all three frees succeed again; a later flair_alloc(HANDLE,...) hangs if the list now cycles.

title: FlairProcess_terminate/kill have no runtime guard against _register'd apps; teardown frees are silently rejected (contract violation undetected)
description:
[FLAIR GUI bug-hunt 2026-06-28, wf_4dfb6f55, adversarially verified] subsystem=process.c (App Contract lifecycle).
EVIDENCE: process.h:226-227 documents that _register'd apps have app->block==NULL and must NOT be torn down with FlairProcess_terminate, but there is no runtime check in terminate (process.c:368) or kill (process.c:397). Both call teardown_common -> flair_free(.., app->block) (process.c:335, NULL), flair_free(.., app->records_block) (process.c:345, NULL), flair_free(.., app) (process.c:355, caller-owned non-heap). flair_free short-circuits NULL (heap.c:152) and rejects out-of-window payloads (heap.c:155) silently. The magic check (process.c:373/403) cannot distinguish _register from _launch (both FLAIR_APP_MAGIC).

EXPECTED: terminate/kill check app->block==NULL (or an is_registered flag) and panic (Rule 2) or skip the heap frees.

ACTUAL: Terminate/kill on a _register'd app is accepted silently; all three flair_free calls are rejected with no error and no memory freed.

REPRO: Register an app with caller-owned storage; FlairProcess_terminate it; no panic/error, master heap n_free does not increment.

title: flair_route_updates: WindowMgr_validate clears damage unconditionally even when the updateEvt is not delivered
description:
[FLAIR GUI bug-hunt 2026-06-28, wf_4dfb6f55, adversarially verified] subsystem=process.c (App Contract dispatcher).
EVIDENCE: process.c:646-658: the updateEvt is delivered only inside `if (owner->procs && owner->procs->event != ...)`, but WindowMgr_validate(w) at line 658 is OUTSIDE that guard and runs unconditionally. A tenant with NULL procs/event has its updateRgn cleared without the event ever firing, so content is never refreshed and no future repaint is triggered — permanently stale.

EXPECTED: WindowMgr_validate(w) only when the updateEvt was actually delivered (inside the guard).

ACTUAL: Damage is cleared regardless of delivery; a NULL-event-proc tenant is left permanently stale.

REPRO: Register an app with procs->event==NULL; expose it to damage; flair_route_updates clears updateRgn without delivering the event.
notes: 2026-07-21 solidity forensics: the filed process.c:658 instance is the LESSER half. The bigger instance: desktop_paint_damage validates EVERY window's updateRgn unconditionally at desktop.c:269-273 after painting CHROME ONLY, and flair_route_updates is invoked solely inside the foreground-switch block (kmain.c:2406-2413), never on inDrag/inGoAway (kmain.c:1208,1236). Absorbed by root bead initech-gofc (epic initech-av7s); keep this open for the narrow validate-inside-guard cleanup within that fix.
close_reason: SUPERSEDED by the ratified DQ1 contract (WL-0076, epic initech-av7s design field): validation now records 'damage serviced by the pump cycle' (chrome painted + delivery attempted), NOT 'updateEvt delivered' -- flair_route_updates validates EVERY walked window unconditionally, because under the DQ2 pump order the compositor's chrome phase has already serviced unowned/eventless windows (their full paint). The validate-inside-guard ask dissolves; an owned-but-eventless window gets WDEF paint + validate rather than immortal pending damage. Contract documented in process.c/h + desktop.h; graded by test-process-update (WU flips to validated-no-delivery) + its extended SKIP_VALIDATE self-mutant.

title: ADR-0013 tension: app-death survival vs WindowRecords-in-child-arena (Sec 3.4 vs 3.6)
description: ADR-0013 Sec 3.4 claims application DEATH (crash, not clean quit) survives a corrupt child arena because 'WindowRecords are caller-owned records the WindowMgr threads, so removing them from the z-order does not read the dead heap.' But Sec 3.2/3.6 has the tenant allocate its WindowRecords + region pools FROM its child arena -- so the z-order links (w->nextWindow) live in the arena that death corrupts, and DisposeWindow/z-order removal WOULD read the dead heap. Internal tension. Options: (a) WindowMgr keeps a separate window index not reliant on traversing arena-resident nextWindow; (b) tenant WindowRecords live in a shell-owned pool separate from the app DATA arena (split the arena: a shell-owned 'records' region + an app 'data' arena); (c) accept death-survival is best-effort and scope it to data-only corruption. NEEDS a committee ruling + ADR-0013 amendment. Clean teardown (close/DisposeWindow/one-shot-free/promote) + the O-3 leak invariant are UNAFFECTED and land in the first cut (initech-vi5k/xp5t); only the corrupt-arena-DEATH sub-test of O-3 is deferred pending this. Raised during App Contract Wave 3 orchestration.
close_reason: RESOLVED via ADR-0013 Amendment AC-2 (split-arena), committee-ratified + adversarial-verified (wf_00931e9e), commit 3eb39e4. Tenant WindowRecords + region pools now carve from a master-backed records_arena (FLAIR_CLASS_HANDLE) separate from the DATA arena; new FlairProcess_kill death path reads ONLY records-resident structural state, so app death provably survives a corrupt DATA arena. BC-6 now satisfied (was FALSE). O-3 gained the previously-deferred corrupt-arena death sub-test (scribble app->block -> kill -> list/z-order empty, no panic, avail stable); mutants UBD0_MUT_RECORDS_IN_DATA_ARENA (kill reads scribbled arena -> SIGSEGV/RED) + TEARDOWN_MUT_LEAK_RECORDS bite. 287 host + 57 emu + Bochs boot leg GREEN.

title: Harness: deterministic, regenerable GUI-interaction VIDEO capture (frame-stitch record mode + ffmpeg GIF/MP4 + make record-flair + auto-on-failure clip)
description:
GOAL: capture SHORT, REPRODUCIBLE videos of FLAIR GUI interactions for diagnosis -- temporal artifacts (the frozen-then-teleport drag of initech-34gp; the modal erased mid-drag of initech-pipa) are structurally invisible to single screendumps. Scripted/deterministic capture is the priority; output BOTH a lightweight GIF/APNG (embed in beads/worklogs) AND a high-fidelity MP4/WebM; integrate as BOTH an on-demand make target AND opt-in auto-capture on a red emu gate.

DESIGN (deep-research verified core, adversarially fact-checked against QEMU primary docs + the record/replay author's KVM-Forum talk; full report in docs/ or the session transcript):
- QEMU has NO native movie command; `screendump` (one frame; supports format=ppm|png since 7.1) is the only screen primitive -> VIDEO = stitch frames + ONE external encoder (ffmpeg). Keep the dependency footprint to exactly ffmpeg + the existing C QMP harness (Law 3).
- DETERMINISM (Rule 11): run QEMU single-CPU TCG (NO kvm) with a FIXED `-icount shift=N` (NEVER shift=auto -- auto resyncs to wall-clock and breaks reproducibility). Under fixed icount the guest virtual clock is a function of executed instructions, not host time. CLOCK the screendumps to the GUEST time base (a PIT-tick / serial FLAIR-FRAME marker the live build emits), NOT host wall-clock, so frame cadence is reproducible. Full bit-for-bit hardening = layer record/replay (rr=record once WITH the injected --mouse/--keys, then rr=replay to capture frames -- NOTE on replay live QMP input is IGNORED, events come from the log); but since the harness input is ALREADY scripted/deterministic, START with plain fixed-icount + guest-tick-clocked dumps and only add rr if frame nondeterminism appears (record/replay is historically fragile + version-pinned).
- ENCODE (ffmpeg only, both formats): GIF = palettegen/paletteuse single-pass split with stats_mode=diff (static desktop) + scale=flags=neighbor (crisp 8bpp pixel art, NOT lanczos); the indexed-8 palette reproduces exactly. MP4/WebM = libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p (or libvpx-vp9) with scale=flags=neighbor. For byte-reproducible outputs strip ffmpeg metadata: -fflags +bitexact -flags:v +bitexact -map_metadata -1 (no creation_time/encoder tag).

DELIVERABLES:
1. Extend harness/emu/qemu.c with a RECORD mode: dump screendump frame_%05d.ppm on each guest FLAIR-FRAME marker (or every K PIT ticks) while replaying a scripted interaction; add the -icount shift=N flag.

title: FLAIR live drop-shadow integration: widen window clip to include the shadow band (decouple drawer frame-rect from strucRgn clip)
description: Follow-up from initech-54nw. The documentProc 1px drop shadow at offset (1,1) is correctly EMITTED by flair_draw_document_window (graded GREEN by test-chrome-fidelity, host/unclipped) but is INVISIBLE on the booted desktop. Root cause (verified via screendump probe + desktop.c read): the live compositor clips each window's chrome to w->strucRgn (desktop.c:223 paint_window_chrome(dst,w,w->strucRgn,w->strucRgn)), and strucRgn == the window bounds rect (window.c region_set_rect(strucRgn,bounds)). The shadow draws at x=right / y=bottom, OUTSIDE [left,right)x[top,bottom), so clip_in() drops it. DESIGN HAZARD: the drawer's frame rect is itself region_get_bbox(w->strucRgn) (desktop.c:117), so naively widening strucRgn by the shadow band shifts bbox.right->561 and the FRAME would move to 560, shadow to 561 (wrong); it also changes occlusion semantics (fronts_union/visible_into) + drag-expose + FindWindow. Real System 7 CalcDoc: struct region = content + frame + SHADOW BAND (window-frame.md Sec 1, StandardWDEF_a.txt L1230-1235 InsetRect MinusOne + DBox shadow). FIX (region-layer): decouple the drawer's window-frame rect from the clip region -- e.g. pass the window-bounds rect to flair_draw_document_window explicitly while making the clip = strucRgn-with-shadow-band; OR composite the shadow in desktop.c into the exposed desktop region with z-order (a front window's shadow over a back window). Then amend ppm_flair_check (c) to assert x=W1_R is FRAME ink (shadow) + x=W1_R+1 teal. Sequences with the window-region / 5l5z event-loop work (shares strucRgn + expose math). Cite window-frame.md Sec 1/Sec 4.
notes: 2026-07-21 solidity forensics — ROOT FOUND: the drop shadow IS drawn (chrome.c:854-865, column at x=right, row at y=bottom) but both write 1px OUTSIDE the window frame == strucRgn bbox (desktop.c:133,139), and clip_in (chrome.c:66-80) rejects everything outside visRgn ⊆ strucRgn — every shadow pixel is discarded. Fix = the already-planned strucRgn widening (CalcDoc-style shadow band, ../system7-decomp/specs/chrome/window-frame.md L36: struct = content grown 1px + shadow band) so visible(W) includes the shadow band; exposure/damage math then handles shadow erasure for free. In epic initech-av7s scope.

title: Kernel-growth runway exhausted at PROGRAM_BASE=0x40000 -- next growth needs high-half / extended-memory relocation
description: re30.2 (Step A) performed the SECOND +0x8000 whole-map shift (0x38000->0x40000), spending the LAST of the conventional free gap. The kernel stack region is now [0x90000,0xA0000), ESP=0x9FFFC, butting the 0xA0000 VGA / mode-0x13 LFB fallback aperture with ZERO gap (disjoint: 0x9FFFC < 0xA0000, but no slack). This is the MAXIMUM PROGRAM_BASE raise possible under the conventional-memory (<640 KiB) scheme: a third +0x8000 shift would push the kernel stack top into/over 0xA0000. The kernel.ld B0 ASSERT and memory_map.h now say so. CONSEQUENCE: any future kernel-resident growth past the current ~17 KiB shell-kernel headroom (FLAIR call sites in re30.3+, the verb layer, more Managers, MILTON redirection) cannot be absorbed by another raise. The mitigation when this binds: relocate the kernel and/or its stack to a high-half / extended-memory layout (the FLAIR heap already lives at 0x100000+; ADR-0001 makes >1 MiB directly addressable in flat 32-bit). This needs an ADR/committee decision (kernel link base, stack placement, stage2 load path, the self-host fixpoint determinism implications). NOT urgent now (re30.2 fits with ~17 KiB to spare) -- file-and-watch. Trip condition: the kernel.ld ASSERT(_kernel_end < 0x40000) fires, OR the KERNEL_SECTORS window can no longer grow within IMG_SECTORS.

title: Loader: child PSP inherits the parent JFT (enables external EXEC output redirect)
description: psp_build (os/milton/psp.c) HARD-RESETS the child JFT standard handles to CON (jft[0]=0 stdin, jft[1]=1 stdout, jft[2]=1 stderr, jft[3]=2 aux, jft[4]=3 prn) on every EXEC, ignoring the parent's open/redirected handles. Authentic DOS has the child INHERIT the parent's JFT (the AH=4Bh child gets a copy of the parent's handle table). RESULT: COMMAND.COM's > / >> redirect (hsct OUTPUT increment) works for BUILTINS (they run in the shell's own PSP with the DUP2'd handle 1 -> file) but NOT for external .COM EXEC children (their handle 1 is reset to CON). Empirically confirmed: GREET.COM> GOUT.TXT prints GREETINGS to SCREEN and leaves GOUT.TXT empty. FIX: thread the parent JFT (handles 0..4, or all 20) into psp_build via a params field and copy them into the child PSP when a parent PSP exists (g_cur_psp at EXEC time). Oracle: a child-inherits-parent-JFT property test + an emu gate mirroring test-hsct-redir but EXEC'ing GREET.COM> file and asserting GREETINGS appears via TYPE (from the file), not on screen during the EXEC. Touch: psp.c/psp.h/loader.c (the loader/PSP layer hsct deliberately did NOT touch). Ref: ADR-0003 DEC-06; MS-DOS 3.3 Tech Ref (handle inheritance on EXEC); the hsct OUTPUT increment driver already brackets EXEC correctly -- zero command.c change needed once this lands.

title: INT 21h subdir EXEC + subdir WRITE (CREAT/UNLINK/WRITE inside a subdir)
description:
Follow-up split out of initech-mzxa (ti8 Layer 2). mzxa wired the READ-side subdir resolution into the INT 21h file backend: OPEN/READ + FINDFIRST/NEXT now resolve and enumerate \SUB\FILE paths via fat12_resolve_path/fat12_read_dir (real-backend integration green). TWO deferred pieces, both because the underlying fat12 write/load primitives are ROOT-only:

(1) do_exec (AH=4Bh) stays ROOT-ONLY (mzxa decision 3): the EXEC source feeds the loader program-load path (load_program_from_fat -> load_program), which locates the .COM by a ROOT-dir 8.3 name. Threading a resolved containing-directory cluster into the loader is a riskier loader-internal change; mzxa kept do_exec rejecting subdir paths (path_has_subdir_or_drive at int21.c do_exec). This bead: let EXEC load a program from a subdirectory by resolving the source path to its dir_entry and feeding the located entry's own start_cluster to the loader.

(2) CREATE/UNLINK/WRITE inside a subdirectory: fileio_fat.c fat_create/fat_unlink return 0x0003 for a non-root dir_start_cluster (fat12_create/fat12_unlink/fat12_write_partial work over the ROOT dir + a root-dir slot for write-back). The mzxa file backend threads dir_start through create/unlink additively (param present, root==0 byte-identical), but the WRITE primitives must become subdir-aware (allocate a dir slot in a subdir cluster chain, write-back into it). This is the FAT WRITE-side subdir work (sibling of initech-509.11).

GROUNDED POINTERS (mzxa session): fileio_fat.c fat_create/fat_unlink non-root guards; int21.c do_exec path_has_subdir_or_drive; the resolve seam (int21_file_backend_t.resolve + resolve_dir_path). ORACLE: extend test_fileio_subdir.c (real backend) with subdir CREAT/WRITE/UNLINK round-trips + a subdir EXEC over a nested data disk.

title: ti8 Layer 2: thread resolved subdir through the INT 21h file backend (vtable cross-cut + g_cwd)
description:
Core-tier cross-cut (Rule 7) split out of initech-ti8 after grounding (workflow wf_fc0ea9c9-a7a, this session). ti8 Layer 1 (fat12.c: fat12_dir_t + fat12_read_dir + fat12_resolve_path, READ-side) is additive and self-contained, oracle-gated at the fat12 layer. THIS bead is Layer 2: actually wire subdir-path resolution into the INT 21h DOS API so OPEN/FINDFIRST/etc. resolve \SUB\FILE paths.

WHY SEPARATE: the int21_file_backend_t vtable (int21.h:149-220, VERIFIED) is purely root-relative today (open()/create()/dir_entry()/unlink() take only name83 / a flat index). Threading a resolved directory (a uint16 start_cluster, 0=root, is the lowest-coupling thread) is a multi-file change: int21.h + fileio_fat.c (real backend, fat_open@81/fat_dir_entry@147) + THREE host mocks in lockstep (test_fileio.c@319, test_int21.c@103, test_int21_edge.c) or nothing compiles.

GROUNDED SCOPE (all line numbers VERIFIED this session, the brief's were stale):
- 5 path_has_subdir_or_drive() rejection sites to replace with resolve_path: do_open@858, do_creat@931, do_unlink@995, do_findfirst@1405, do_exec@1476. Preserve AX=0x0003 PATH_NOT_FOUND on a bad/non-dir component (keeps do_geterr AH=59h class/action/locus green) and preserve the INT21_PATH_SCAN_MAX overlength fail-loud + the INT21_MUTATE_PATHSCAN_NOBOUND mutation oracle.
- g_cwd: a file-static in int21.c near the globals block (~L52), NOT a psp_t field (psp_t is LOCKED spec with sizeof==256 _Static_assert). Reset to root on program launch (loader.c:287 beside int21_set_psp/int21_mcb_reset) and on do_terminate (int21.c:1721); save/restore around the 5 kmain.c int21_set_psp(&g_kernel_psp) sites (423/462/837/1048/1086) so kernel-context CWD does not leak a child's dir. Wire do_getcwd (int21.c:1895, currently hard-codes root buf[0]=0) to report g_cwd.
- DEPENDS ON ti8 (Layer 1: fat12_resolve_path + fat12_dir_t must exist first).

OPEN DECISIONS (operator/committee): (a) do_exec subdir scope -- resolve a subdir-qualified EXEC target (bigger blast radius: loader load_program_from_fat must accept a non-root start-cluster) or keep EXEC root-only and leave its site rejecting? (b) CWD inheritance: real DOS gives a child its own inherited copy; simplest ti8 model is reset-to-root on launch -- confirm acceptable. (c) when AH=56h RENAME (gnrc) lands it must also use resolve_path.

ORACLE: extend test_int21/test_fileio with resolved-path open/findfirst cases (mocks model a tiny nested namespace); mutation points INT21_MUTATE_RESOLVE_NODRIVE / INT21_MUTATE_RESOLVE_FINALDIR. Mutation-prove.
notes: 2026-10-17 PM DECISION: a launched program starts in the drive's CURRENT directory (DOS 3.30 Tech Ref 6-121/6-188/4-4; MS-DOS 3.3 UG p.114), not reset to root; the kernel restores its own directory after the child exits; mutant LOADER_MUT_CWD_RESET (lane/tps, initech-3p1a). Resolves the open CWD-inheritance question.

design:
TRANCHE-E design (grounded WL-0037+ audit). Three increments, each RED->GREEN->mutation-proven->make test, SERIAL on shared files (Rule 3):
INC-1 (no shared-file risk): NEW pure-logic module os/milton/env.c + env.h -- a freestanding master environment store (fixed-capacity arena, NO libc): env_set(name,val) (upsert, upcases name per DOS), env_get, env_unset (NAME= clears), env_count/iter, and env_serialize(buf,cap)-> DOS-format block = sequence of ASCIIZ 'NAME=VALUE\0' strings + a final extra '\0' (empty env = lone '\0\0'). Host oracle test_env.c (HOSTED, like cmd_* TU). Seed PATH/COMSPEC/PROMPT.
INC-2 (command.c): NEW CMD_SET in command.h enum + cmd_classify table row; cmd_set handler: 'SET' lists 'NAME=VALUE' lines, 'SET NAME=VALUE' upserts, 'SET NAME=' clears. Wire the global master env into kmain shell loop. test via test_command + an emu DIR-style leg later.
INC-3 (loader.c): on EXEC, env_serialize the master env into ENV_BLOCK (0x5F000) and pass env_linear=ENV_BLOCK (not 0) so child PSP env_seg points at the real block (psp_build already does flat_to_fake_paragraph). Per-process: child inherits a COPY (already physically separate region). Mutation: drop the serialize -> child sees empty env -> oracle RED.
Ground truth: DOS env block format = ASCIIZ NAME=VALUE strings, double-NUL terminated (Ralf Brown INT 21h/AH=4Bh EPB + PSP:2Ch). DOS 3.0+ trailing word-count=1 + progpath is OPTIONAL nicety, deferred. Unblocks dibc(PROMPT)/atf(PATH)/xw1(batch %VAR%).
close_reason: Tranche E complete: env store (inc-1) + SET built-in (inc-2) + EXEC env inheritance (inc-3), all RED->GREEN, mutation-proven, 220 host gates + test-program emu EXEC green.

title: console_init accepts degenerate geometry; no padded-pitch or 8bpp DAC oracle
description: console_init (console.c:273-290) copies lfb_pitch/width/height verbatim with no validation: pitch==0 aliases all scanlines to row 0 (silent FB corruption); width==0 draws nothing while returning CONSOLE_OK; pitch<width*bpp overruns into the next scanline. Violates console.h:84 'refuse bad input, do not scribble' + Rule 2. Test gaps: test_console.c always sets pitch==width*bpp (the 'honor pitch not width' contract is never exercised -- exactly the padded-LFB bug Bochs/86Box 24bpp hit), and the 8bpp DAC index->seafoam binding (kmain.c:548-551) has no end-to-end oracle. Audit: console console-init-no-pitch-validation + console-pitch-padding-test-gap + console-8bpp-dac-no-oracle.
acceptance_criteria: console_init returns CONSOLE_ERR_* on width==0/height==0/pitch<width*(bpp/8) and leaves console unusable; test_console adds a padded-pitch case (pitch=width*bpp+64) asserting correct scanline + untouched padding (mutation-proven by stride=width*bpp -> RED); a DAC/screendump oracle asserts idx1->seafoam, idx15->gray; make test green.
close_reason: console_init rejects degenerate geometry (width/height 0, pitch<width*bpp) via CONSOLE_ERR_GEOMETRY; added padded-pitch coverage test (pitch>width*bpp). Both mutation-proven (remove guard->RED; width*bpp stride->RED). 8bpp DAC end-to-end oracle split to follow-up (needs mode-0x13 screendump infra). make test 55h+19e GREEN.

title: Loader control-transfer asm reads jump target via memory operand after switching ESP
description: Entry asm (loader.c:323-336) does mov stack_top,%esp THEN jmp *entry_eip where entry_eip is a memory operand. Correct only because KERNEL_CFLAGS is -O0 with a frame pointer (EBP-relative locals resolve into the kernel frame). If the build moves to -O2 or -fomit-frame-pointer, entry_eip/psp_ptr/stack_top become ESP-relative and jmp *%4 dereferences the just-switched PROGRAM stack -> garbage/triple-fault. No compile-time guard pins this. Audit: loader-psp loader-asm-jmp-reads-operand-after-esp-switch.
acceptance_criteria: Load entry_eip into a dedicated register BEFORE the ESP switch (or pin the fn with an optimize/no-omit-frame-pointer attribute + a guard); behavior unchanged at -O0 and -O2; make test green.
close_reason: Entry asm loads the jump target (entry_eip) into EAX BEFORE the ESP switch and jmps via register, eliminating the only post-switch memory read. By construction optimization-safe. Demonstrated RED->GREEN at -O2 -fomit-frame-pointer (pre-fix: GREET.COM never runs; fixed: passes); no -O0 regression. The permanent -O2 coverage arrives free when the toolchain moves to -O2/i686-elf (initech-6pm/CDR-0001) -- test-exec then becomes the -O2 gate and now stays green. make test 55h+21e GREEN.

title: CONFIG.SYS larger than 1024-byte scratch is silently discarded (comment claims truncation)
description: sysinit_apply_config reads CONFIG.SYS into static char cfg_buf[1024] via fat12_read_file, which returns FAT12_ERR_BUFFER (does NOT truncate) when file>buf. So a >1024B CONFIG.SYS makes from_disk stay 0 and the user's whole file is silently ignored for SYSINIT_CONFIG_BASELINE; summary prints source=baseline masking the discard. Comment at sysinit.c:134-135 wrongly claims truncation. A 1024B CONFIG.SYS is period-realistic. Audit: sysinit-boot configsys-oversize-silent-baseline-fallback (+ sysinit-phases-no-host-test).
acceptance_criteria: Either honor truncation via incremental read, or fail loud (distinct 'SYSINIT: CONFIG.SYS too large' marker before fallback) and fix the comment; factor the file-read so sysinit_apply_config is host-drivable with an injected fake; host tests for from_disk success, oversize, FILES-absent baseline=20, FILES clamp; make test green.
close_reason: sysinit honors first 1KB of an oversize CONFIG.SYS via fat12_read_partial (trim to last line) + flags it 'source=CONFIG.SYS(truncated@1024)' instead of silently discarding to baseline (operator choice). Fixed misleading comment. New test-sysinit-oversize gate (oversize fixture, FILES=8 in first lines): RED (baseline FILES=20) -> GREEN (truncated@1024 FILES=8), mutation-proven. make test 55h+21e GREEN.

title: dos_reentry_panic serial output spins unbounded on a dead UART
description: panic.c bounds its serial spin (PSERIAL_SPIN_MAX) precisely so the fail-loud path cannot wedge. The sibling path irq.c rserial_putc (irq.c:60-66) spins while !(LSR&THRE) with NO bound; on an absent/stuck UART (common 86Box config) dos_reentry_panic hangs before it can int3 into the real panic -- defeating the loud-and-bounded guarantee. Audit: interrupts dos-reentry-panic-unbounded-serial-spin.
acceptance_criteria: irq.c rserial_putc uses the same bounded spin (PSERIAL_SPIN_MAX, drop byte on timeout) as pserial_putc; make test green.
close_reason: bcg.5: do_puts NULL-guard + INT21_PUTS_SCAN_MAX bound; RED (NULL deref segfault)->GREEN, mutation-proven. bcg.8: rserial_putc bounded by RSERIAL_SPIN_MAX mirroring panic.c (target-only port I/O; emu irq-storm serial path confirms no regression). make test 55h+19e GREEN.

title: 8259A spurious IRQ7 (0x2F) / IRQ15 (0x37) wedge the machine; no spurious-IRQ EOI discipline
description: Vectors 0x2F/0x37 are never installed with real handlers, so an 8259A spurious interrupt (INTR deasserted before ack -- electrical noise/timing) lands on isr_spurious -> permanent cli;hlt. Real-hw contract: master spurious (IRQ7) -> send NO EOI; slave spurious (IRQ15) -> EOI to master only. On period PCs (Rule 5) one line-noise glitch on IRQ7 halts the system. Audit: interrupts pic-spurious-irq7-irq15-unhandled.
acceptance_criteria: Dedicated stubs at 0x2F/0x37 checking the in-service register: master spurious IRET no-EOI; slave spurious EOI-to-master then IRET; not routed to the halt path; mutation-proven oracle; make test green.
close_reason: Dedicated isr_irq7_spurious(0x2F)/isr_irq15_spurious(0x37) stubs push real vectors; idt installs them; isr_dispatch_c applies EOI discipline (slave spurious 0x37 -> master-only EOI; master spurious 0x2F -> no EOI) then resumes. test-spurious extended to fire 0x2F/0x37, asserts vec=2F/37 (dedicated stubs ran) + resume; mutation-proven (remove installs -> RED). EOI correctness by-construction per 8259A datasheet (real spurious not deterministically triggerable). make test 55h+20e GREEN; test-boot-bochs PASS. Also fixed test_idt host stubs for the new externs.

title: Spurious/unhandled-vector ISR halts forever instead of returning cleanly
description: idt_init points all non-exception vectors at isr_spurious -> isr_common -> isr_dispatch_c, which ends in for(;;) cli;hlt (panic.c:140-142) for ANY vector. Spec says the spurious handler should print diagnostics and RETURN cleanly so a stray vector does not wedge the desktop. As written any unexpected software int / non-PIT-non-kbd hw vector permanently halts. Audit: interrupts spurious-halts-not-returns.
acceptance_criteria: Split spurious path from exception path: spurious stub emits a serial diagnostic and IRETs (isr_selftest pattern); permanent halt reserved for CPU exceptions 0-31; oracle fires an unexpected vector and asserts execution resumes; make test green.
close_reason: isr_dispatch_c now resumes (clean iret via isr_common) for spurious/unhandled vectors (vector>31, sentinel 0xFF), reserving the permanent halt for CPU exceptions 0-31. New test-spurious emu gate: BOOT_SPURIOUS fires int 0x70, asserts SPURIOUS-RESUMED + no PANIC + no triple-fault; RED->GREEN, mutation-proven. make test 55h+20e GREEN; test-boot-bochs PASS (interrupt-minefield Bochs check).

title: INT 21h AH=09h do_puts dereferences EDX with no NULL check and unbounded scan
description: do_puts (int21.c:313-331) walks bytes at EDX until 0x24 ('$') with NO NULL guard and NO scan bound. EDX==0 or a string lacking '$' walks arbitrary memory (fault on flat target / megabytes of garbage to CON). Contrast path-deref fns (NULL-check + INT21_PATH_SCAN_MAX) and do_read/write (DEC-14 guarded). AH=09h is the most common DOS output call; DEC-14's fail-loud rationale applies verbatim. Audit: int21 puts-unbounded-unguarded-edx.
acceptance_criteria: NULL check on EDX + runaway bound mirroring INT21_PATH_SCAN_MAX; no-'$' and EDX==0 fixtures; mutation-proven; make test green.
close_reason: bcg.5: do_puts NULL-guard + INT21_PUTS_SCAN_MAX bound; RED (NULL deref segfault)->GREEN, mutation-proven. bcg.8: rserial_putc bounded by RSERIAL_SPIN_MAX mirroring panic.c (target-only port I/O; emu irq-storm serial path confirms no regression). make test 55h+19e GREEN.

title: CONFIG.SYS decimal-overflow guard off-by-one (config_sys.c:76)
description: cfg_parse_uint guard 'if (v > 429496729u)' is checked before v=v*10+digit; at v==429496729 with next digit 6-9 the multiply-add overflows uint32 and WRAPS instead of saturating at 0xFFFFFFFF (the documented contract). 2^32-family values (e.g. FILES=4294967296) wrap to ~0 and clamp UP to FILES_MIN instead of DOWN to FILES_MAX. Benign (still in-range) but violates the saturation contract. Found by the wave-B CONFIG.SYS fuzzer (initech-hjv). Fix: guard 'v > (0xFFFFFFFFu - digit)/10u'. Must update the fuzzer's ref_parse_uint to the corrected saturating logic + add an explicit 2^32-family clamp-to-MAX assertion + a mutant restoring the off-by-one.

title: Build-time guard: kernel _kernel_end must stay below PROGRAM_BASE (0x20000)
description: The kernel size guards in the Makefile check only the LOADED .bin size vs KERNEL_SECTORS*512 -- they do NOT check that _kernel_end (the end of .bss, which is NOT in the .bin) stays below PROGRAM_BASE (0x20000). During 509.2 the shell kernel's .bss (cfg_fat_buf[4608]) pushed _kernel_end to 0x1FF60 -- only 160 bytes below PROGRAM_BASE -- a SILENT near-collision the existing guards could not see (the .bin still fit). A future kernel .bss growth would silently corrupt the program-load region (0x20000). Add a build-time check (extract _kernel_end via nm from each kernel ELF, assert < PROGRAM_BASE with a margin) so this fails LOUD (Rule 2) like the .bin-size guard does. Apply to all kernel variants (or the largest as a canary). Cite spec/memory_map.h PROGRAM_BASE.
acceptance_criteria: Building any kernel whose _kernel_end >= PROGRAM_BASE (or within a small margin) fails the build with a clear message naming _kernel_end and PROGRAM_BASE; deliberately bloating a kernel's .bss past 0x20000 is caught at build, not at runtime.
close_reason: Build-time _kernel_end < PROGRAM_BASE guard added to all 15 kernel .bin recipes: nm extracts _kernel_end, asserts < PROGRAM_BASE-256 (parsed from spec/memory_map.h), fails loud with actionable message. Mutation-proven (orchestrator independently: 0x1000 .bss bloat -> _kernel_end=0x20d60 -> build RED; .bin guard stayed green proving the gap closed). Current headroom: 480 bytes.

title: FINDFIRST DTA layout deviates from real-DOS byte offsets

title: fat12_read_file uses 5760-byte on-stack chain[2880] scratch
description: os/milton/fat12.c:529 fat12_read_file declares uint16_t chain[2880] (~5.6KB) on the stack, sized to the 1.44MB floppy cluster count. Safe for the floppy read path, but a kernel-stack hazard: (a) the kernel stack budget is small, (b) FAT16 HDD geometry (initech-z01) has far more clusters and would overflow it. Rule 3 (all bugs deep): move to a caller-provided chain buffer OR a streaming cluster-by-cluster walk (no full-chain materialization). Surfaced during initech-adf dir/read implementation; not yet a live bug on the floppy path.
acceptance_criteria: fat12_read_file no longer holds a geometry-sized array on the stack; FAT16 path cannot overflow; floppy read tests stay green.
close_reason: Streaming cluster walk landed + verified (WL-0027, 654e48a); on-stack chain[2880] eliminated, anti-hang + RISK-5 + corrupt-fuzzer contract preserved; test-fat-readfile-mutant (3) + BIGCHAIN large-file leg. 93 host + 27 emu green.

description: Root cause: os/i123/app/face_a.c:502-508 paints only message/CALC/CIRC. os/flair/event.c:497-518 consumes Caps Lock as modifier state (no keyDown), :503-504 latches ALPHA_LOCK; the event cooker has no Num Lock latch. Exact native indicator placement must be captured/locked independently. Pickup: Add a reliable guest lock-state observation/refresh path and render CAPS/NUM on/off without losing CALC/CIRC/error/status text. Respect that Caps-only input may yield nullEvent and Num Lock currently needs an explicit platform state contract; do not infer a toggle from arbitrary printable events. Acceptance oracle: Extend Event Manager and Face A host oracles with one physical toggle, held-key repeat, release, second toggle, no unrelated keypress and repaint/resize; compare with independent lock-state expectations. Replay keyslook on QEMU/Bochs with visible on/off states and record a record-flair clip. Mutants omitting the lock latch or the status renderer must fail. title: Validate BREAK operands against an independently captured DOS grammar
description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:2989 recognizes ON/OFF but :2995 silently falls through for every other operand and :3000 reports the unchanged state. This is explicit existing policy, also documented in pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch2-entries-a.tex:67-68; strict invalid-operand reporting was never built. Ground truth: Shipped Reference BREAK syntax at ch2-entries-a.tex:59 and the explicit lenient text at :67-68; ADR-0003 DEC-16 3.3 governs the flag, not invalid command-line wording. The audit supplies only a tester expectation for rejection, so capture a real DOS 3.3 BREAK INVALID/trailing-operand golden before changing the narrow policy. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Add C command-argument tests for empty, mixed-case ON/OFF, INVALID and extra words; assert rejected input never changes the flag. description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:995 cmd_render_prompt has no V/v switch arm; its default at :1147 emits the character literally, producing V>. dos_getver at :2343 already exposes AH=30h, but prompt_ctx_t has no version supplied to the renderer. QEMU promptversion must show the correct version rather than V>; compare formatting to real DOS 3.3 and keep VER/AH=30h consistent. Mutant: remove the V arm or force a stale version; the prompt assertion must fail. Add $V to the shipped prompt table. Scope: A missing documented period prompt code; do not reinterpret every other unknown code as part of this pickup. title: Make Date and Time edit-snapshot behavior clear
description: B21. Root cause: os/apps/cpanels/cpanels.c:63 reads the clock only when entering a panel; core.c:71 retains original_time for Cancel and :40 renders state.time as Time. There is no live polling while the edit transaction remains open; core.c:84 commits that edited snapshot on OK. Ground truth: The report states a usability expectation, not a measured real-Mac live-update requirement. The existing cp_state transaction and Cancel/OK behavior in os/apps/cpanels/core.c are the local contract; no evidence shows that the underlying system clock stops. Scope: First pickup: label the displayed value clearly as an editable snapshot and explain when OK sets it, or design live display separated from dirty edited fields. Do not overwrite a user edit with polling or certify that the panel is a frozen system clock. Acceptance oracle: Extend test-cpanels with a locked clock advanced across a minute while the panel stays open, with both untouched and edited fields, Cancel and OK. Target samples must show the agreed snapshot label or live display and unchanged edits. A missing-label/frozen-live-view mutant must fail. Record a record-flair clip. title: Provide text-surface I-beam feedback and timed caret blinking
description: B20. Root cause: os/flair/cursor.c:224 selects only busy/hourglass or arrow, while os/milton/kmain.c:1555 only moves the pointer; InitechText has no cursor-shape request. itext.c:210 always draws a solid active insertion caret and acknowledges absent blink at :40. os/flair/process.c:856 drops null/idle events, so a tenant cannot drive TEIdle. Ground truth: Macintosh guide printed p.28 describes the I-beam/insertion point; ../system7-decomp/specs/toolbox/textedit.md Sec 2 and TEIdle define active caret blinking. CLAUDE.md retains the hourglass during busy operations. Scope: Add bounded cursor ownership/hit regions and a cooperative time/idle delivery contract; use an I-beam only over editable text and blink only the active insertion point. Preserve selection drawing and busy-hourglass precedence; reset shape on leaving, deactivation or exit. Acceptance oracle: Extend cursor/TextEdit/tenant host tests with an injected clock and inside/outside/focus changes. Use phase-separated target samples (not one-second aliasing) and a pointer-crossing trace; mutants forcing arrow or holding caret on must fail independently. Record a record-flair clip. description: B19. Root cause: os/apps/calcda/calcda.c:102 executes immediately on mouseDown and command at :75 repaints only the readout. Ground truth: Independent real Mac OS 8 Calculator capture evidence/references/s8_calc_key7_pressed.png shows the held 7 key inverted; spec/calcda/calcda_layout.h defines this app layout. Scope: Deliver the needed release/track state through the App Contract and retain one pressed key for painting; clear it on release, drag-out or deactivation according to an independently captured rule. Preserve one arithmetic action per accepted press. Acceptance oracle: Extend test-calcda routing/render tests with down/held/drag/release and key equivalents. Add a target screenshot during the hold matched to the independent pressed capture. A no-pressed-paint or lost-release mutant must fail; record a record-flair clip. title: Offer mouse reading of long Scrapbook text clips
description: B18. Root cause: os/apps/notepad/notepad.c:190 configures the shared bar for clip count/page position; :341 uses it to turn clips. Only Down/Up keys alter intra-clip g_scroll at :398. Mouse scrolling within a clip has no entry point. Ground truth: The audit explicitly bases this on usability. The Macintosh guide printed p.152 (evidence/references/mac-guide.txt:6764) warns that an oversized Scrapbook image may be fully visible only after pasting elsewhere; its bar browses clips. Do not describe the existing clip-navigation model as disproved by a native scrolling reference. Scope: Add a discoverable mouse route to read hidden lines while preserving clip navigation and persistence. Specify whether to add separate text scrolling controls or a clear mode, rather than silently repurposing the existing page bar. Priority is polish because keyboard reading already works. Acceptance oracle: Extend test-scrapbook-route with one long clip and several short clips; emulator mouse actions must expose LAST and still reach previous/next clips. A mutant ignoring intra-clip mouse steps must fail. Check saved clips unchanged and record a record-flair clip. title: Defensive: conin_cooked_line should bound against a non-terminating BOUND conin source (not just unbound)
description: Adversarial review of x8fs flagged that the host-hang guard covers the NO-source case (g_conin_get==NULL) but not a bound-but-broken source returning 0x00 forever -> conin_cooked_line would spin. ASSESSED NOT CURRENTLY REACHABLE: the kernel binds the real keyboard (blocks for real keys, never a 0x00 stream) and the host mock (test_conin.c:129-151) FATALs on underflow ('can never hang'). So this is latent fragility, not a live defect. Defensive hardening: treat a sustained no-progress condition (e.g. repeated 0x00 with a full buffer) as EOF, or have host mocks return -1/EOF on exhaustion and handle it. Low priority -- the real (no-source) hang that cost a session is already fixed (commit ddef39a).

notes: Adversarial review of ro6c (2026-06-15) found int21.h:63-68 mislabels the device-info bit NAMES for bits 1-4 vs the real MS-DOS char-device contract. Correct layout to ground from the PRM/RBIL: bit0=stdin, bit1=stdout, bit2=NUL, bit3=CLOCK, bit4=special, bit5=raw/binary, bit6=not-EOF-on-input, bit14=IOCTL-strings, bit15=ISDEV. The header currently has ISCIN=bit1/ISCOT=bit2/ISNUL=bit3/ISCLK=bit4 (shifted one position). These macros are DEAD today (CON=0x80D3 literal + ISDEV/STDIN are the only ones referenced) and the shipped VALUE 0x80D3 is correct, so NO behavioral impact -- but this bead MUST correct the bit-name labels (PRM-grounded) before implementing the AL=01/06/07/08 minors against them.

title: FAT12 allocator: free-cluster search hints from prev+1, can falsely report NO_SPACE under fragmentation
description: Lens-2 finding during zs24 L1 verification (pre-existing, NOT introduced by zs24). fat12_grow_dir (fat12.c ~1120) and the file-extend/write paths (fat12.c ~1796, ~2056) call fat12_find_free(vol,fat,fat_len, prev+1), i.e. search for the lowest free cluster AT OR ABOVE the current tail. If all free clusters sit below the tail, allocation returns FAT12_ERR_NO_SPACE even though space exists. Mirrors the established extend convention so it is self-consistent, but a fragmented volume can spuriously fail. Fix uniformly across all three call sites (wrap-around search from cluster 2) with a fuzz case that places free clusters only below the tail. Low priority (floppy/low-fragmentation today).

Build ONE policy-free mechanism + the two heritages become two DECORATION POLICIES over it. HOW TO APPLY: re30.4 (one palette module, kill the 5 duplicated index->RGB switches) is the FIRST mechanism/policy cut -- extract color into a POLICY layer the mechanism reads from, not a dedup'd lookup baked into chrome/control/dialog. re30.5 GrafPort verbs land the imaging mechanism policy-free. Clock-skew gotcha (env): build/ artifacts can acquire mtimes ~tens of minutes in the FUTURE relative to the system clock, which makes GNU make skip ALL rebuilds (every target looks newer than freshly-edited sources) -> false-green/false-red oracles. Symptom: 'Clock skew detected. Your build may be incomplete.' + a mutation-proof gate (e.g. test-dosmsg-mutant [B]) fails to bite because the intermediate 'make kernel_shell.bin' is a silent no-op. FIX: 'make clean' wipes the future-dated artifacts; rebuild from clean gives clock-consistent mtimes and the gates behave. Always 'make clean' before trusting an incremental oracle run if the skew warning appears.

Bochs RFB display does NOT render VGA mode 0x13 (initech-6pj/564): even a pristine REAL-MODE fill of mode 0x13 (index 1 everywhere + DAC[1] programmed), halted before the kernel, comes back ALL BLACK over the RFB display plugin (raw framebuffer bytes 0/345600 nonzero; RFB serves the guest as 720x530 true-color 3-3-2). The OS writes the mode-0x13 framebuffer CORRECTLY -- proven 4 independent ways: (1) stage2 real-mode write/readback at 0xA0000 returns the written byte; (2) Bochs debugger write-watchpoint on 0xAF9FF fires (kernel fill reaches the high framebuffer byte); (3) host oracle test-console 8bpp 57 checks; (4) serial shows BANNER-BEGIN/text/BANNER-END through console_putc. So Bochs's RFB plugin (the only headless display in this build) cannot display chained 256-color mode 0x13 -- a Bochs RFB limitation, NOT an InitechOS bug. CONSEQUENCE: the Bochs tri-emulator gate must assert on SERIAL markers + no-triple-fault (resolution/display-independent, the rigorous Rule-5 signal), not a screendump. A visual Bochs screendump of mode 0x13 is not achievable via RFB here; mode 0x12 (640x480x16 planar) MIGHT render on RFB (untested) but needs a planar renderer. /tmp/rfb_capture.py is the (working) RFB framebuffer-capture client.

MCB arena (509.6 part 2) placement: the cleanest, LOWEST-RISK option is a per-load DYNAMIC arena over the free tail of the image region -- the loader, after copying the .COM, inits an mcb_arena over [paragraph_align(PROGRAM_IMAGE + image_size) .. ENV_BLOCK(0x5F000)), owner = the program's PSP segment (0x3000). This is the authentic DOS model (program owns memory above its image), needs NO spec/memory_map.h change (avoids the load-bearing PROGRAM_IMAGE_MAX edit), and the arena ceiling 0x5F000 stays below the env block + stack so there is no collision. Wire AH=48/49/4A behind an int21 mem-backend SEAM (like int21_set_exec_backend) so int21.c stays mcb-free and host-testable without adding mcb.c to every test link line; the kernel binds an mcb-backed backend in kmain.c (which already links mcb.c) and does the data_para->DOS-segment conversion ((arena_base>>4)+data_para).
